Rotate your torso and pull the handle diagonally down across your body.
Keep your hips steady and your core braced.
Return slowly, finish your reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: cable twisting overhead press
exercises.description: An overhead cable press where you rotate your torso as you push. It works the shoulders and the core together.
steps: Set a cable low and stand sideways, holding the handle at your shoulder.
Brace your core and turn slightly toward the cable.
Press the handle overhead while rotating your torso to face forward.
Lower the handle back to your shoulder with control.
Finish your reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: cable twisting standing high row
exercises.description: A standing cable row at a high angle with a torso twist. It hits the upper back and rear shoulders.
steps: Set a cable at about head height and stand facing it with the handle in one hand.
Take a split stance and lean back slightly.
Pull the handle toward your upper chest, turning your torso as you go.
Squeeze your shoulder blade, then return slowly.
Complete the set and switch sides.

exercises.name: cable twisting standing one arm chest press
exercises.description: A standing single-arm cable press with a rotation. It trains the chest and the core's ability to resist and produce twist.
steps: Set the cable at chest height and stand sideways with the handle in your inside hand.
Take a stable stance and hold the handle at your chest.
Press the handle forward while rotating your torso toward the press.
Return to the start with control.
Complete your reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: cable twisting standing row
exercises.description: A standing cable row where you turn your torso as you pull. It works the back with some added core rotation.
steps: Set a cable at mid height and stand facing it, holding the handle with one hand.
Stand in a stable stance with a slight lean back.
Pull the handle to your ribs and rotate your torso open.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the end.
Return slowly, finish your reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: cable vertical pallof press
exercises.description: A cable press performed upward or downward in a vertical line while holding the core still. It trains anti-rotation and shoulder stability.
steps: Set a cable at a high or low position and stand sideways to it.
Hold the handle at your chest with both hands.
Press the handle straight up (or down) along a vertical line.
Hold for a second without letting your torso twist.
Return to your chest, finish the set, then switch sides.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline reverse grip 30 degrees bench press
exercises.description: A low-incline dumbbell press with palms facing you. The reverse grip puts extra focus on the upper chest.
steps: Set a bench to about 30 degrees and lie back with dumbbells held palms facing you.
Start with the dumbbells at your chest.
Press them up until your arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly back to your chest.
Keep your elbows close to your body.

exercises.name: dumbbell side lunge
exercises.description: A lateral lunge with dumbbells that trains the glutes, quads and inner thighs in the frontal plane.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand or one at your chest and stand tall.
Step out wide to one side and sit your hips back.
Keep the other leg straight and your chest upright.
Push through the bent leg to return to the middle.
Alternate sides or finish all reps on one side before switching.

exercises.name: lever seated one leg calf raise
exercises.description: A one-leg seated calf raise on a machine. Working each leg alone helps balance strength and targets the soleus.
steps: Sit on the machine and place the ball of one foot on the platform.
Set the pad on your thigh and release the safety.
Lower your heel for a stretch.
Press up as high as you can onto your toes.
Pause, lower slowly, then switch legs.

exercises.name: lever calf raise (bench press machine)
exercises.description: A calf raise done on a chest press style lever machine, using the seat and handles to load the calves.
steps: Sit on the machine and place the balls of your feet on the lower platform or press plate.
Push to straighten your legs and release the safety.
Lower your heels as far as is comfortable.
Rise up onto your toes as high as possible.
Pause at the top and lower under control.

exercises.name: lever shrug (bench press machine)
exercises.description: Shrugging with a lever press machine as the load. It builds the upper traps with a stable, guided path.
steps: Set the machine so the handles are at your sides and grip them firmly.
Stand or sit tall with your arms straight.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause at the top for a moment.
Lower your shoulders slowly without rolling them.

exercises.name: assisted close grip underhand chin up
exercises.description: A chin-up with machine assistance and a narrow underhand grip. It lets you build pulling strength with less bodyweight.
steps: Set the assistance weight and kneel or stand on the platform.
Grip the bar with palms facing you, hands close together.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
Squeeze your back and biceps at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.

exercises.name: underhand grip inverted back row
exercises.description: A bodyweight row under a low bar with an underhand grip. It builds the back and biceps.
steps: Set a bar at waist height and lie under it, gripping it with palms facing you.
Straighten your body from heels to head.
Pull your chest up to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower yourself under control until your arms are straight.
Keep your hips up the whole time.

exercises.name: smith standing shoulder press
exercises.description: A standing overhead press on the Smith machine. The fixed bar path lets you focus on pushing.
steps: Set the bar at shoulder height and stand under it with a shoulder width grip.
Unrack the bar and hold it at your collarbone.
Press up until your arms are straight.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders slowly.
Brace your core and keep your ribs down.

exercises.name: standing plate presses
exercises.description: Pressing a weight plate overhead with both hands. A simple way to train the shoulders and arms.
steps: Stand tall holding a plate at the sides with both hands at chest height.
Brace your core and keep your elbows slightly forward.
Press the plate overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower it slowly to your chest.
Keep your ribs down and avoid arching.

exercises.name: ez barbell standing overhead press
exercises.description: An overhead press with an EZ bar. The angled grips can feel kinder on the wrists while you train the shoulders.
steps: Stand holding an EZ bar at your upper chest with a comfortable grip.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower it slowly back to your chest.
Keep your head neutral and avoid leaning back.

exercises.name: cable standing one arm triceps pushdown (overhand grip)
exercises.description: A single-arm pushdown with an overhand grip. It isolates one triceps at a time.
steps: Attach a handle to a high pulley and stand facing it.
Hold the handle with an overhand grip and tuck your elbow to your side.
Push down until your arm is fully straight.
Squeeze your triceps, then let the handle rise slowly.
Finish your reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell standing inner biceps curl
exercises.description: A standing dumbbell curl with the elbows turned slightly out to emphasise the inner head of the biceps.
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, elbows slightly out from your sides.
Curl the weights toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower them slowly to the start.
Keep your upper arms still.

exercises.name: cable standing lat pushdown (rope equipment)
exercises.description: A straight-arm pushdown with a rope on a high cable. It isolates the lats with almost no help from the arms.
steps: Attach a rope to a high pulley and stand facing it, hinging slightly forward.
Grab the rope with straight arms.
Push the rope down to your thighs, keeping your arms nearly straight.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Let the rope rise slowly to shoulder height.

exercises.name: dumbbell standing alternate vertical front raises
exercises.description: Raising one dumbbell at a time in front of you with a neutral grip. It works the front shoulders.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your thighs with palms facing in.
Raise one dumbbell straight up to shoulder height.
Pause, then lower it slowly.
Repeat with the other arm and keep alternating.
Avoid swinging your body.

exercises.name: dumbbell seated one arm shoulder press
exercises.description: A seated overhead press with one dumbbell. Working one arm at a time shows any imbalances.
steps: Sit on a bench with back support, holding a dumbbell at your shoulder.
Brace your core.
Press the dumbbell up until your arm is straight.
Lower it slowly to your shoulder.
Finish your reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: lever seated squat
exercises.description: A squat on a seated lever machine with a supported torso. It loads the thighs and glutes with a guided path.
steps: Sit in the machine with your back against the pad and shoulders under the supports.
Place your feet on the platform about shoulder width apart.
Push through your feet to extend your legs.
Lower slowly until your knees are comfortably bent.
Keep your knees in line with your toes.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline alternate hammer curl
exercises.description: Hammer curls on an incline bench, one arm at a time. The stretched position makes the biceps and brachialis work hard.
steps: Sit back on an incline bench holding dumbbells with palms facing in.
Let your arms hang straight down.
Curl one dumbbell up without twisting your wrist.
Lower it slowly and repeat with the other arm.
Keep your upper arms still.

exercises.name: plate hyperextension
exercises.description: A back extension holding a plate at your chest. It strengthens the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Set the hyperextension bench so your hips are just past the pad.
Hold a weight plate against your chest and cross your arms over it.
Lower your torso toward the floor with a flat back.
Raise your torso until your body forms a straight line.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and avoid overarching.

exercises.name: lever one arm seated row (seated row machine)
exercises.description: A single-arm row on a seated machine. It lets you load one side of the back at a time.
steps: Sit at the machine with your chest on the pad and grab one handle.
Start with your arm extended.
Pull the handle toward your torso, driving your elbow back.
Squeeze your shoulder blade, then return slowly.
Finish your reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm row (rack support)
exercises.description: A one-arm row with your free hand braced on a rack for support. It lets you pull heavy while keeping your back steady.
steps: Place one hand on a rack or sturdy support and hinge forward with a flat back.
Hold a dumbbell in your other hand with your arm hanging.
Row the dumbbell toward your hip.
Squeeze your back at the top, then lower slowly.
Finish your reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: lever row (plate loaded)
exercises.description: A plate-loaded machine row. The guided path lets you pull heavy with good back engagement.
steps: Adjust the seat and chest pad, then grab the handles.
Sit tall with your chest against the pad.
Pull the handles toward your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Pause for a moment.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.

exercises.name: cable seated row (bent bar)
exercises.description: A seated cable row using a bent bar. The angled bar suits many wrists while you train the back.
steps: Sit at a low cable station with your feet on the platform and knees slightly bent.
Grab the bent bar with both hands.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs, keeping your back straight.
Squeeze your shoulder blades.
Extend your arms slowly without rounding forward.

exercises.name: bird dog
exercises.description: From hands and knees, you extend opposite arm and leg. It builds core control and back stability.
steps: Start on all fours with hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Extend your right arm forward and left leg back.
Keep your hips level and your back flat.
Hold for a moment, then return.
Repeat on the other side and alternate.

exercises.name: crunch (on bosu ball)
exercises.description: A crunch on a bosu ball. The unstable surface asks more from your core.
steps: Sit on the bosu ball and lie back so it supports your lower back.
Place your hands lightly behind your head.
Curl your shoulders up by contracting your abs.
Hold the top briefly.
Lower slowly and keep your feet planted.

exercises.name: dead bug v. 2
exercises.description: A lying core drill where arms and legs reach out while your back stays down. It trains core control.
steps: Lie on your back with arms pointing up and knees bent at 90 degrees.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Lower your right arm and left leg toward the floor.
Return and switch sides.
Move slowly and keep your back flat.

exercises.name: flutter kicks v. 3
exercises.description: Small alternating leg kicks while lying down. They fire up the lower abs and hip flexors.
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight and hands under your hips.
Lift your legs a few inches off the floor.
Kick your legs up and down in small alternating motions.
Keep your lower back pressed to the floor.
Continue for a set time and breathe steadily.

exercises.name: lying leg raise and hold
exercises.description: Raising your legs from the floor and holding them up. It targets the lower abs.
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your hands by your sides.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Raise your legs until they are vertical.
Lower them to just above the floor and hold for a couple of seconds.
Repeat without letting your back arch.

exercises.name: hollow hold
exercises.description: A gymnastics-style hold with your shoulders and legs lifted. It builds deep core strength.
steps: Lie on your back with your arms overhead and legs straight.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your shoulders and legs a few inches off the ground.
Hold the shape and breathe steadily.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then rest.

exercises.name: russian twist (with medicine ball)
exercises.description: Rotating a medicine ball from side to side while seated. It works the obliques.
steps: Sit with your knees bent and lean back slightly, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Lift your feet slightly if you can.
Rotate your torso to one side and tap the ball by your hip.
Rotate to the other side.
Keep your chest tall and move with control.

exercises.name: half wipers (bent leg)
exercises.description: Lying on your back and swinging bent legs side to side. It trains the obliques and lower abs.
steps: Lie on your back with your arms out to the sides for support.
Lift your knees to 90 degrees.
Lower both knees to one side, stopping before the floor.
Bring them back to the middle and go to the other side.
Keep your shoulders on the floor.

exercises.name: wipers (straight leg)
exercises.description: Swinging straight legs from side to side like windshield wipers. It is a tough one for the obliques and lower abs.
steps: Lie on your back with your arms out to the sides.
Raise your legs straight up over your hips.
Lower both legs to one side with control.
Lift them back to the middle and lower to the other side.
Keep your shoulders flat on the floor.

exercises.name: weighted crunch (behind head)
exercises.description: A crunch with a weight held behind your head. The extra load makes it harder on the abs.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a weight behind your head with your elbows out.
Curl your shoulders up, contracting your abs.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly without pulling on your neck.

exercises.name: lever donkey calf raise
exercises.description: A donkey calf raise on a lever machine. It trains the calves.
steps: Adjust the leverage machine to the appropriate height for your body.
Position yourself facing the machine, with your toes on the foot platform and your heels hanging off the edge.
Place your hands on the handles or the support bars for stability.
Engage your calves and lift your heels as high as possible, using the balls of your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: band bench press
exercises.description: A bench press using resistance bands. It trains the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Grasp the band handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms fully, pushing the bands away from your chest.
Slowly lower the bands back down to your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell decline pullover
exercises.description: A pullover on a decline bench with a barbell. It trains the chest and lats.
steps: Lie down on a decline bench with your head lower than your hips and your feet secured.
Hold the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the barbell in an arc motion behind your head, feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Pause for a moment, then return the barbell to the starting position by reversing the motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell reverse grip decline bench press
exercises.description: A reverse-grip bench press on a decline bench. It trains the lower chest and triceps.
steps: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your hips.
Grasp the barbell with a reverse grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell reverse grip incline bench press
exercises.description: A reverse-grip bench press on an incline bench. It trains the upper chest and triceps.
steps: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with a reverse grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell wide reverse grip bench press
exercises.description: A wide reverse-grip bench press. It trains the chest and triceps.
steps: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Grasp the barbell with a wide reverse grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in and your wrists straight.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest, then push it back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: behind head chest stretch
exercises.description: A stretch with the hands behind the head, pulling the elbows back. It opens the chest and shoulders.
steps: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Interlace your fingers behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Slowly squeeze your shoulder blades together and push your chest forward.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Release the stretch and repeat as desired.

exercises.name: cable decline one arm press
exercises.description: A one-arm cable press from a decline angle. It trains the chest and triceps.
steps: Adjust the cable machine to a decline position.
Stand facing away from the machine and grab the handle with one hand.
Position yourself with your back against the decline bench and your arm extended straight in front of you.
Bend your elbow and lower the handle towards your chest while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the handle back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: cable decline press
exercises.description: A decline cable press for the lower chest. It trains the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Adjust the cable machine to a decline position.
Sit on the decline bench facing the cable machine.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position them at chest level.
Keep your feet flat on the ground and your back firmly against the bench.
Exhale and push the handles away from your body, extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, squeezing your chest muscles.
Inhale and slowly return the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable one arm decline chest fly
exercises.description: A one-arm decline chest fly with a cable. It trains the lower chest.
steps: Attach a D-handle to a low pulley cable machine and set the bench to a decline angle.
Lie down on the bench with your head towards the machine and grab the handle with your right hand.
Extend your arm straight up above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
With a controlled motion, lower your arm out to the side until your hand is in line with your shoulder.
Pause for a moment, then reverse the motion and bring your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left arm and repeat the exercise.

exercises.name: cable one arm fly on exercise ball
exercises.description: A one-arm cable fly seated on an exercise ball. It trains the chest and core.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold a cable handle in one hand and extend your arm out to the side, parallel to the ground.
Keep your elbow slightly bent and your palm facing forward.
Slowly bring your arm across your body, squeezing your chest muscles.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exercises.name: cable one arm incline fly on exercise ball
exercises.description: A one-arm incline cable fly on an exercise ball. It trains the upper chest.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back against an incline bench.
Hold a cable handle in one hand with your arm extended and palm facing inward.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbow, slowly lower your arm out to the side until your hand is in line with your shoulder.
Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: cable one arm incline press
exercises.description: A one-arm incline cable press. It trains the upper chest and shoulders.
steps: Adjust the cable machine to a low pulley position.
Sit on an incline bench facing away from the cable machine.
Grasp the handle with one hand and bring it up to shoulder height.
Position your feet firmly on the ground and maintain a stable position.
Press the handle forward and upward, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exercises.name: cable one arm incline press on exercise ball
exercises.description: A one-arm incline cable press on an exercise ball. It trains the upper chest and balance.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back resting against an incline bench.
Hold a cable handle in one hand and position your arm at a 90-degree angle with your elbow bent.
Press the cable handle forward and upward, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: cable one arm press on exercise ball
exercises.description: A one-arm cable press on an exercise ball. It trains the chest and core.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold a cable handle in one hand and position your arm at chest height, elbow bent.
Place your other hand on your hip for stability.
Press the cable handle forward, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: cable press on exercise ball
exercises.description: A cable chest press on an exercise ball. It trains the chest and challenges balance.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees at a 90-degree angle.
Hold the cable handles at chest height with your palms facing down and your elbows bent.
Engage your core and press the cable handles forward until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment, then slowly release the tension and bring the cable handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable standing up straight crossovers
exercises.description: Standing cable crossovers with the hands crossing in front. It trains the chest.
steps: Stand in the middle of a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the handles of the cables with your palms facing down and your arms extended straight out to the sides.
Keeping your arms straight, bring your hands together in front of your body, crossing them over each other.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position, keeping your arms extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable upper chest crossovers
exercises.description: Cable crossovers aimed at the upper chest. It trains the upper pecs.
steps: Attach the handles to the cables at chest height.
Stand in the center of the cable machine with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Grasp the handles with your palms facing down and your arms extended out to the sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and engage your core.
Pull the cables together in front of your chest, crossing them over each other.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Slowly release the cables back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: chest and front of shoulder stretch
exercises.description: A stretch for the chest and the fronts of the shoulders with the hands clasped. It loosens the chest.
steps: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height.
Cross your arms in front of your body, with your right arm on top of your left arm.
Interlace your fingers and press your palms together.
Gently squeeze your shoulder blades together and push your hands forward, feeling a stretch in your chest and front of your shoulders.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: chest stretch with exercise ball
exercises.description: A chest stretch using an exercise ball held out in front. It loosens the chest.
steps: Sit on the stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold the exercise ball with both hands and extend your arms straight out in front of you.
Slowly bring the exercise ball towards your chest, feeling a stretch in your chest muscles.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: clap push up
exercises.description: An explosive push-up with a clap in mid-air. It builds power in the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your core engaged.
Push through your palms explosively to propel your body off the ground.
While in mid-air, clap your hands together before landing back in the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: deep push up
exercises.description: A deep push-up with a longer range of motion. It trains the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: drop push up
exercises.description: A push-up that drops to the knees and presses back up. It trains the chest and triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lower your chest towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Once your chest is just above the ground, quickly drop your knees to the ground.
Push yourself back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell decline one arm fly
exercises.description: Lying on a decline bench, you open one arm out to the side with a dumbbell and bring it back over your chest. It works the lower chest one side at a time.
steps: Lie down on a decline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on your thigh.
Using your thigh to help raise the dumbbell, lift it up to shoulder width with your palm facing your torso.
Rotate your wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing forward.
As you breathe in, lower the dumbbell slowly to the side until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Exhale and use your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell fly on exercise ball
exercises.description: A dumbbell fly done lying back on a stability ball. The unstable surface makes your core work while the chest does the opening and closing.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported by the ball.
Extend your arms straight up above your chest, palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows slightly and lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause for a moment, then reverse the movement and squeeze your chest muscles as you bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline fly on exercise ball
exercises.description: Dumbbell fly with your upper back on an incline bench and your hips supported by a stability ball. It hits the upper chest and challenges balance.
steps: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on an exercise ball and roll forward until your upper back is resting on the incline bench.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest.
Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline one arm fly
exercises.description: A single-arm fly on an incline bench that targets the upper chest. Working one side at a time helps you spot and fix left-right differences.
steps: Adjust the incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on your thigh.
Lie back on the bench, keeping your feet flat on the ground.
Hold the dumbbell with your arm extended straight up over your chest.
Lower the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause when your arm is parallel to the ground, then reverse the motion to bring the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline one arm fly on exercise ball
exercises.description: One-arm incline fly with your back supported on a stability ball. The unstable base adds a core challenge to the upper chest stretch.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell with your arm extended straight up over your chest, palm facing inwards.
Slowly lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause for a moment when your arm is parallel to the ground.
Engage your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline one arm press
exercises.description: Press a single dumbbell up from shoulder height on an incline bench. It builds the upper chest and shoulders and evens out strength between sides.
steps: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your thigh.
Lie back on the bench and position the dumbbell at shoulder level, palm facing forward.
Press the dumbbell upward and slightly inward, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline one arm press on exercise ball
exercises.description: A one-arm dumbbell press done with your upper back on a stability ball. Your core has to stay tight to keep you steady while the chest presses.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand, feet flat on the ground.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell at shoulder height with your palm facing forward.
Press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline press on exercise ball
exercises.description: A two-dumbbell press with your upper back on a stability ball. It trains the chest and shoulders while your core works to keep you balanced.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling your body down the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder level, elbows bent and pointing out to the sides.
Press the dumbbells upward, extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell lying pullover on exercise ball
exercises.description: Lying across a stability ball, you arc one dumbbell back over your head and return it. It stretches and works the chest and lats.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball and roll forward until your upper back is resting on the ball.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up over your chest.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your arms straight.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm bench fly
exercises.description: Flat bench fly with a single dumbbell. Lowering in a wide arc stretches one side of the chest, and bringing it back squeezes it.
steps: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on top of your thigh.
Lie back on the bench, keeping the dumbbell pressed against your thigh.
Using your free hand, help lift the dumbbell up to the starting position.
Hold the dumbbell directly above your shoulder with your arm extended and palm facing inward.
Lower the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause when your arm is parallel to the ground, then reverse the movement and bring the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms and repeat.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm chest fly on exercise ball
exercises.description: A one-arm chest fly with your upper back on a stability ball. The wobbly base brings your core in while the chest does the work.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet flat on the ground.
Walk your feet forward, rolling the ball until your upper back is supported on the ball and your head, neck, and shoulders are off the ball.
Extend your arm with the dumbbell straight up above your chest, palm facing inward.
Slowly lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause for a moment when your arm is parallel to the ground.
Engage your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm decline chest press
exercises.description: Press a single dumbbell up from a decline bench. It focuses on the lower chest and lets you train each side separately.
steps: Lie on a decline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your chest.
Place your feet flat on the ground and keep your back pressed against the bench.
Extend your arm and push the dumbbell up towards the ceiling, fully extending your elbow.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm fly on exercise ball
exercises.description: One-arm dumbbell fly with your upper back on a stability ball. It stretches and shapes the chest while your core keeps you steady.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet flat on the ground.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your upper back is resting on the exercise ball.
Extend your arm with the dumbbell straight up above your chest, palm facing inwards.
Slowly lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm incline chest press
exercises.description: Press one dumbbell up on an incline bench to train the upper chest and front shoulder. Working one arm at a time helps balance both sides.
steps: Adjust the incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your back against the pad and feet flat on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip, resting it on your shoulder.
Push the dumbbell up and away from your body, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm press on exercise ball
exercises.description: A single-arm dumbbell press done seated or lying on a stability ball. Balance and core control are part of every rep.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and position it at shoulder height, with your elbow bent and palm facing forward.
Slowly press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended, while keeping your core engaged and maintaining balance on the exercise ball.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm pullover on exercise ball
exercises.description: A pullover with one dumbbell while your upper back rests on a stability ball. It stretches the chest and lats and asks your core to stay braced.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell with one hand and extend your arm straight up above your chest.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your arm straight.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell one leg fly on exercise ball
exercises.description: A dumbbell fly on a stability ball with one leg lifted, which makes balance harder. It works the chest and trains core stability.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Place one foot on the ground and extend the other leg straight out in front of you.
Lean forward slightly and bring your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells down and out to the sides, feeling a stretch in your chest.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.

exercises.name: dumbbell press on exercise ball
exercises.description: Press two dumbbells up while your upper back rests on a stability ball. A good way to train the chest with extra core and balance demand.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and dumbbells in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball until your lower back is supported on the ball and your knees are at a 90-degree angle.
Raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell pullover hip extension on exercise ball
exercises.description: A dumbbell pullover on a stability ball combined with a hip lift. It trains the chest and lats while the glutes and core hold your body steady.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and the dumbbell resting on your thighs.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball down your back until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your arms straight and maintaining control.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
While keeping your arms extended, lift your hips off the ground, squeezing your glutes and engaging your core.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell pullover on exercise ball
exercises.description: A dumbbell pullover performed on a stability ball. The arc behind your head stretches the chest and lats and keeps your core busy.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball and hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest, arms extended.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your arms straight.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball pike push up
exercises.description: A pike push-up with your feet on a stability ball. It builds shoulders and chest and works your core to hold the ball steady.
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands on the floor and your shins resting on the stability ball.
Engage your core and lift your hips up towards the ceiling, rolling the ball towards your hands.
Keep your legs straight and your body in a pike position, forming an inverted V shape.
Bend your elbows and lower your upper body towards the floor, keeping your head in line with your hands.
Push through your hands and extend your arms to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: isometric chest squeeze
exercises.description: Press your palms or arms together in front of your chest and hold the squeeze. A simple way to feel and train the chest with no equipment.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the ground, with your palms facing each other.
Squeeze your chest muscles together as hard as you can, while keeping your arms straight.
Hold this position for a few seconds, focusing on contracting your chest muscles.
Release the squeeze and relax your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: kettlebell one arm floor press
exercises.description: Lying on the floor, press a kettlebell straight up with one arm. The floor limits the range, which is gentle on the shoulder while building the chest and triceps.
steps: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the kettlebell in one hand with your palm facing towards your feet and your arm extended straight up towards the ceiling.
Slowly lower the kettlebell towards your chest by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm close to your body.
Pause for a moment when the kettlebell is just above your chest, then push it back up to the starting position by extending your elbow.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: lever incline chest press
exercises.description: A machine press with the handles set on an incline path. It works the upper chest and front shoulders with a fixed, stable motion.
steps: Adjust the seat and backrest of the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Push the handles forward and away from your body until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bend your elbows and lower the handles back towards your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever decline chest press
exercises.description: A machine press that travels along a decline path. It focuses on the lower chest and triceps in a fixed, stable motion.
steps: Adjust the seat height and backrest of the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Push the handles forward and away from your body until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly lower the handles back towards your chest, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: machine inner chest press
exercises.description: A seated machine chest press where the handles bring your hands together. It emphasises the inner chest in a stable path.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, exhaling during the movement.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position, inhaling as you do so.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: medicine ball chest pass
exercises.description: Throw a medicine ball forward from your chest with a quick push, then catch it and repeat. It builds explosive pushing power in the chest and arms.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the medicine ball at chest level.
Extend your arms forward, pushing the medicine ball away from your chest with force.
As you release the ball, follow through with your arms and torso, transferring your weight from your back foot to your front foot.
Catch the ball as it rebounds off the wall or partner, and immediately repeat the movement.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: medicine ball chest push from 3 point stance
exercises.description: From a three point stance with one hand on a medicine ball, you push the ball away explosively. It trains the chest and arms with power and balance.
steps: Start in a 3 point stance with one hand on the medicine ball and the other hand on the ground.
Extend your legs and position your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest towards the ground while keeping your back straight.
Push the medicine ball away from your body, extending your arm fully.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: medicine ball chest push multiple response
exercises.description: Push a medicine ball away from your chest and catch it again in a quick, repeated flow. It builds explosive chest and arm power.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball at chest level.
Extend your arms forward, pushing the medicine ball away from your chest.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bring the medicine ball back to your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: medicine ball chest push single response
exercises.description: Push a medicine ball away from your chest in one strong effort, reset, then go again. It trains explosive power in the chest and arms.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the medicine ball at chest level.
Extend your arms forward, pushing the medicine ball away from your chest.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bring the medicine ball back to your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: plyo push up
exercises.description: A push-up that you drive explosively so your hands leave the floor. It builds fast pressing power in the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your body in a straight line.
Push explosively off the ground, using your chest muscles to propel your upper body off the ground.
Land softly with your hands back in the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: push up on bosu ball
exercises.description: A push-up with your hands on a bosu ball. The unstable surface makes your chest, shoulders and core work harder to stay steady.
steps: Place the bosu ball on the ground with the flat side facing up.
Position yourself in a push-up position with your hands on the outer edges of the bosu ball.
Engage your core and lower your body down towards the bosu ball by bending your elbows.
Push yourself back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith wide grip bench press
exercises.description: A bench press on a smith machine with a wide grip. The fixed bar path lets you focus on pressing, with extra work for the outer chest.
steps: Adjust the bench to a comfortable position on the smith machine.
Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows out to the sides.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith wide grip decline bench press
exercises.description: A smith machine bench press on a decline bench with a wide grip. It targets the lower chest along a guided bar path.
steps: Adjust the decline bench to the desired angle.
Lie down on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows pointed outwards.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: weighted drop push up
exercises.description: A weighted push-up variation where you drop and shift your hands between push-ups for extra load. It challenges the chest and triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Lower your chest towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Once your chest is just above the ground, explosively push yourself up, lifting your hands off the ground.
As you push up, quickly move your hands out to the sides and slightly forward, allowing your body to drop down towards the ground.
Catch yourself with your hands in the wider position and immediately lower your chest towards the ground again.
Repeat the push-up motion, dropping down and catching yourself with your hands in the narrower position.
Continue alternating between the wider and narrower hand positions for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: wide hand push up
exercises.description: A push-up with your hands placed wider than your shoulders. It puts more emphasis on the chest and less on the triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to toe.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: medicine ball chest push with run release
exercises.description: Push a medicine ball forward from your chest, then sprint after it and catch it. It trains explosive chest power plus quick acceleration.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball at chest level.
Step forward with your right foot and simultaneously push the medicine ball forward, extending your arms fully.
As you push the ball forward, release it and let it roll forward.
Quickly run forward and catch the ball before it hits the ground.
Once you catch the ball, bring it back to your chest and repeat the movement with your left foot forward.
Continue alternating legs and repeating the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever unilateral row
exercises.description: A machine row where you pull each handle independently. It works the upper back and lets you even out strength differences between sides.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself facing the machine.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your back straight.
Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: back extension on exercise ball
exercises.description: Lie face down over a stability ball and lift your chest to extend your back. It strengthens the lower back and glutes in a supported way.
steps: Place the stability ball on the ground and lie face down on top of it, with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall or other stable surface.
Position your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: back relaxation
exercises.description: A gentle resting position that lets the back relax and lengthen after training.
steps: Get into a comfortable resting position, such as kneeling with your torso folded forward.
Rest your arms in a relaxed position.
Let your back round and release.
Breathe slowly into your lower back.
Hold for 30-60 seconds.

exercises.name: barbell bent arm pullover
exercises.description: Lying on a bench, move a barbell in an arc behind your head and back over your chest with soft elbows. It works the lats and chest.
steps: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Hold a barbell with a shoulder-width grip and extend your arms straight above your chest.
Lower the barbell behind your head while keeping your arms slightly bent.
Pause for a moment, then raise the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell reverse grip incline bench row
exercises.description: A barbell row with an underhand grip, done chest down on an incline bench. The support removes momentum and targets the upper back and biceps.
steps: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench facing the backrest with your chest against it.
Grab the barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing down) and hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Pull the barbell towards your upper abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable incline bench row
exercises.description: A cable row done on an incline bench so your torso is supported. It works the upper back and biceps without lower back strain.
steps: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle and attach a cable handle to the low pulley.
Sit on the bench facing the cable machine with your feet flat on the floor and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the cable handle with an overhand grip and extend your arms fully in front of you.
Lean forward from your hips while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the cable handle towards your chest by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement, then slowly extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable palm rotational row
exercises.description: A cable row where your palms rotate from facing down to facing up as you pull. It works the upper back, lats and biceps through a twisting path.
steps: Attach a handle to a cable machine at waist height.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Step back to create tension on the cable, keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent.
Pull the handle towards your body, rotating your palms to face upwards as you do so.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Slowly release the handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable rope crossover seated row
exercises.description: A seated cable row using a rope so your hands can cross and finish wide. It works the upper back and lats with a longer range of motion.
steps: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the cable ropes with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Lean back slightly, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the cable ropes towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable rope elevated seated row
exercises.description: A seated cable row using a rope from an elevated seat position. It trains the upper back, lats and biceps with a neutral grip.
steps: Sit on the elevated seat facing the cable machine.
Grab the cable rope handles with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly back, maintaining a slight bend in your knees.
Pull the cable towards your body by retracting your shoulder blades and squeezing your back muscles.
Pause for a moment at the fully contracted position.
Slowly release the tension and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable rope extension incline bench row
exercises.description: A rope cable row done chest down on an incline bench. The support keeps your torso still so the upper back does the pulling.
steps: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle and attach a cable machine to the low pulley.
Attach a rope handle to the cable machine and sit on the incline bench facing the machine.
Grab the rope handle with an overhand grip and lean forward, keeping your back straight.
Extend your arms fully, pulling the rope towards your upper chest while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable rope seated row
exercises.description: A seated row with a rope attachment on a cable station. The neutral grip works the upper back, lats and biceps.
steps: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet flat on the footrests and knees slightly bent.
Grasp the cable ropes with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Pull the cable ropes towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable upper row
exercises.description: A cable row with a straight bar pulled toward your upper chest. It targets the upper back and rear shoulders.
steps: Attach a straight bar to a cable machine at chest height.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the bar towards your upper chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly release the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable wide grip rear pulldown behind neck
exercises.description: A wide grip pulldown where the bar travels behind your neck. It works the lats and upper back but needs good shoulder mobility and control.
steps: Adjust the cable machine so that the pulldown bar is at a height above your head.
Sit down on the seat and grab the pulldown bar with a wide overhand grip.
Keep your back straight and your chest up as you lean back slightly.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the bar back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: chin-up
exercises.description: Hang from a bar with an underhand grip and pull until your chin clears it. A classic builder of the lats and biceps.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing towards you and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: close grip chin-up
exercises.description: A chin-up with your hands close together on an underhand grip. It works the lats and puts extra load on the biceps.
steps: Grab the pull-up bar with your palms facing towards you and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your feet off the ground.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell lying rear delt row
exercises.description: Lie face down on a bench and row two dumbbells up and out. It targets the rear shoulders and upper back without any body swing.
steps: Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Extend your arms straight down towards the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Engaging your back muscles, lift the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell palm rotational bent over row
exercises.description: A bent over dumbbell row where your palms rotate as you pull. It works the upper back, lats and biceps through a varied path.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent.
Let your arms hang straight down, palms facing your body.
Engage your core and pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
As you pull the dumbbells up, rotate your palms so they face away from your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position, rotating your palms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell reverse grip incline bench one arm row
exercises.description: A one-arm row with an underhand grip, supported on an incline bench. It works the upper back and biceps one side at a time.
steps: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Place a dumbbell on the floor next to the bench.
Stand facing the bench with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend at the waist and place your left knee and left hand on the bench for support.
Pick up the dumbbell with your right hand using a reverse grip (palm facing down).
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the dumbbell up towards your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch sides and repeat the exercise with your left arm.

exercises.name: dumbbell reverse grip incline bench two arm row
exercises.description: A two-arm dumbbell row with an underhand grip, chest down on an incline bench. The support keeps you strict so the back and biceps work.
steps: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your chest against the backrest and your feet flat on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Lean forward and let your arms hang straight down, fully extended.
Pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball alternating arm ups
exercises.description: Seated on a stability ball, you raise dumbbells one arm at a time. It trains the shoulders and upper back while your core keeps you balanced.
steps: Sit on the stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards and your arms extended down by your sides.
Engage your core and slowly lift one arm up towards your shoulder, keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arm back down to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball back extension with arms extended
exercises.description: Lie face down on a stability ball with your arms reaching forward and lift your torso. It strengthens the lower back and glutes with extra leverage.
steps: Place the stability ball on the ground and lie face down on top of it, with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall for stability.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, with your palms facing down.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, keeping your back straight and your neck in line with your spine.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball back extension with hands behind head
exercises.description: A stability ball back extension with your hands behind your head. It strengthens the lower back, glutes and upper back.
steps: Place the stability ball on the ground and lie face down on top of it with your hips resting on the ball.
Position your feet against a wall or other stable surface for support.
Cross your arms behind your head, with your hands touching the back of your head.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your hips.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball back extension with knees off ground
exercises.description: A back extension on a stability ball with your legs braced so your knees stay off the ground. It works the lower back and glutes.
steps: Place the stability ball on the ground and lie face down on top of it, with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall for stability.
Position your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball back extension with rotation
exercises.description: A stability ball back extension where you add a twist at the top. It trains the lower back, glutes and obliques.
steps: Start by lying face down on the stability ball with your hips resting on the ball and your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Place your hands behind your head or cross them over your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly rotate your torso to one side, keeping your hips and legs stable.
Return to the center and repeat the rotation to the other side.
Lower your upper body back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball back stretch
exercises.description: Draping your back over a stability ball to lengthen the spine and stretch the lats.
steps: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward.
Lean back until your back rests over the ball.
Let your arms fall overhead and relax.
Breathe deeply and let your back open.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: exercise ball hug
exercises.description: Sit on a stability ball and lean back into it while hugging the ball. It gently opens up the back and stretches the spine.
steps: Sit on the stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold the stability ball with both hands, hugging it close to your chest.
Engage your core muscles and slowly lean back, keeping your back straight and your feet planted on the ground.
Continue leaning back until you feel a stretch in your back muscles.
Hold the position for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball lat stretch
exercises.description: Sit on a stability ball and reach one arm overhead as you lean to the other side. It stretches the lat and the side of your torso.
steps: Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and extend your arm straight up overhead.
Slowly lean to the opposite side, feeling a stretch in your lat muscle.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: exercise ball lower back prone stretch
exercises.description: Lying face down over a stability ball to stretch the lower back.
steps: Kneel by a stability ball and lay your torso over it.
Roll forward so your hips rest on the ball.
Let your arms and head hang down in a relaxed way.
Breathe slowly and let your lower back release.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: exercise ball lower back stretch (pyramid)
exercises.description: Lie back over a stability ball to open up and stretch the lower back. It is a gentle, supported way to ease tightness.
steps: Sit on the stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the ball down your back until your lower back is resting on the ball.
Place your hands behind your head or cross them over your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lower your upper body towards the ground, allowing your lower back to stretch over the ball.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball lying side lat stretch
exercises.description: Lie on your side with a stability ball supporting you and reach overhead. It stretches the lat and the side of your torso.
steps: Lie on your side with your legs extended and your head supported by the stability ball.
Place your top arm on the ball for stability.
Reach your top arm overhead and allow your torso to rotate slightly.
Feel the stretch in your lat muscles on the side of your body.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides and repeat.

exercises.name: exercise ball prone leg raise
exercises.description: Lie face down with your toes on a stability ball and lift your legs. It works the lower back and glutes with a gentle range.
steps: Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended and your toes resting on top of the stability ball.
Place your hands on the ground, shoulder-width apart, and engage your core muscles.
Keeping your legs straight, slowly lift them off the ground, using your lower back and glutes to raise them as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: ez bar reverse grip bent over row
exercises.description: A bent over row with an ez barbell and an underhand grip. It targets the upper back and lats with extra work for the biceps.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and hands shoulder-width apart.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up, until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
Pull the ez barbell towards your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the ez barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: kettlebell two arm row
exercises.description: Hinge forward and row a kettlebell in each hand to your sides. It works the upper back and lats and trains grip strength.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a kettlebell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the kettlebells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the kettlebells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: kneeling lat stretch
exercises.description: Kneel and reach your arms overhead, then lean to one side. It stretches the lat and the side of your torso.
steps: Kneel on the ground with your knees hip-width apart and your toes pointing back.
Extend your arms overhead and interlace your fingers.
Keeping your back straight, slowly lean to the right side, feeling a stretch in your left lat muscle.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then return to the starting position.
Repeat the stretch on the left side, leaning to the left and feeling a stretch in your right lat muscle.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever one arm lateral wide pulldown
exercises.description: A one-arm pulldown on a lever machine that works the lats one side at a time. It helps even out strength between left and right.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handle with an overhand grip and fully extend your arm, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pull the handle down and across your body towards your opposite hip, squeezing your lat muscle at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return the handle to the starting position, fully extending your arm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exercises.name: lever reverse grip vertical row
exercises.description: A machine row with an underhand grip and a vertical handle path. It works the upper back, lats and biceps.
steps: Adjust the seat height and footplate position to ensure proper alignment.
Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the footplate.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever reverse t-bar row
exercises.description: A reverse grip row on a t-bar style machine, chest supported. It builds the upper back and lats with a strict path.
steps: Adjust the seat height and footplate position on the leverage machine.
Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the footplate.
