Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever seated row
exercises.description: A seated row on a lever machine with chest support. It works the upper back and lats with minimal lower back strain.
steps: Adjust the seat height and footrests to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet on the footrests.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement.
Slowly release the handles and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever t-bar reverse grip row
exercises.description: A t-bar style machine row with a reverse grip and chest support. It works the upper back, lats and biceps.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lower back curl
exercises.description: Lie face down and lift your chest off the floor in a curling motion. It strengthens the lower back with a gentle bodyweight movement.
steps: Lie flat on your stomach with your legs extended and your arms by your sides.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings, and slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling your back upwards.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: medicine ball catch and overhead throw
exercises.description: Squat down, then explode up and throw a medicine ball overhead and catch it again. It trains power through the hips, back and shoulders.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball in both hands at chest level.
Bend your knees slightly and engage your core.
Lower your body into a squat position, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Explosively extend your hips and legs, while simultaneously throwing the medicine ball overhead.
Release the ball at the top of the movement and catch it on the way down.
Lower your body back into the squat position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: medicine ball overhead slam
exercises.description: Lift a medicine ball overhead and slam it into the floor with force. It builds full body power and trains the lats, core and shoulders.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball with both hands above your head.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Bend your knees slightly and forcefully slam the medicine ball down to the ground in front of you.
As you slam the ball down, use your entire body to generate power, including your shoulders and core.
Catch the ball on the bounce and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: one arm against wall
exercises.description: Stand facing a wall and press one arm into it while you lean in. It switches on the lats and shoulder with no equipment.
steps: Stand facing a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend one arm straight out in front of you and place your palm against the wall.
Engage your core and lean your body forward, keeping your arm straight and your back flat.
Slowly push against the wall with your palm, activating your lat muscles.
Hold the position for a few seconds, then release and repeat with the other arm.

exercises.name: lever one arm lateral high row
exercises.description: A one-arm high row on a lever machine. It works the upper back and lats and lets you train each side on its own.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself facing the machine.
Grasp the handle with one hand and keep your back straight.
Pull the handle towards your body, keeping your elbow close to your side.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly release the handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: one handed hang
exercises.description: Hanging from a bar with just one hand. It builds grip strength and gives the shoulder a stretch.
steps: Stand under a pull-up bar and grip it with one hand.
Lift your feet and hang with your arm straight.
Keep your shoulder active and your body still.
Hold for 10-20 seconds.
Lower yourself carefully and switch hands.

exercises.name: side lying floor stretch
exercises.description: Lie on your side and reach overhead to open up the side of your torso. It stretches the lats and the muscles between your ribs.
steps: Lie on your side with your legs straight and your bottom arm extended straight overhead.
Bend your top knee and place your foot on the ground in front of your bottom leg.
Reach your top arm over your head and grab onto something stable, like a wall or a piece of furniture.
Slowly lift your bottom leg off the ground, keeping it straight, until you feel a stretch in your side.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then slowly lower your leg back down.
Repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: smith bent over row
exercises.description: A bent over row using a smith machine bar with an overhand grip. The fixed path helps you focus on the upper back and lats.
steps: Set up the smith machine with the bar at hip height.
Stand facing the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Pull the bar towards your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the bar back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith one arm row
exercises.description: A one-arm row using a smith machine bar. It trains the upper back and lats one side at a time along a guided path.
steps: Adjust the height of the smith machine bar to waist level.
Stand facing the smith machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Grasp the bar with one hand using an overhand grip, with your palm facing down.
Keep your elbow close to your body and pull the bar towards your waist, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: smith reverse grip bent over row
exercises.description: A bent over row on a smith machine with an underhand grip. It works the upper back, lats and biceps along a guided path.
steps: Set up the smith machine with the bar at hip height.
Stand facing the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull the bar towards your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the bar back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: sphinx
exercises.description: Lie face down and prop yourself up on your forearms with your chest lifted. It gently extends the spine and opens the chest.
steps: Lie face down on the ground with your forearms flat on the floor, elbows directly under your shoulders.
Engage your core and lift your chest off the ground, keeping your forearms and toes on the floor.
Hold this position for a few seconds, making sure to keep your neck in a neutral position.
Slowly lower your chest back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: spine stretch
exercises.description: Sit with your legs out in front of you and lean back on your hands. It gives the spine and front of the torso a gentle stretch.
steps: Sit on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Place your hands on the ground behind you, fingers pointing towards your body.
Engage your core and slowly lean back, keeping your back straight.
Continue leaning back until you feel a stretch in your spine.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: standing pelvic tilt
exercises.description: Stand and tilt your pelvis back and forth to move your lower back. It loosens the lower back and teaches pelvic control.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Place your hands on your hips or let them hang by your sides.
Engage your core muscles and tilt your pelvis forward, pushing your lower back towards the wall behind you.
Hold the position for a few seconds, then release and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: upper back stretch
exercises.description: Reach your arms forward and round your upper back to open up the space between your shoulder blades. It stretches the upper back.
steps: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms straight in front of you, parallel to the ground.
Interlace your fingers and rotate your palms away from your body.
Slowly raise your arms overhead, keeping them straight and parallel to each other.
As you raise your arms, squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then release and repeat.

exercises.name: upward facing dog
exercises.description: A yoga pose where you lift your chest and thighs off the floor on straight arms. It opens the chest and strengthens the back.
steps: Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended behind you.
Place your hands on the floor next to your lower ribs, fingers pointing forward.
Press your hands firmly into the floor and straighten your arms, lifting your torso and thighs off the ground.
Roll your shoulders back and down, opening your chest and lifting your gaze towards the ceiling.
Hold this position for a few breaths, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: wide grip rear pull-up
exercises.description: A pull-up on a wide overhand grip, pulling to the back of your neck or upper chest. It targets the lats and upper back.
steps: Grab the pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: ankle circles
exercises.description: Sit and move your foot in slow circles from the ankle. It warms up the ankle joint and the muscles around the calf.
steps: Sit on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Lift one leg off the ground and rotate your ankle in a circular motion.
Perform the desired number of circles in one direction, then switch to the other direction.
Repeat with the other leg.

exercises.name: band two legs calf raise - (band under both legs) v. 2
exercises.description: A standing calf raise with a resistance band under both feet. It builds the calves and ankle strength with progressive tension.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a resistance band under both feet.
Hold the ends of the band with your hands for stability.
Raise your heels off the ground as high as possible, using your calves.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell floor calf raise
exercises.description: Stand with a barbell across your back and raise onto your toes from the floor. It works the calves, with the full range limited to flat ground.
steps: Place a barbell on the floor in front of you.
Stand with the balls of your feet on the edge of the barbell, with your heels hanging off.
Hold onto a stable object for balance if needed.
Raise your heels as high as possible, using your calves to lift your body.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell seated calf raise
exercises.description: Seated calf raise with a barbell resting on your thighs. The bent knee shifts the work to the soleus muscle under the calf.
steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and a barbell resting on your thighs.
Place the balls of your feet on a raised platform, such as a block or step.
Lower your heels as far as possible, feeling a stretch in your calves.
Raise your heels as high as possible, contracting your calves.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell standing calf raise
exercises.description: Stand with a barbell on your upper back and rise onto your toes. It builds the calves and ankle strength.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a barbell across your upper back.
Raise your heels off the ground as high as possible, using only your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: bodyweight standing calf raise
exercises.description: A standing calf raise using just your body weight. It strengthens the calves and ankles and needs no equipment.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward.
Place your hands on a wall or stable surface for balance.
Slowly raise your heels off the ground, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: box jump down with one leg stabilization
exercises.description: Step off a box and land on both feet, then hold the landing on one leg. It builds landing control and strengthens the calves and ankle.
steps: Stand in front of a box or platform with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and jump onto the box, landing softly with one foot on the box and the other foot hanging off the edge.
Stabilize yourself on the box with the foot that is on it, while keeping the other foot off the ground.
Hold this position for a few seconds, engaging your calf muscles to maintain balance.
Slowly step down with the foot that is on the box, returning to the starting position.
Repeat the exercise with the other leg.

exercises.name: cable standing calf raise
exercises.description: A standing calf raise using a cable for resistance. It builds the calves with a steady pull through the whole movement.
steps: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold onto the cable machine handles or attach a cable ankle strap to your ankles.
Raise your heels off the ground by extending your ankles as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable standing one leg calf raise
exercises.description: A one-leg standing calf raise using a cable for resistance. It trains each calf separately and helps balance.
steps: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold onto the cable machine for support.
Lift one leg off the ground and balance on the other leg.
Slowly raise your heel off the ground, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.

exercises.name: calf stretch with hands against wall
exercises.description: Stand facing a wall and place your hands on it, one foot back with heel down. It stretches the calf of the back leg.
steps: Stand facing a wall with your feet hip-width apart.
Place your hands against the wall at shoulder height.
Step your right foot back, keeping your heel on the ground and your leg straight.
Bend your left knee and lean forward, keeping your back leg straight and your heel on the ground.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Switch legs and repeat the stretch.

exercises.name: calf stretch with rope
exercises.description: A calf stretch where you use a rope to help pull your toes toward you. It stretches the calf and the back of the lower leg.
steps: Stand facing a wall or sturdy object with your feet hip-width apart.
Hold the ends of the rope in each hand and place the middle of the rope around the ball of your right foot.
Step back with your left foot, keeping your heel on the ground and your leg straight.
Lean forward, keeping your back straight, and gently pull on the rope to stretch your calf.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release.
Repeat on the other leg.

exercises.name: dumbbell seated calf raise
exercises.description: Seated calf raise with a dumbbell resting on your knees. The bent knee focuses on the soleus beneath the calf.
steps: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the ground and a dumbbell resting on your thighs.
Place the balls of your feet on a raised surface such as a step or block, with your heels hanging off the edge.
Hold onto the dumbbell for stability.
Raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell seated one leg calf raise - hammer grip
exercises.description: A one-leg seated calf raise with a dumbbell held in a hammer grip. It trains the soleus under the calf one side at a time.
steps: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the ground and a dumbbell resting on your thighs.
Place one foot on a raised surface, such as a step or block, with your heel hanging off the edge.
Hold the dumbbell with a hammer grip, meaning your palms are facing each other and your fingers are wrapped around the handle.
Keeping your core engaged and your back straight, slowly raise your heel as high as possible by pushing through the ball of your foot.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.

exercises.name: dumbbell seated one leg calf raise - palm up
exercises.description: A one-leg seated calf raise with a dumbbell held with your palm up. It works the soleus under the calf one side at a time.
steps: Sit on a bench or chair with your back straight and your feet flat on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and place it on top of your thigh, palm facing up.
Lift one leg off the ground and extend it in front of you, keeping your knee slightly bent.
Raise your heel as high as possible by pushing through the ball of your foot.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.

exercises.name: exercise ball on the wall calf raise
exercises.description: Calf raises with a stability ball held between your back and a wall. It works the calves while the ball helps you stay balanced.
steps: Stand with your back against a wall and place an exercise ball between your lower back and the wall.
Position your feet shoulder-width apart, with your toes pointing forward.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, with your arms extended by your sides.
Raise your heels off the ground, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: hack calf raise
exercises.description: A calf raise on a hack machine, pushing through the balls of your feet. It builds the calves under a supported load.
steps: Adjust the sled machine to a comfortable weight.
Stand on the sled machine with your toes on the platform and your heels hanging off.
Hold onto the handles for stability.
Raise your heels as high as possible by pushing through the balls of your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: hack one leg calf raise
exercises.description: A one-leg calf raise on a hack machine. It lets you train each calf on its own under a supported load.
steps: Adjust the sled machine to an appropriate weight.
Stand on the sled machine with one foot, keeping the other foot off the ground.
Hold onto the handles for stability.
Raise your heel as high as possible, lifting your body up on the ball of your foot.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch legs and repeat the exercise.

exercises.name: lever seated squat calf raise on leg press machine
exercises.description: A calf raise performed on a leg press machine by pressing with your toes. It builds the calves with a stable, supported load.
steps: Adjust the seat of the leg press machine so that your knees are slightly bent when your feet are on the footplate.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the footplate, shoulder-width apart.
Place your toes and the balls of your feet on the footplate, keeping your heels off the edge.
Release the safety handles and push the footplate away from you by extending your knees.
Once your knees are fully extended, slowly lower your heels by flexing your calves.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the footplate back up by extending your calves.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: one leg donkey calf raise
exercises.description: A one-leg donkey calf raise where you bend forward and rise onto your toes. It trains the calf with a deep stretch at the bottom.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward.
Place your hands on a stable surface for support, such as a wall or a bar.
Lift one leg off the ground, keeping your knee slightly bent.
Raise your heel as high as possible, using your calf muscles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.

exercises.name: one leg floor calf raise
exercises.description: A one-leg calf raise on the floor with a hand on a wall for balance. It builds calf strength and ankle stability.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place your hands on a wall or sturdy object for balance.
Lift one foot off the ground and balance on the other foot.
Slowly raise your heel off the ground, lifting your body up onto the ball of your foot.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.

exercises.name: peroneals stretch
exercises.description: A seated stretch where you turn your foot to open the outer side of your lower leg. It targets the peroneal muscles beside the calf.
steps: Sit on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Loop the rope around the ball of your foot and hold the ends of the rope with your hands.
Gently pull the rope towards you, flexing your foot and stretching your calf muscles.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Release the tension on the rope and repeat the stretch on the other leg.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: posterior tibialis stretch
exercises.description: A seated stretch that opens the inner side of the lower leg. It targets the posterior tibialis along your shin and ankle.
steps: Sit on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Loop the rope around the ball of your foot and hold the ends of the rope with your hands.
Gently pull the rope towards you, flexing your foot and stretching your calf muscles.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release the tension on the rope and relax your foot.
Repeat the stretch on the other leg.

exercises.name: seated calf stretch (male)
exercises.description: Sit on a chair and reach to pull your toes toward you. It stretches the calf and the back of the lower leg.
steps: Sit on the edge of a chair or bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Extend one leg straight out in front of you, keeping your heel on the ground.
Lean forward slightly, feeling a stretch in your calf muscle.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Switch legs and repeat the stretch.

exercises.name: sled calf press on leg press
exercises.description: A calf press done on a leg press sled using only your toes. It builds the calves under a supported load.
steps: Adjust the seat of the leg press machine so that your knees are slightly bent when your feet are on the sled.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart on the sled, with your toes pointing forward.
Release the safety handles and push the sled away from you by extending your knees and ankles.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the sled back down by bending your knees and ankles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: sled one leg calf press on leg press
exercises.description: A one-leg calf press on a leg press sled using only your toes. It trains each calf separately under a supported load.
steps: Adjust the seat of the leg press machine so that your knees are slightly bent when your feet are on the sled.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet on the sled, shoulder-width apart.
Place your toes and the balls of your feet on the sled, keeping your heels off.
Push the sled forward by extending your ankles, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the sled back down by flexing your ankles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith one leg floor calf raise
exercises.description: A one-leg calf raise lifting a smith machine bar from the floor. It works each calf on its own under a guided bar path.
steps: Position yourself on the floor under the smith machine bar, facing away from the machine.
Place the balls of your feet on a raised surface, such as a weight plate or block.
Position the smith machine bar across your lower legs, just above your ankles.
Hold onto the bar with your hands for stability.
Raise your heels off the ground by extending your ankles, lifting your body up.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith reverse calf raises
exercises.description: A smith machine calf raise done with the bar in front of you. It targets the calves and the muscles around the shin.
steps: Adjust the smith machine bar to a height just below your shoulders.
Stand facing the bar with your feet hip-width apart and toes pointing forward.
Place the balls of your feet on the edge of a step or platform, with your heels hanging off.
Hold onto the bar for support.
Raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith seated one leg calf raise
exercises.description: A seated one-leg calf raise using a smith machine. The bent knee puts the focus on the soleus under the calf.
steps: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and your feet on the footrest.
Place one leg on the footrest and keep the other leg off the footrest.
Using your calf muscles, raise your heel as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.

exercises.name: smith toe raise
exercises.description: A smith machine toe raise where you rise onto the balls of your feet. It builds the calves and ankle strength.
steps: Adjust the smith machine bar to a height that allows you to comfortably stand with your feet flat on the ground.
Position yourself under the bar with your shoulders directly below it and your feet shoulder-width apart.
Place the balls of your feet on a raised platform or weight plates, with your heels hanging off the edge.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the exercise.
Slowly raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: standing calves
exercises.description: A standing calf raise where you lift your heels as high as you can. It builds the calf muscles.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward.
Raise your heels off the ground as high as possible, standing on your toes.
Hold the position for a moment, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: standing calves calf stretch
exercises.description: Stand facing a wall and step one foot back with the heel down. It stretches the calf of the back leg.
steps: Stand facing a wall or sturdy object, about an arm's length away.
Place your hands on the wall or object at shoulder height.
Step back with one foot, keeping your heel flat on the ground.
Bend your front knee slightly and lean forward, keeping your back leg straight.
You should feel a stretch in your calf muscle.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Repeat on the other leg.

exercises.name: bench dip on floor
exercises.description: With your hands on a bench behind you and your feet on the floor, you bend and straighten your elbows. It builds the triceps, chest and shoulders.
steps: Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with your hands gripping the edge, fingers pointing forward.
Slide your butt off the bench, supporting your weight with your hands.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: squat side kick
exercises.description: Squatting down and then kicking one leg out to the side. It trains the thighs and glutes.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Squat down with your chest up.
Stand up and kick your right leg out to the side.
Return the foot to the floor and drop into the next squat.
Alternate sides each rep.

exercises.name: muscle-up (on vertical bar)
exercises.description: A muscle-up on a vertical bar, pulling up and then pressing over the top. It trains the lats, chest and triceps in one flowing move.
steps: Start by hanging from a vertical bar with your palms facing away from you and your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
As you pull yourself up, lean back slightly and bring your elbows towards your sides.
Continue pulling until your chest reaches the bar and your elbows are fully bent.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: l sit
exercises.description: An isometric hold where your body is supported by your arms and your legs stay straight out in front, forming an L.
steps: Sit between two supports or on the floor and place your hands beside your hips.
Press down through your hands to lift your hips and legs off the floor.
Extend your legs straight in front of you.
Keep your shoulders pressed down and your core tight.
Hold for as long as you can with good form, then lower.

exercises.name: neck side stretch
exercises.description: Gently tilt your head sideways to stretch the side of your neck. It eases tension in the neck and upper shoulder.
steps: Stand or sit up straight with your shoulders relaxed.
Tilt your head to one side, bringing your ear towards your shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Repeat on the other side.
Perform 2-4 sets on each side.

exercises.name: back stretch
exercises.description: A simple stretch to lengthen the back and ease tightness.
steps: Stand or sit tall and clasp your hands in front of you.
Press your arms forward and round your upper back.
Let your head drop gently.
Breathe slowly into your back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: back pec stretch
exercises.description: A stretch for the chest and front of the shoulder with your arms reached behind you. It opens up the pecs and lats.
steps: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the ground.
Cross your arms in front of your body, with your right arm over your left arm.
Interlock your fingers and rotate your palms away from your body.
Slowly raise your arms up and away from your body, feeling a stretch in your back and chest.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then release.
Repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.name: hamstring lying stretch
exercises.description: A simple lying hamstring stretch that eases tightness at the back of the thigh.
steps: Lie on your back with both legs extended.
Raise one leg and hold behind the thigh or calf.
Gently straighten the knee while pulling the leg toward you.
Keep your other leg flat and your back relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.

exercises.name: calf push stretch with hands against wall
exercises.description: Stand facing a wall with your hands on it and push your heel down on the back leg. It stretches the calf of the back leg.
steps: Stand facing a wall with your feet hip-width apart.
Place your hands against the wall at shoulder height.
Step back with one foot, keeping your heel on the ground and your leg straight.
Bend your front knee slightly and lean forward, feeling a stretch in your calf.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Switch legs and repeat the stretch.

exercises.name: band hip lift
exercises.description: Lie on your back with a band around your thighs and lift your hips. It strengthens the glutes and the outer hips.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place a resistance band just above your knees.
Engage your glutes and core muscles.
Press your heels into the ground and lift your hips off the floor, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell glute bridge
exercises.description: Lie on your back with a barbell across your hips and lift your hips high. It builds the glutes and the back of the thighs.
steps: Start by lying flat on your back on the ground with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place a barbell across your hips, holding it securely with both hands.
Engage your glutes and core muscles, then lift your hips off the ground until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your glutes.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell lateral lunge
exercises.description: With a barbell on your upper back, step to the side and sit into a lateral lunge. It works the glutes, inner thighs and quads.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back.
Take a big step to the side with your right foot, keeping your left foot planted.
Bend your right knee and lower your body down into a lunge position, keeping your left leg straight.
Push off with your right foot and return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side, stepping with your left foot.

exercises.name: barbell palms down wrist curl over a bench
exercises.description: Sit with your forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms down, and curl a barbell up with your wrists. It strengthens the back of the forearms.
steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your forearms resting on your thighs, palms facing down.
Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Lower the barbell towards the ground by flexing your wrists, keeping your forearms stationary.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly raise the barbell back up by extending your wrists.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell palms up wrist curl over a bench
exercises.description: Sit with your forearms on a bench, palms up, and curl a barbell with your wrists. It strengthens the front of the forearms and grip.
steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Rest your forearms on the bench, allowing your wrists to hang off the edge.
Keeping your forearms stationary, exhale and curl your wrists upwards as far as possible.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause, then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable reverse one arm curl
exercises.description: A one-arm curl with a cable using an overhand grip. It works the forearms and the outer part of the biceps.
steps: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the cable handle with an underhand grip, palm facing down.
Keep your elbow close to your side and slowly curl your forearm up towards your shoulder.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your forearm back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm reverse preacher curl
exercises.description: Rest your arm on a preacher bench and curl a dumbbell with an overhand grip. It targets the biceps and forearms with no body swing.
steps: Sit on a preacher bench with your chest against the pad and your arm extended over the edge of the bench, holding a dumbbell with an underhand grip.
Lower the dumbbell slowly until your arm is fully extended.
Curl the dumbbell back up towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm seated neutral wrist curl
exercises.description: Sit with your forearm supported and curl a dumbbell with your wrist in a neutral position. It strengthens the forearms and builds grip.
steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing up.
Rest your forearm on your thigh, allowing your wrist to hang off the edge.
Keeping your forearm stationary, curl your wrist upward as far as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your wrist back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other hand.

exercises.name: exercise ball one leg prone lower body rotation
exercises.description: Lie face down over a stability ball with one leg lifted and rotate it slightly. It strengthens the glutes and hips while your core balances.
steps: Lie face down on the stability ball with your hips resting on the ball and your legs extended straight behind you.
Place your hands on the ground in front of you for support.
Engage your glutes and core muscles to stabilize your body.
Slowly lift one leg off the ground, keeping it straight and parallel to the floor.
Rotate your leg outward, away from your body, while keeping your hips and upper body stable.
Pause for a moment at the end of the rotation, then slowly return your leg to the starting position.
Repeat the rotation with the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball one legged diagonal kick hamstring curl
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your heels on a stability ball and curl one leg toward you while kicking diagonally. It works the hamstrings, glutes and core.
steps: Start by lying on your back with your legs extended and your heels resting on top of the stability ball.
Place your arms by your sides for stability.
Engage your glutes and core muscles to lift your hips off the ground, creating a straight line from your shoulders to your heels.
Bend your right knee and bring it towards your chest, keeping your left leg extended and your foot flexed.
Kick your right leg diagonally across your body, extending it fully and engaging your hamstrings.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position, maintaining control and stability.
Repeat the movement with your left leg, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: hug keens to chest
exercises.description: Stand and pull one knee up to your chest with both hands. It stretches the glutes and loosens the hip and lower back.
steps: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and lower your body down into a squat position.
As you squat down, bring your knees up towards your chest and hug them with your arms.
Hold this position for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: iron cross stretch
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your arms out and cross one leg over your body toward the opposite hand. It stretches the glutes and lower back.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your arms extended out to the sides.
Raise your legs up towards the ceiling, keeping them straight.
Slowly lower your legs to one side, aiming to touch the floor with your feet.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then return your legs to the starting position.
Repeat the stretch on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: kneeling jump squat
exercises.description: Start on your knees and explosively swing your arms to jump up onto your feet. It builds power in the glutes and hips.
steps: Start by kneeling on the ground with your feet hip-width apart and your toes pointing forward.
Hold a barbell across your upper back, resting it on your shoulders.
Engage your core and glutes, then explosively jump up into the air, extending your hips and knees.
As you jump, push through your toes and fully extend your ankles, knees, and hips.
Land softly back on the ground, bending your knees to absorb the impact.
Immediately go into the next repetition, repeating the jump squat motion.

exercises.name: modified push up to lower arms
exercises.description: A modified push-up variation where you shift your weight toward your wrists. It strengthens the forearms, chest and shoulders.
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Lower your body down towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Once your elbows are at a 90-degree angle, lower your forearms to the ground, keeping your elbows directly under your shoulders.
Pause for a moment, then push through your palms to lift your forearms back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: pelvic tilt into bridge
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your knees bent, tilt your pelvis, then lift into a bridge. It warms up the glutes, lower back and core.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your arms by your sides with your palms facing down.
Engage your glutes and core muscles.
Tilt your pelvis upward, lifting your hips off the ground.
Hold the bridge position for a few seconds.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: reverse hyper on flat bench
exercises.description: Lie face down with your hips at the end of a bench and swing your legs up behind you. It works the glutes and lower back.
steps: Lie face down on a flat bench with your hips at the edge and your legs hanging off the bench.
Hold onto the bench for stability.
Keeping your legs straight, raise them up towards the ceiling as high as you can.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: seated glute stretch
exercises.description: Sit on the floor and cross one ankle over the opposite knee, then lean in. It stretches the glutes and the outer hip.
steps: Sit on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Bend your right knee and cross your right ankle over your left thigh.
Place your right hand on the ground behind you for support.
With your left hand, gently press down on your right knee to deepen the stretch.
Hold the stretch for 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Switch sides and repeat.

exercises.name: sled 45 degrees one leg press
exercises.description: A one-leg press on a sled machine set at a 45 degree angle. It trains the glutes, quads and hamstrings one side at a time.
steps: Adjust the sled machine to a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the sled machine with your back against the pad and your feet on the footplate.
Place one foot on the footplate and extend your leg, pushing the sled away from you.
Slowly bend your knee and lower the sled back to the starting position.
Repeat with the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith seated wrist curl
exercises.description: Sit in front of a smith machine and curl the bar with your wrists. It strengthens the forearms and builds grip.
steps: Sit on a bench in front of a Smith machine with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang off.
Slowly curl your wrists upward, bringing the barbell towards your forearms.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: straight leg outer hip abductor
exercises.description: Lie on your side with your legs straight and lift the top leg. It works the outer hip and glute muscles that stabilise your pelvis.
steps: Lie on your side with your legs straight and stacked on top of each other.
Place your bottom arm under your head for support.
Engage your core and lift your top leg as high as possible without rotating your hips or leaning backward.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your leg back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exercises.name: wrist circles
exercises.description: Hold your arms out and move your wrists in slow circles. It warms up the wrist joints and forearm muscles.
steps: Extend your arms straight out in front of you.
Make a fist with both hands.
Rotate your wrists in a circular motion, keeping your arms still.
Continue the wrist circles for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: wide grip pull-up
exercises.description: A pull-up on a wide overhand grip, pulling your chin above the bar. It targets the lats and upper back.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you and your hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Pull your body up towards the bar until your chin is above the bar.
Lower your body back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: chest dip (on dip-pull-up cage)
exercises.description: A chest dip done on a dip station with a forward lean. It works the lower chest, triceps and front shoulders.
steps: Adjust the dip bars to a height that allows you to comfortably grip them.
Stand between the bars and place your hands on each bar, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Jump up and straighten your arms, supporting your body weight on the bars.
Bend your knees and cross your ankles behind you.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping your chest up and your shoulders down.
Continue lowering until your shoulders are below your elbows or until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Push through your palms and extend your elbows to raise your body back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: assisted standing chin-up
exercises.description: A chin-up done on an assisted machine that takes part of your body weight. It builds the lats and biceps while you work up to full chin-ups.
steps: Adjust the machine to your desired assistance level.
Stand on the foot platform and grip the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your chest up and shoulders back, engage your core, and slightly bend your knees.
Pull your body up by flexing your elbows and driving your elbows down towards your sides.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: assisted standing pull-up
exercises.description: A pull-up done on an assisted machine that takes part of your body weight. It builds the lats and upper back while you work up to full pull-ups.
steps: Adjust the machine to your desired weight and height settings.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your lats and biceps, and pull yourself up towards the handles.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your back muscles.
Slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith front squat (clean grip)
exercises.description: A front squat on a smith machine with a clean grip. The bar path is guided so you can focus on the quads and glutes.
steps: Set up the smith machine with the barbell at shoulder height.
Stand facing the barbell with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step back and position the barbell on your front shoulders, resting it on your collarbone and deltoids.
Keep your chest up, back straight, and core engaged.
Lower your body by bending at the knees and hips, as if sitting back into a chair.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith low bar squat
exercises.description: A low bar squat on the smith machine, with the bar sitting lower on the back. It builds the glutes, quads and hamstrings along a fixed bar path.
steps: Set up the smith machine with the barbell at a height that allows you to comfortably rest it on your upper back.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned outwards.
Step under the bar and position it across your upper back, resting it on your traps.
Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar by straightening your legs and stepping back from the rack.
Take a deep breath and brace your core.
Initiate the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Lower your body until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Keep your chest up and your back straight throughout the movement.
Drive through your heels to stand back up, extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell low bar squat
exercises.description: A squat with the bar resting low across the rear delts, which leans you forward a bit more. It loads the glutes, hamstrings and lower back heavily.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and the barbell resting on your upper back.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, slowly lower your body by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell high bar squat
exercises.description: The classic back squat with the bar sitting high on the traps and a more upright torso. It is a staple for quad and glute strength.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Place the barbell on your upper back, resting it on your traps.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to squat down, pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Drive through your heels to stand back up, extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell finger curls
exercises.description: Small dumbbell curls where the bar rolls down to your fingertips and back up. A simple way to build finger and forearm grip strength.
steps: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip, resting your forearm on your thigh, palm facing up.
Allow the dumbbell to roll down to your fingertips, then curl it back up by flexing your fingers.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other hand.

exercises.name: kettlebell seated two arm military press
exercises.description: A seated overhead press with a kettlebell in each hand. It trains the shoulders and triceps while the seat keeps your legs out of the lift.
steps: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder level with your palms facing forward.
Press the kettlebells overhead by extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the kettlebells back to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever gripless shrug v. 2
exercises.description: A shrug on a lever machine without handles to grip, so the lift comes from the traps alone. Version 2 of the machine drawing.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the pad.
Grasp the handles or bars with an overhand grip, keeping your arms straight.
Keeping your back straight, lift your shoulders up towards your ears as high as possible.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: plank arm lifts
exercises.description: A plank where you lift one arm at a time, training core stability and anti-rotation strength.
steps: Get into a forearm or high plank with your body in a straight line.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
Lift one arm forward without letting your hips rotate.
Place it back down with control and lift the other.
Keep your neck neutral and alternate arms for the planned reps.

exercises.name: dumbbell over bench one arm reverse wrist curl
exercises.description: A one-arm reverse wrist curl with your forearm resting over a bench. It strengthens the wrist extensors on the top of the forearm.
steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down.
Rest your forearm on the bench with your wrist hanging off the edge.
Slowly curl your wrist upwards, bringing the dumbbell towards your forearm.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: dip hold
exercises.description: Holding the top of a dip on parallel bars. It builds the triceps and shoulder stability.
steps: Grip the parallel bars and press yourself up with straight arms.
Lean slightly forward and lock your shoulders down.
Hold the position with your body still.
Keep your elbows near your sides.
Hold for 15-30 seconds and step down.

exercises.name: dumbbell lying pronated grip maltese hold
exercises.description: Holding dumbbells out to the sides in a lying Maltese position. It is an advanced hold for the shoulders and chest.
steps: Lie face up with a dumbbell in each hand, palms down.
Lift your arms out to the sides at about hip level.
Keep your arms straight and your body tight.
Hold the position without letting the weights drop.
Hold for 10-20 seconds, then lower carefully.

exercises.name: dumbbell bent arm pullover hold
exercises.description: Holding a dumbbell over your chest with bent arms in a pullover position. It keeps the chest and lats under tension.
steps: Lie on a bench holding a dumbbell with both hands over your chest.
Lower it behind your head with your elbows bent.
Stop where you feel a stretch in your chest and lats.
Hold the position with your core tight.
Hold for 15-30 seconds, then lift it back up.

exercises.name: dumbbell rdl stretch
exercises.description: Holding the bottom of a Romanian deadlift with dumbbells. It loads the hamstrings in their stretched position.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Push your hips back and lower the dumbbells along your legs.
Stop when you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Hold the position with a flat back.
Hold for 15-30 seconds, then stand up.

exercises.name: barbell zercher squat hold
exercises.description: Holding the bottom of a Zercher squat with the bar in your elbows. It challenges the legs and core.
steps: Place the barbell in the crooks of your elbows.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel.
Keep your chest up and your core tight.
Hold the bottom position steadily.
Hold for 10-20 seconds, then stand up.

exercises.name: lever calf stretch (plate loaded)
exercises.description: A calf stretch on a plate-loaded lever machine, using the platform to push the heel down and lengthen the lower leg.
steps: Set up on the machine and place the ball of one foot on the platform with the heel free.
Keep your knee straight and stand tall.
Let the heel sink down until you feel a stretch in the calf.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing steadily, then release slowly.
Switch legs and repeat.

exercises.name: barbell pullover hold
exercises.description: Hold a barbell overhead behind you while lying on a bench. It builds lat and chest control in the stretched position.
steps: Lie on a bench holding a light barbell above your chest with arms nearly straight.
Lower the bar back over your head until you feel a deep stretch in your lats.
Brace your core and keep your ribs down and your elbows softly bent.
Hold the position for 15-30 seconds without letting the bar drift.
Return the bar over your chest with control and set it down safely.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline 30 degrees flye hold
exercises.description: A static hold at the bottom of an incline flye. It teaches chest tension and builds control in the stretched position.
steps: Set a bench to about 30 degrees and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand above your chest.
Open your arms wide with soft elbows until the dumbbells are level with your chest.
Keep your shoulder blades pinned back and down.
Hold the stretched position for 15-30 seconds without sagging.
Bring the weights back together over your chest and set them down carefully.

exercises.name: dumbbell flat flye hold
exercises.description: A static hold at the bottom of a flat flye. It builds chest tension and control in the stretched position.
steps: Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand above your chest.
Open your arms wide with soft elbows until the dumbbells are level with your chest.
Keep your shoulder blades pinned back and your feet planted.
Hold the position for 15-30 seconds without letting the weights drop.
Bring the dumbbells back together over your chest and set them down carefully.

exercises.name: lever seated dip
exercises.description: A seated dip on a lever machine that mimics the dip motion with guided support. It targets the triceps and also works the chest and front delts.
steps: Adjust the seat height so that your feet are flat on the ground and your knees are at a 90-degree angle.
Grasp the handles of the leverage machine with your palms facing down and your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever seated crunch
exercises.description: A seated machine crunch where you curl your torso toward your hips against resistance. It trains the abs with a controlled, fixed path.
steps: Sit on the leverage machine with your back against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles or place your hands on the side pads for support.
Engage your abs and slowly lean back, allowing the pad to move with you.
Once your upper body is at a 45-degree angle, contract your abs and crunch forward, bringing your chest towards your knees.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever seated twist
exercises.description: A seated machine twist that trains the trunk rotators and abs against a controlled load.
steps: Sit on the machine, adjust the pads and place your arms or hands as designed.
Sit tall with your hips facing forward.
Rotate your torso to one side with a smooth, controlled turn.
Pause briefly, then return to the centre without letting the weight stack slam.
Repeat to the other side and keep alternating.

exercises.name: lever seated shoulder press
exercises.description: A machine overhead press that builds the shoulders and triceps with a fixed, stable path.
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles start near shoulder height and sit with your back on the pad.
Grip the handles and brace your core.
Press the handles overhead until your arms are nearly straight.
Pause briefly at the top without shrugging.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height and repeat.

exercises.name: lever chest press v. 2
exercises.description: A machine chest press with a lever arm that guides the push. It builds the chest and triceps.
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Sit back with your shoulder blades against the pad and feet flat.
Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Pause, then return slowly until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Keep your wrists straight and your back on the pad throughout.

exercises.name: barbell standing close grip military press
exercises.description: A standing barbell overhead press with a narrow grip. It hits the front delts and triceps and asks your core to keep you steady.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly closer than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell to shoulder height, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Press the barbell overhead, extending your arms fully.
Lower the barbell back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell standing wide military press
exercises.description: A standing barbell overhead press with a wide grip, which shifts more work to the shoulders. Keep your ribs down and your core tight.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lift the barbell to shoulder height, keeping your elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Press the barbell overhead, extending your arms fully.
Lower the barbell back to shoulder height and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: ez barbell seated curls
exercises.description: Seated curls with an EZ bar, which is gentler on the wrists. A good way to build the biceps without swinging your body.
steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Rest your upper arms on your thighs, allowing the ez barbell to hang down in front of you.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the ez barbell upwards towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the ez barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell romanian deadlift
exercises.description: A hip hinge with dumbbells that lowers them down the legs while your back stays flat. It trains the hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, hinge at the hips and lower the dumbbells towards the ground, allowing your knees to bend slightly.
Lower the dumbbells until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, then push through your heels and engage your glutes to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: walking lunge
exercises.description: Stepping forward into one lunge after another, moving across the room. It works the quads and glutes and challenges balance.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Take a step forward with your right leg, lowering your body into a lunge position.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee aligned with your ankle.
Push off with your right foot and bring your left foot forward, stepping into a lunge position with your left leg.
Continue alternating legs and walking forward, maintaining a controlled and steady pace.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell full squat (back pov)
exercises.description: A full-depth barbell squat shown from behind. It builds the quads, glutes and core and is a great check of back and knee alignment.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Hold the barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps or rear delts.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to lower your body down.
Bend at the knees and hips, pushing your hips back and down as if sitting into a chair.
Lower your body until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Keep your knees in line with your toes and your weight in your heels.
Drive through your heels to stand back up, extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell full squat (side pov)
exercises.description: A full-depth barbell squat shown from the side. It builds the quads, glutes and core and shows your depth and back angle clearly.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Hold the barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps or rear delts.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to lower your body down.
Bend at the knees and hips, pushing your hips back and down as if sitting into a chair.
Lower your body until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Keep your knees in line with your toes and your weight in your heels.
Drive through your heels to stand back up, extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: sled 45° leg press (side pov)
exercises.description: A leg press on a 45 degree sled, shown from the side. It loads the quads and glutes with your back supported.
steps: Adjust the seat of the sled machine so that your knees are at a 90-degree angle when your feet are on the footplate.
Sit on the sled machine with your back flat against the backrest and your feet shoulder-width apart on the footplate.
Grip the handles on the sides of the seat for stability.
Push against the footplate to extend your legs, straightening them completely.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly bend your knees to lower the footplate back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: sled 45° leg press (back pov)
exercises.description: A leg press on a 45 degree sled, shown from behind. It loads the quads and glutes with your back supported.
steps: Adjust the seat of the sled machine so that your knees are at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the sled machine with your back against the backrest and your feet shoulder-width apart on the footplate.
Grip the handles on the sides of the seat for stability.
Push the footplate away from your body by extending your legs, keeping your heels on the footplate.
Pause for a moment at the fully extended position.
Slowly bend your knees and lower the footplate back towards your body, controlling the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: 45 degree hyperextension (arms in front of chest) (side pov)
exercises.description: A back extension on a 45 degree bench viewed from the side, targeting the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Set the pad at hip height and hook your heels under the roller.
Cross your arms over your chest and keep your body straight.
Lower your torso with a flat back until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Raise back up until your body is in line, without overarching.
Move slowly and squeeze your glutes at the top.

exercises.name: twist hip lift
exercises.description: Lying on your back, you lift your hips and add a gentle twist. It wakes up the glutes and obliques.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands by your sides for support.
Engage your glutes and lift your hips off the ground, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
While keeping your hips lifted, twist your lower body to the right side, bringing your knees towards the ground.
Return to the starting position and repeat the twist to the left side.
Continue alternating twists for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: push-up on lower arms
exercises.description: A push-up with your forearms on the floor instead of your hands. It is tough on the triceps and the core.
steps: Start in a plank position with your forearms on the ground and elbows directly below your shoulders.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to toe.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: crab twist toe touch
exercises.description: From a crab position you twist and reach one hand to the opposite foot. It works the abs and obliques and gets the shoulders moving.
steps: Start by sitting on the ground with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands behind you, fingers pointing towards your feet, and lift your hips off the ground.
Extend one leg straight out in front of you while simultaneously reaching your opposite hand towards your toes.
Return to the starting position and repeat on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lateral side plank (bent leg)
exercises.description: An easier side plank with the bottom knee bent, building oblique and hip stability.
steps: Lie on your side with your forearm under your shoulder and your knees bent.
Stack your hips and shoulders in a line.
Lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from knee to head.
Keep your core tight and your hips from sagging.
Hold for the planned time, then switch sides.

exercises.name: lateral side plank
exercises.description: A classic side plank that trains the obliques and hip stabilisers.
steps: Lie on your side with your forearm under your shoulder and your legs straight.
Stack your feet or stagger them for balance.
Lift your hips to form a straight line from head to feet.
Keep your core tight and your hips from sagging.
Hold for the planned time, then switch sides.

exercises.name: inchworm
exercises.description: You walk your hands out from standing into a plank and walk them back. It warms up the hamstrings, shoulders and core in one go.
steps: Start in a standing position with your feet hip-width apart.
Bend forward at the waist and place your hands on the ground in front of you.
Walk your hands forward until you are in a high plank position, with your body in a straight line from head to toe.
Pause for a moment, then walk your hands back towards your feet, keeping your legs as straight as possible.
Once your hands reach your feet, stand back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: forward jump
exercises.description: A bodyweight jump forward with a soft landing. It builds explosive power in the quads and glutes.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and lower your body into a squat position.
Swing your arms back for momentum.
Jump forward explosively, extending your hips, knees, and ankles.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and immediately go into the next jump.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: backward jump
exercises.description: A bodyweight jump backward with a soft landing. It builds explosive power in the quads and trains control.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and jump backwards, pushing off with both feet.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, bending your knees to absorb the impact.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: one leg squat
exercises.description: A squat on a single leg that challenges strength and balance. It targets the glutes and quads on one side at a time.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend one leg forward, keeping it off the ground.
Bend your standing leg and lower your body down as if sitting back into a chair.
Keep your chest up and your back straight.
Push through your heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat with the other leg.

exercises.name: jack plank
exercises.description: A plank where your feet jump in and out like a jumping jack, combining core stability with cardio.
steps: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your hips level.
Jump your feet apart, then jump them back together.
Keep your upper body steady and your hips from rising.
Continue at a steady pace for the planned time.

exercises.name: lever incline chest press v. 2
exercises.description: A lever machine chest press with an inclined path, version 2. It builds the upper chest, front delts and triceps.
steps: Adjust the seat height and backrest angle on the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Push the handles forward and away from your body until your arms are fully extended, but without locking your elbows.
Pause for a moment at the fully extended position, then slowly bend your elbows and lower the handles back towards your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: biceps stretch behind the back
exercises.description: A stretch that opens the front of the arm and chest by reaching the arms behind you.
steps: Stand tall and reach both arms behind your back.
Straighten your elbows and turn your palms down or clasp your hands.
Lift your hands slightly away from your body until you feel a stretch in the biceps.
Keep your chest open and your neck relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing steadily, then release slowly.

exercises.name: bow yoga pose
exercises.description: A yoga backbend where you lie on your belly and hold your ankles. It stretches the thighs, chest and front of the hips.
steps: Lie on your stomach with your arms along your sides.
Bend your knees and reach back to hold your ankles.
Lift your chest and kick your feet gently into your hands to raise your thighs.
Keep your gaze forward and breathe steadily.
Hold for 15-30 seconds, then release slowly and rest on the mat.

exercises.name: cobra yoga pose
exercises.description: A gentle yoga backbend that opens the chest and stretches the front of the abs while strengthening the back.
steps: Lie on your stomach with your palms under your shoulders and legs extended.
Press the tops of your feet into the floor.
Lift your chest by straightening your arms partway, keeping your hips down.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears and your neck long.
Hold for 15-30 seconds, then lower slowly.

exercises.name: full lotus yoga pose
exercises.description: A seated yoga posture with both feet resting on opposite thighs. It opens the hips and needs good flexibility.
steps: Sit tall on the floor with your legs extended.
Bring one foot onto the opposite thigh, then the other foot on top of the other thigh.
Only go as far as your hips allow, and never force your knees.
Rest your hands on your knees and lengthen your spine.
Hold for 20-30 seconds with calm breathing, then switch the leg order next time.

exercises.name: locust yoga pose (iron man pose)
exercises.description: A yoga pose on your belly where you lift legs and chest at once. It strengthens the lower back and glutes.
steps: Lie face down with your arms along your sides and palms facing up.
Press your pelvis into the floor and engage your glutes.
Lift your chest, arms and legs off the floor together.
Look slightly forward and keep your neck long.
Hold for 10-20 seconds, then lower slowly and rest.

exercises.name: plow yoga pose
exercises.description: An inverted yoga pose where the legs are lowered behind the head. It stretches the spine, shoulders and hamstrings.
steps: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides.
Lift your legs and hips up and over, supporting your lower back with your hands if needed.
Lower your toes toward the floor behind your head.
Keep your neck relaxed and do not turn your head.
Hold for 15-30 seconds, then roll down slowly one vertebra at a time.

exercises.name: push up (with push up handles)
exercises.description: A push-up on handles that lets you go a little deeper and keeps the wrists neutral. It trains the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Place the handles shoulder-width apart and grip them in a plank position.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest until it is between the handles, elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
