Keep your core tight and your hips from sagging.

exercises.name: shoulder stand yoga pose
exercises.description: An inverted yoga pose balanced on the shoulders. It builds shoulder and core control and stretches the neck-side muscles.
steps: Lie on your back and lift your legs overhead, supporting your lower back with your hands.
Walk your hands up toward your shoulder blades.
Raise your legs straight up so your body forms a line over your shoulders.
Keep your neck long and still, and do not turn your head.
Hold for 15-30 seconds, then lower slowly.

exercises.name: shoulder stretch behind the back
exercises.description: A simple stretch that opens the front of the shoulders and chest by clasping the hands behind you.
steps: Stand tall and clasp your hands behind your back.
Straighten your arms and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lift your hands gently away from your body until you feel a stretch.
Keep your chest open and avoid arching your lower back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing steadily, then release slowly.

exercises.name: sissy squat
exercises.description: A squat where your knees travel far forward as you lean back. It isolates the quads with only your body weight.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing slightly outward.
Hold onto a stable object for balance if needed.
Slowly lower your body by bending your knees and leaning back, keeping your torso upright.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as far as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: standing calf raise (on a staircase)
exercises.description: A calf raise with your heels hanging off a stair step for extra range. It trains the calves through a deep stretch.
steps: Stand on the edge of a step or a sturdy platform with your heels hanging off and your toes on the step.
Hold onto a railing or wall for balance if needed.
Slowly raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: supine spinal twist yoga pose
exercises.description: A relaxing lying twist that mobilises the spine and stretches the hips and sides of the trunk.
steps: Lie on your back with your arms out to the sides.
Pull one knee toward your chest.
Guide that knee across your body toward the floor on the opposite side.
Keep both shoulders on the floor and turn your head the other way if comfortable.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: triceps dip stretch
exercises.description: A stretch for the back of the upper arm, taken with the elbow bent overhead.
steps: Stand or sit tall and raise one arm overhead.
Bend the elbow so your hand drops behind your head.
Use your other hand to gently press the elbow back and down.
Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch arms.

exercises.name: wheel pose yoga pose
exercises.description: A deep yoga backbend with hands and feet on the floor and the body arched upward. It opens the chest and strengthens the back.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat near your hips.
Place your palms beside your head with fingers pointing toward your shoulders.
Press through your hands and feet to lift your hips and then your head.
Straighten your arms as far as comfortable and keep your thighs parallel.
Hold for 5-15 seconds, then lower slowly with your chin tucked.

exercises.name: butterfly yoga pose
exercises.description: A seated pose with the soles of your feet together and knees dropped out. It opens the inner thighs and hips.
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you.
Bend your knees and bring the soles of your feet together, allowing your knees to fall out to the sides.
Hold onto your ankles or feet with your hands.
Sit up tall and lengthen your spine.
Gently press your knees down towards the floor, feeling a stretch in your inner thighs.
Hold this position for a few breaths.
To release, slowly bring your knees back up and extend your legs.

exercises.name: oblique crunch v. 2
exercises.description: An oblique crunch where you curl up and to the side, version 2. It trains the side abs.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands behind your head or cross them over your chest.
Engage your abs and lift your shoulder blades off the ground, rotating your torso to one side.
Pause for a moment, then lower your shoulder blades back down to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: sledge hammer
exercises.description: Swinging a sledgehammer down onto a tire in a controlled arc. It trains the abs and obliques and also the shoulders and grip.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the sledge hammer with both hands.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Swing the sledge hammer down towards the ground, using your core and upper body strength.
As you swing down, pivot your hips and transfer the force to the hammer.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell reverse band bench press
exercises.description: A bench press with bands that lighten the load at the bottom and add heavier tension near the top. It builds pressing strength.
steps: Set up on a bench with bands anchored to the rack and attached to the bar.
Lie back with your eyes under the bar and your shoulder blades pinched.
Lower the bar to your mid chest with control.
Press the bar back up to straight arms, feeling the band resistance change.
Keep your feet planted and your wrists stacked over your elbows.

exercises.name: band decline sit up
exercises.description: A decline sit-up with a band adding resistance. It trains the abs through a long range.
steps: Anchor a band behind you and hold the other end at your chest.
Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured.
Curl your torso up toward your knees, keeping tension on the band.
Pause at the top without pulling on your neck.
Lower back down slowly under control.

exercises.name: band behind neck shoulder press
exercises.description: A band-resisted overhead press from behind the neck. It trains the shoulders and triceps with rising tension.
steps: Stand on the band and hold the ends at the back of your shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your head forward.
Press your hands straight up until your arms are extended.
Lower slowly back behind your head to shoulder level.
Only use this variation if your shoulders move comfortably in that position.

exercises.name: band upright row (under two feet)
exercises.description: An upright row where the band is held under both feet. It builds the shoulders and upper traps.
steps: Stand with both feet on the middle of the band and hold the ends in front of your thighs.
Keep your chest up and your core tight.
Pull your hands up along your body until they reach chest height, elbows leading.
Pause briefly without shrugging too high.
Lower slowly back down.

exercises.name: band side plank row with partner
exercises.description: A side plank with a rowing motion against a band held by a partner. It trains the lats and trunk stability.
steps: Get into a side plank on one forearm, with a partner holding the band in front of you.
Grip the band with your top hand and keep your hips lifted.
Row your hand back toward your ribs, squeezing the shoulder blade.
Return slowly without letting your hips drop.
Finish your reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: band pushdown
exercises.description: A band version of the triceps pushdown that isolates the back of the arm.
steps: Anchor the band high and hold the ends with your elbows at your sides.
Stand tall with a slight forward lean.
Push your hands down until your arms are straight.
Pause and squeeze your triceps.
Return slowly while keeping your elbows pinned to your sides.

exercises.name: band pull apart
exercises.description: A simple band move pulling the arms apart in front of you. It strengthens the upper back and rear shoulders and helps posture.
steps: Hold a band in front of you at shoulder height with your arms straight.
Keep your ribs down and your shoulders away from your ears.
Pull the band apart by moving your hands out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Return slowly with control.

exercises.name: band skull crusher
exercises.description: A lying triceps extension using a band for resistance. It isolates the back of the upper arm.
steps: Anchor the band behind your head and lie on your back holding the ends.
Start with your arms straight above your chest.
Bend only your elbows to lower your hands toward your forehead.
Extend your arms back up against the band.
Keep your upper arms still throughout.

exercises.name: band calf raise v. 3
exercises.description: A calf raise using a band for resistance. It builds calf strength and ankle control.
steps: Secure the band under your feet or around your shoulders as set up.
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause and squeeze your calves.
Lower slowly until your heels are back on the floor.

exercises.name: band ez barbell close grip curl
exercises.description: A close-grip curl on an EZ bar with a band adding tension near the top. It targets the biceps.
steps: Stand on the band and hold the EZ bar with a close grip, palms up.
Keep your elbows at your sides and your chest tall.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top without swinging.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.

exercises.name: band hip flexion
exercises.description: A standing hip flexion with a band around the foot or leg. It trains the hip flexors and quads.
steps: Attach a band to a low anchor and loop it around one ankle.
Stand tall and hold a support for balance.
Lift the knee forward and up toward hip height.
Pause briefly, then lower with control.
Finish your reps and switch legs.

exercises.name: band lateral raise v. 2
exercises.description: A band lateral raise that builds the sides of the shoulders.
steps: Stand on the band and hold the ends at your sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Pause briefly without shrugging.
Lower slowly back to your sides.

exercises.name: barbell bench squat (with chains)
exercises.description: A barbell squat to a bench with chains adding load as you stand. It builds leg and hip strength and teaches consistent depth.
steps: Set a bench behind you and load the bar with chains.
Place the bar on your upper back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Sit back and down until you touch the bench lightly.
Keep your chest up and your knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your feet to stand, feeling the chains add weight.

exercises.name: crossover reverse lunge
exercises.description: A reverse lunge where the back leg steps behind and across the line of the front leg. It trains glutes, thighs and balance.
steps: Stand tall with your hands on your hips.
Step one foot back and across behind your other leg.
Lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee stable.
Push through the front foot to stand, then repeat or switch sides.

exercises.name: hamstring stretch
exercises.description: A stretch for the back of the thigh. You reach toward your toes with a long spine and feel the hamstrings lengthen.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step forward with your right foot and shift your weight onto your right leg.
Keeping your back straight, slowly bend forward at the hips, reaching towards your right foot with both hands.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: all fours squad stretch
exercises.description: On all fours you pull one foot toward your glutes to stretch the front of the thigh. It eases tight quads.
steps: Start on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips.
Extend one leg straight back, keeping your knee bent and your foot flexed.
Slowly lower your hips towards the ground, feeling a stretch in your quads.
Hold this position for 20-30 seconds.
Switch legs and repeat the stretch on the other side.

exercises.name: band good morning
exercises.description: A hip hinge with a band across your shoulders. It strengthens the hamstrings, glutes and lower back.
steps: Stand on the band and loop it behind your neck across your shoulders.
Keep your knees softly bent and your back flat.
Push your hips back and lean your torso forward.
Stop when you feel a stretch in the hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall again.

exercises.name: barbell quarter squat
exercises.description: A short-range squat that goes only a quarter of the way down. It lets you handle heavier loads and builds leg strength.
steps: Rest the bar on your upper back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Bend your knees and hips a short way, about a quarter of the full depth.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
Drive up through your feet to stand tall.

exercises.name: barbell clean deadlift
exercises.description: A deadlift performed with a clean-style setup and path. It trains the pulling position used in the clean.
steps: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot and grip just outside your knees.
Set a flat back, chest up and shoulders over the bar.
Push the floor away to lift the bar, keeping it close to your legs.
Stand tall with hips and knees fully extended.
Lower the bar back down with control along the same path.

exercises.name: barbell clean from blocks
exercises.description: A clean started from blocks at about knee height. It trains the explosive pull and the catch without the first pull from the floor.
steps: Set the bar on blocks and grip it just outside your knees with a flat back.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it on your front shoulders in a full squat.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell clean pull
exercises.description: The explosive pull of a clean, finished with a shrug and without the catch. It builds power and bar speed.
steps: Set up over the bar with a flat back and a grip just outside your knees.
Lift the bar past your knees, keeping it close.
Extend your hips and knees explosively and shrug.
Let your elbows rise high, but do not catch the bar.
Lower the bar with control and reset.

exercises.name: barbell decline bench lunge
exercises.description: A split squat with the back foot on a decline bench and a barbell on your back. It builds single-leg strength.
steps: Place the bar on your upper back and rest one foot behind you on a decline bench.
Step the front foot out to set a stable stance.
Lower your back knee toward the floor, torso upright.
Drive through the front foot to rise.
Finish your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: smith good morning off pins
exercises.description: A good morning on the Smith machine starting from the pins. It builds the hamstrings, glutes and lower back.
steps: Set the bar on the pins at upper-chest height and duck under it.
Stand tall with the bar on your upper back and knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back, keeping your back flat.
Stop when your torso is near parallel with the floor.
Drive your hips forward to stand, then return the bar to the pins when done.

exercises.name: barbell hang clean
exercises.description: A clean that starts from the hang at the thighs. It trains the explosive hip drive and the catch.
steps: Stand holding the bar at mid-thigh with a grip just outside your legs and a flat back.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it on your front shoulders in a squat.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell hang clean below the knees
exercises.description: A hang clean started from below the knees. It lengthens the pull for more power.
steps: Hold the bar just below your knees with a flat back and your shoulders over the bar.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it on your front shoulders in a squat.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell hang snatch
exercises.description: A snatch that starts from the hang at the thighs. It trains the explosive pull and catching the bar overhead.
steps: Hold the bar at mid-thigh with a wide snatch grip and a flat back.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull under the bar and catch it overhead with locked arms in a squat.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell hang snatch below the knees
exercises.description: A hang snatch started from below the knees. It lengthens the pull for more power.
steps: Hold the bar just below your knees with a wide grip and a flat back.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull under the bar and catch it overhead with locked arms in a squat.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell heaving snatch balance
exercises.description: A snatch drill where you dip, drive and drop under a bar on your back into an overhead squat. It builds speed and overhead stability.
steps: Rest the bar on your upper back and take a wide snatch grip.
Dip and drive up explosively, pushing the bar off your shoulders.
Drop quickly into a squat while pressing the bar overhead.
Catch it with locked arms over your mid-foot.
Stand up with control and return the bar to your back.

exercises.name: barbell jerk dip squat
exercises.description: The dip and drive part of the jerk, practised with a barbell on the shoulders. It trains a vertical dip and strong leg drive.
steps: Rack the bar on your front shoulders and stand with feet hip-width apart.
Keep your torso upright and your core tight.
Dip a short way by bending your knees straight down.
Drive up explosively through your whole foot.
Settle back to standing and reset.

exercises.name: barbell muscle snatch
exercises.description: A snatch lifted overhead with straight arms and no re-bend of the knees. It trains the upper pull and arm turnover.
steps: Hold the bar at the hips with a wide grip, shoulders over the bar.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull the bar up high with your elbows, turn it over and press to locked arms overhead without squatting.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell olympic squat
exercises.description: A deep, upright high-bar squat in the weightlifting style. It builds leg strength and mobility.
steps: Place the bar high on your upper back and set your feet about shoulder-width.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Sit straight down as deep as you can with heels flat.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
Drive up through your feet to stand tall.

exercises.name: barbell power clean from blocks
exercises.description: A clean caught above parallel, started from blocks. It builds explosive power.
steps: Set the bar on blocks and grip it just outside your knees with a flat back.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull and catch the bar on your front shoulders in a quarter squat.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell power jerk
exercises.description: An explosive overhead lift where you dip, drive and catch the bar with locked arms in a quarter squat.
steps: Rack the bar on your front shoulders with elbows slightly forward.
Dip a short way with your torso upright.
Drive up explosively and punch the bar overhead.
Dip under slightly and catch it with locked arms.
Stand tall, then lower the bar to your shoulders with control.

exercises.name: barbell power snatch
exercises.description: A snatch caught overhead above parallel. It builds explosive power and speed.
steps: Hold the bar at your shins with a wide grip, flat back and chest up.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull under and catch the bar overhead with locked arms in a quarter squat.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell power snatch from blocks
exercises.description: A power snatch started from blocks. It trains the explosive pull and the overhead catch.
steps: Set the bar on blocks and take a wide grip with a flat back.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull under and catch the bar overhead with locked arms in a quarter squat.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell romanian deadlift from deficit
exercises.description: A Romanian deadlift standing on a small platform for extra range. It builds the hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Stand on a low platform holding the bar at your thighs.
Keep your knees soft and your back flat.
Push your hips back and slide the bar down your legs.
Lower as far as you can with a flat back.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.

exercises.name: barbell snatch
exercises.description: The full snatch, lifting the bar from the floor to overhead in one motion and catching it in a deep squat.
steps: Grip the bar wide, with it over your mid-foot, flat back and chest up.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull under the bar and catch it overhead in a full squat, then stand up.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell snatch balance
exercises.description: A drill where you drop under a bar on your back into an overhead squat. It builds overhead stability and speed.
steps: Rest the bar on your upper back and take a wide snatch grip.
Dip a short way and drive up.
Drop into a squat while pressing the bar overhead.
Catch it with locked arms and your chest up.
Stand up with control and return the bar to your back.

exercises.name: barbell snatch deadlift
exercises.description: A deadlift with a wide snatch grip. It strengthens the pulling position used in the snatch.
steps: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot and take a wide snatch grip.
Set your back flat and chest up.
Push the floor away to lift the bar, keeping it close.
Stand tall with your hips and knees extended.
Lower the bar with control along the same path.

exercises.name: barbell snatch from blocks
exercises.description: A snatch started from blocks. It trains the pull and the deep overhead catch.
steps: Set the bar on blocks and take a wide grip with a flat back.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Pull under the bar and catch it overhead in a full squat, then stand up.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell split clean
exercises.description: A clean caught in a split stance instead of a squat. It trains the explosive pull and the catch.
steps: Grip the bar just outside your legs with a flat back, shoulders over the bar.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your body.
Extend your hips and knees powerfully and shrug your shoulders.
Split your feet front and back and catch the bar on your front shoulders.
Stand tall to finish, then lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell split jerk
exercises.description: An overhead lift where you dip, drive and catch the bar with locked arms in a split stance.
steps: Rack the bar on your front shoulders with elbows slightly forward.
Dip a short way with your torso upright.
Drive up explosively and press the bar overhead.
Split your feet front and back and catch with locked arms.
Bring your feet back together and lower the bar with control.

exercises.name: barbell split jump
exercises.description: A jump with a barbell on the back where you switch the front and back leg in the air. It builds leg power.
steps: Rest a light bar on your upper back and take a split stance.
Lower into a shallow lunge.
Jump explosively and switch your legs in the air.
Land softly in the opposite split stance.
Keep your torso upright and continue alternating.

exercises.name: barbell squat to shoulder press
exercises.description: A squat that flows straight into an overhead press. It trains legs and shoulders together in one fluid rep.
steps: Hold the barbell at your upper chest with your elbows slightly forward and feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up.
Drive up through your heels and use that momentum to press the bar overhead.
Lock out the press with the bar over your mid-foot, then lower it back to your chest.
Keep your core braced the whole time and avoid arching your lower back.

exercises.name: barbell squat to upright row (thighs)
exercises.description: Squat down with the bar hanging in front of you, then stand and pull it up to chest height. Works thighs, glutes and upper back in one move.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Push your hips back and squat down, letting the bar slide down to your knees.
Drive up through your heels to stand tall.
As you rise, pull the bar up close to your body until your elbows reach shoulder height.
Lower the bar under control and go straight into the next squat.

exercises.name: barbell stiff leg deadlift on bench
exercises.description: A stiff-legged deadlift performed while standing on a bench, giving you extra range of motion. It stretches and strengthens the hamstrings and lower back.
steps: Stand on a sturdy bench holding a barbell at thigh level, feet hip-width apart.
Keep your knees almost straight and push your hips back.
Lower the bar toward your toes with a flat back as far as your hamstrings allow.
Pause briefly, then squeeze your glutes to stand back up.
Keep the bar close to your legs and stay in control throughout.

exercises.name: barbell stiff legged deadlift
exercises.description: The classic stiff-legged deadlift, hinging at the hips with nearly straight knees. A great builder for hamstrings, glutes and the lower back.
steps: Stand holding a barbell in front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and push your hips back.
Lower the bar along your legs until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Keep your back flat and your chest proud the whole way.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.

exercises.name: barbell wide stance stiff leg deadlift
exercises.description: A stiff-legged deadlift with a wide stance that brings in the inner thighs and glutes. It also keeps the hamstrings under a deep stretch.
steps: Take a wide stance, toes slightly out, with the barbell held in front of your thighs.
Keep your knees nearly straight and push your hips back.
Lower the bar between your legs while keeping your back flat.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings and inner thighs.
Squeeze your glutes to rise back to standing.

exercises.name: barbell full zercher squat
exercises.description: A squat with the bar held in the crooks of your elbows at full depth. It hits the quads, glutes and upper back.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.
Hold the barbell in the crooks of your elbows, with your hands gripping the barbell for stability.
Engage your core and keep your chest lifted as you lower your hips back and down into a squat position.
Keep your knees in line with your toes and your weight in your heels.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Drive through your heels to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: bodyweight wall squat
exercises.description: A squat with your back against a wall, which keeps your torso upright and takes pressure off the lower back. Good for building leg endurance.
steps: Lean your back against a wall with your feet about a step in front of you.
Slide down until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor.
Keep your knees in line with your toes and your back flat on the wall.
Press through your heels to slide back up.
Repeat for the planned number of reps.

exercises.name: cable standing leg curl
exercises.description: Standing on one leg, you curl the other against a low cable. It isolates the hamstrings one side at a time.
steps: Attach an ankle cuff to a low pulley and strap it around one ankle.
Stand facing the machine and hold on for balance, with the working leg slightly behind you.
Bend your knee and curl your heel toward your glutes.
Squeeze at the top without swinging your torso.
Lower slowly, finish your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: chair leg extended stretch
exercises.description: Using a chair for support, you extend one leg to stretch the thigh and hip. It loosens up the quads.
steps: Sit on the edge of a chair with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Extend one leg straight out in front of you, keeping your heel on the ground.
Lean forward slightly, feeling a stretch in your quadriceps.
Hold this position for 20-30 seconds.
Switch legs and repeat the stretch.

exercises.name: double leg butt kick
exercises.description: A bouncy jump where both heels flick up toward your glutes. It gets your heart rate up and warms up the hamstrings.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed.
Jump up off both feet.
Kick both heels up toward your glutes while you are in the air.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with slightly bent knees.
Go straight into the next jump at a steady rhythm.

exercises.name: dumbbell bench one leg squat
exercises.description: A single-leg squat with the other foot resting on a bench behind you, holding dumbbells. It hammers the quads and glutes and challenges balance.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand a step in front of a bench, facing away from it.
Rest the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Lower your back knee toward the floor by bending your front leg.
Keep your front knee over your toes and your chest up.
Push through your front heel to stand, then switch legs after your reps.

exercises.name: dumbbell decline bench lunge
exercises.description: A rear-foot-elevated lunge using a decline bench and dumbbells. The raised back foot shifts the load onto the front leg.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand facing away from a decline bench.
Place the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Lower your hips straight down until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee tracking over your toes.
Push through your front foot to rise, then switch legs after your reps.

exercises.name: dumbbell jumping squat
exercises.description: An explosive squat jump holding light dumbbells at your sides. It builds power in the legs and gets the heart pumping.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Explode upward and jump as high as you can.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and sink straight into the next squat.
Keep your chest up and your knees tracking your toes.

exercises.name: dumbbell lateral lunge with bicep curl
exercises.description: A side lunge combined with a biceps curl. It works the legs and arms together and also loosens the inner thighs.
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward.
Take a big step to the side and sit back into that hip, keeping the other leg straight.
Curl both dumbbells up as you lower into the lunge.
Push off your bent leg to return to the middle while lowering the weights.
Alternate sides or finish all reps on one side before switching.

exercises.name: dumbbell split jump
exercises.description: A jumping lunge where you switch legs in the air while holding dumbbells. It builds explosive leg power.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and step into a lunge position.
Lower until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Explode upward and swap your leg positions in the air.
Land softly in a lunge with the opposite leg forward.
Keep your torso upright and move fluidly from rep to rep.

exercises.name: dumbbell squat v. 2
exercises.description: A simple squat holding a dumbbell in each hand. It is a solid all-round leg builder that is easy to load.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower down.
Go until your thighs are parallel to the floor or a bit lower.
Keep your chest up and your heels planted.
Press through your feet to stand back up.

exercises.name: dumbbell stiff leg deadlift on bench
exercises.description: A stiff-legged deadlift with dumbbells while standing on a bench for extra depth. It targets the hamstrings and lower back.
steps: Stand on a sturdy bench holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Keep your knees nearly straight and push your hips back.
Lower the dumbbells down your legs and below the bench level with a flat back.
Pause when you feel a deep hamstring stretch.
Squeeze your glutes to return to standing.

exercises.name: dumbbell walking lunges
exercises.description: Lunges done on the move with dumbbells in your hands. A great move for leg strength, glutes and coordination.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and stand tall.
Step forward with one leg and lower until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee over your ankle.
Push off your back foot and step through into a lunge with the other leg.
Continue walking forward, alternating legs.

exercises.name: dumbbell wall squat
exercises.description: A wall squat made harder by holding dumbbells. It keeps your back supported while loading the legs.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lean your back against a wall.
Walk your feet forward so your knees stay over your ankles when you squat.
Slide down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Keep your back flat against the wall.
Press through your heels to slide back up.

exercises.name: exercise ball hip flexor stretch
exercises.description: You kneel with a stability ball for support and push the hips forward. It stretches the hip flexors at the front of the hip.
steps: Place the stability ball on the ground and kneel in front of it.
Place your right foot on top of the stability ball, with your knee bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend your left leg behind you, keeping it straight.
Lean forward, pushing your hips towards the stability ball, until you feel a stretch in your right hip flexor.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides and repeat.

exercises.name: exercise ball seated hamstring stretch
exercises.description: Seated on a stability ball with one leg extended, you lean forward to stretch the back of the thigh.
steps: Sit on the stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly roll the ball forward, walking your feet out until your upper back is resting on the ball and your legs are extended straight in front of you.
Place your hands on your hips for support.
Engage your core and slowly lower your upper body towards the ground, keeping your back straight and your chest lifted.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, and hold the position for 20-30 seconds.
Slowly return to the starting position by pushing through your heels and using your hamstrings to pull yourself back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: exercise ball seated quad stretch
exercises.description: A gentle quad stretch using a stability ball for support. It opens up the front of the thigh.
steps: Sit on the edge of a stability ball with your torso upright.
Hold on to something steady for balance if needed.
Bend one knee and bring your heel toward your glutes, holding your ankle.
Keep your knees close together and your hips square.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.

exercises.name: exercise ball wall squat
exercises.description: A squat with a stability ball between your back and the wall. The ball keeps the movement smooth and supports your back.
steps: Place a stability ball between your lower back and a wall.
Walk your feet forward about a step and stand shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and let the ball roll down your back as you squat.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Press through your heels to rise back up.

exercises.name: front back leg raises
exercises.description: A standing leg swing forward and backward, loosening the hips. A nice warm-up for the hips and hamstrings.
steps: Stand tall next to a wall or support and hold on with one hand.
Swing your outside leg forward with a straight knee.
Swing it back behind you, squeezing your glute.
Keep your torso upright and avoid arching your lower back.
Do all reps on one side, then turn around and switch legs.

exercises.name: intermediate hip flexor and quad stretch
exercises.description: A deeper stretch for the hip flexors and quads, using a rope or strap to pull the foot toward you.
steps: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold onto a stable object for support.
Bend your right knee and bring your right foot towards your glutes, grabbing the rope with your right hand.
Slowly pull your right foot towards your glutes, feeling a stretch in your right quad.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release the stretch and repeat on the left side.

exercises.name: kettlebell dead clean
exercises.description: A clean that starts from a dead stop on the floor each rep, with no swing. It builds explosive hip drive and pulling power.
steps: Stand over a kettlebell with feet hip-width apart and hinge down to grab the handle.
Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Drive your hips forward and pull the bell up close to your body.
Rotate your hand around the handle and catch the bell at your shoulder.
Lower it back to the floor under control and reset before the next rep.

exercises.name: kettlebell one arm overhead squat (thighs)
exercises.description: A squat while holding a kettlebell locked out overhead with one arm. It trains leg strength together with shoulder stability and core control.
steps: Press a kettlebell overhead with one arm and lock out your elbow.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and keep your ribs down.
Squat down with your chest up while keeping the bell stable over your shoulder.
Go as low as you can with good control.
Drive up through your heels, then switch arms after your reps.

exercises.name: kettlebell open palm clean
exercises.description: A kettlebell clean where your palm stays open and you catch the bell on your forearm. It teaches a smooth hip-driven pull.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a kettlebell on the floor in front of you.
Hinge down and grab the handle with one hand.
Hike the bell back, then drive your hips forward to pull it up.
Keep your hand open and guide the bell to rest at your shoulder.
Lower it back with control and repeat, then switch sides.

exercises.name: kettlebell one arm swing
exercises.description: A one-armed kettlebell swing driven by the hips. It builds the posterior chain and conditioning.
steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulders and hold a kettlebell with one hand.
Hinge at the hips and swing the bell back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward and let the bell float up to chest height.
Keep your arm relaxed and your back flat.
Let the bell fall back and hinge again, then switch hands after your reps.

exercises.name: kettlebell one legged deadlift
exercises.description: A single-leg hip hinge holding a kettlebell. It trains the hamstrings and glutes and challenges your balance.
steps: Hold a kettlebell in one hand and stand on the opposite leg with a soft knee.
Hinge forward at the hip and extend your free leg straight back.
Lower the bell toward the floor while keeping your back flat.
Stop when your torso is about parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glute to return upright, then switch legs.

exercises.name: knee tuck jump
exercises.description: An explosive vertical jump where you pull your knees into your chest at the top. Great for power and conditioning.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms ready.
Dip into a quarter squat and swing your arms back.
Jump explosively and tuck both knees toward your chest.
Extend your legs again before landing.
Land softly on bent knees and reset before the next jump.

exercises.name: lever one leg extension
exercises.description: A machine leg extension done one leg at a time. It isolates the quads and helps even out strength between sides.
steps: Sit on the machine and adjust the pad so it rests on your lower shin.
Set one foot under the pad and keep the other foot on the floor or footrest.
Extend your working leg until it is almost straight.
Squeeze your quad at the top.
Lower slowly, finish your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: lever seated one leg wide squat
exercises.description: A seated machine squat using one leg in a wide stance. It loads the quads, glutes and inner thighs with back support.
steps: Sit in the machine with your back against the pad and shoulders under the supports.
Place one foot wide on the platform and keep the other leg off the load.
Lower by bending your working knee as far as is comfortable.
Keep your knee tracking over your toes.
Press back up, then switch legs after your reps.

exercises.name: lever seated one leg squat
exercises.description: A seated machine squat done on one leg. It lets you load each leg separately with good support.
steps: Sit in the machine with your back against the pad and shoulders under the supports.
Place one foot on the platform at about shoulder width.
Lower under control by bending your knee.
Keep your heel flat and your knee in line with your toes.
Press back up, then switch legs after your reps.

exercises.name: lever seated wide squat
exercises.description: A seated machine squat with a wide stance. It puts extra emphasis on the glutes and inner thighs.
steps: Sit in the machine with your back against the pad and shoulders under the supports.
Set both feet wide on the platform with toes slightly out.
Lower by bending your knees until your thighs are about parallel.
Keep your knees pointing in the same direction as your toes.
Press through your heels to stand back up.

exercises.name: sled 45° narrow stance leg press
exercises.description: A 45 degree sled leg press with feet close together. The narrow stance puts the focus on the quads.
steps: Sit in the sled with your back flat against the pad and feet close together on the platform.
Release the safety handles.
Lower the sled by bending your knees toward your chest.
Stop before your lower back lifts off the pad.
Press through your heels to extend your legs without locking the knees.

exercises.name: leg up hamstring stretch
exercises.description: Lying on your back with one leg raised, you draw it toward you to stretch the hamstring.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended.
Bend one knee and bring it towards your chest, holding onto your thigh or shin.
Straighten your leg as much as possible while keeping it elevated.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Repeat with the other leg.

exercises.name: lying hip flexor
exercises.description: A lying stretch that opens the front of the hip. Handy after long periods of sitting.
steps: Lie on your back near the edge of a bench or bed.
Hug one knee to your chest.
Let the other leg hang off the edge with the knee relaxed.
Keep your lower back pressed down and breathe slowly.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.

exercises.name: one leg quarter squat
exercises.description: A shallow single-leg squat that is easy on the knees. It builds balance and leg strength.
steps: Stand on one leg with the other foot lifted slightly off the floor.
Extend your arms in front for balance.
Bend your knee and sink down about a quarter of the way.
Keep your knee in line with your toes and your chest up.
Stand back up, then switch legs after your reps.

exercises.name: sled one leg hack squat
exercises.description: A hack squat on the sled using one leg at a time. It isolates each quad and glute with solid back support.
steps: Position yourself in the hack squat sled with your back and shoulders against the pads.
Place one foot in the middle of the platform and keep the other foot off.
Release the safety and lower by bending your working knee.
Go as deep as you can with control.
Press up through your heel, then switch legs after your reps.

exercises.name: prisoner squat
exercises.description: A bodyweight squat with your hands behind your head. It keeps your chest open and builds leg strength.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and place your hands behind your head.
Pull your elbows back and keep your chest up.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower down.
Go until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.

exercises.name: bodyweight rear lunge
exercises.description: A lunge where you step back instead of forward. It is gentler on the knees and focuses on the glutes.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back and lower until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright and your front heel planted.
Push through your front foot to return to standing.
Alternate legs or finish all reps on one side first.

exercises.name: reclining big toe pose with rope
exercises.description: Lying on your back, you hold your big toe with a rope and raise the leg straight. It stretches the hamstrings.
steps: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms by your sides.
Loop the rope around the ball of your right foot and hold the ends of the rope with your hands.
Slowly raise your right leg towards your chest, keeping your knee straight and your foot flexed.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly lower your leg back down to the starting position.
Repeat with your left leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: sled reverse hack squat
exercises.description: A hack squat done facing the pad on the sled. It puts more load on the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Face the pad of the hack squat sled with your chest against it and feet on the platform.
Hold the handles and release the safety.
Lower by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Keep your chest pressed against the pad.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.

exercises.name: rocket jump
exercises.description: A deep squat followed by a big vertical jump with your arms reaching up. It builds explosive leg power.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down while swinging your arms back.
Explode upward and reach both arms overhead as you jump.
Extend your whole body like a rocket.
Land softly on bent knees and reset before the next jump.

exercises.name: runners stretch
exercises.description: A lunge position stretch for the hips, thighs and hamstrings, often used by runners to loosen up.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Take a step forward with your right foot, keeping your left foot planted.
Bend your right knee and lower your body down, keeping your left leg straight.
Place your hands on your right thigh for support.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides and repeat.

exercises.name: lever seated one leg curl
exercises.description: A seated hamstring curl on a machine with one leg at a time. It isolates each hamstring.
steps: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and adjust the leg pad above your heel.
Place one leg under the pad and rest the other foot on the footrest.
Curl your heel down and back as far as you can.
Squeeze your hamstring at the bottom.
Return slowly, then switch legs after your reps.

exercises.name: seated wide angle pose sequence
exercises.description: A seated sequence with legs wide that stretches the inner thighs and hamstrings. Move slowly with the breath.
steps: Sit on the ground with your legs extended in a wide angle.
Flex your feet and engage your quadriceps.
Place your hands on the ground behind you for support.
Keeping your back straight, lean forward from your hips.
Continue leaning forward until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Hold this position for a few breaths.
Slowly release the stretch and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: side to side box shuffle
exercises.description: A quick-footed drill where you hop side to side over a box. It builds agility, lower leg stamina and conditioning.
steps: Stand next to a low box or step on one side.
Place the foot closest to it on top.
Hop across, landing the other foot on the box as the first foot goes down.
Keep your steps light and quick.
Continue shuffling side to side at a steady pace.

exercises.name: single leg butt kick
exercises.description: A hopping drill where you flick one heel up to your glutes. It warms up the hamstrings and raises your heart rate.
steps: Stand on one leg with the other foot lifted.
Hop lightly on your standing foot.
Kick your free heel toward your glutes each hop.
Land softly on the ball of your foot.
Complete your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: lever lying single leg curl
exercises.description: A lying hamstring curl on a machine using one leg at a time. It helps balance strength between legs.
steps: Lie face down on the machine and place one leg under the pad above your heel.
Hold the handles and keep your hips pressed down.
Curl your heel up toward your glutes.
Squeeze your hamstring at the top.
Lower slowly, then switch legs after your reps.

exercises.name: single leg push off
exercises.description: An explosive single-leg push off the floor or a step. It builds leg drive useful for running and jumping.
steps: Stand in front of a low step with one foot planted on it.
Lean slightly forward and keep your core tight.
Push off the step explosively with that leg and drive your opposite knee up.
Land softly on the same foot.
Complete your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: single leg stride jump
exercises.description: A bounding jump from one leg to the other leg. It develops power and single-leg control.
steps: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend.
Push off and leap forward as far as you can.
Land on the opposite leg and absorb the impact with a soft knee.
Hold the landing for a moment to stay balanced.
Repeat, alternating legs or staying on one side.

exercises.name: sit squat
exercises.description: A squat down to a seat and back up. The chair gives you a depth target and builds confidence.
steps: Stand in front of a chair or bench with feet shoulder-width apart.
Push your hips back and lower yourself toward the seat.
Lightly touch the seat without relaxing completely.
Keep your chest up and your knees over your toes.
Press through your heels to stand back up.

exercises.name: smith frankenstein squat
exercises.description: A front-loaded squat on the smith machine with your arms stretched straight in front. It strongly challenges the quads and upper back posture.
steps: Set the bar at upper chest height and rest it on your front shoulders.
Extend your arms straight forward, like a zombie, to keep the bar in place.
Unrack the bar and step into a stable stance.
Squat down with your chest up and your torso upright.
Drive through your heels to stand and rerack when finished.

exercises.name: smith front squat
exercises.description: A front squat with the bar guided by the smith machine. It trains the quads with an upright torso.
steps: Set the bar at shoulder height and rest it on the front of your shoulders with elbows up.
Unrack it and step your feet slightly forward.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Keep your elbows high and your chest up.
Press through your heels to stand and rerack when done.

exercises.name: smith squat to bench
exercises.description: A smith machine squat down to a bench behind you. The bench gives a consistent depth target.
steps: Place a bench behind you under the smith bar.
Rest the bar on your upper back and unrack it.
Sit your hips back and lower until you touch the bench lightly.
Keep your chest up and your knees tracking your toes.
Drive through your heels to stand and rerack when finished.

exercises.name: smith stiff legged deadlift
exercises.description: A stiff-legged deadlift using the smith machine bar. The fixed path lets you focus on feeling the hamstrings work.
steps: Stand close to the smith bar with feet hip-width apart and grip the bar overhand.
Unrack it and keep your knees nearly straight.
Push your hips back and slide the bar down your legs.
Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes to stand tall.

exercises.name: smith zercher squat
exercises.description: A squat holding the bar in the crooks of your elbows on the smith machine. It trains the legs while taxing the core and upper back.
steps: Set the bar at waist height and hook your elbows under it with your arms crossed.
Unrack and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down while keeping your chest up and the bar close to your body.
Go until your thighs are about parallel.
Press through your heels to stand and rerack when done.

exercises.name: standing hamstring and calf stretch with strap
exercises.description: Standing with a strap around your foot, you pull your toes toward you to stretch the hamstring and calf.
steps: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the strap with both hands and place it around the ball of your foot.
Keep your leg straight and slowly lean forward from your hips, keeping your back straight.
Feel the stretch in your hamstring and calf muscles.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release the stretch and repeat with the other leg.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: standing long jump
exercises.description: A jump for distance from a standing start. It builds explosive power in the hips and legs.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart at a clear starting line.
Swing your arms back and bend your knees.
Swing your arms forward and jump as far as you can.
Land on both feet with your knees bent to absorb the impact.
Reset and repeat.

exercises.name: standing straight leg hamstring contract relax on exercise ball
exercises.description: A hamstring stretch with the heel on a stability ball, using a contract and relax method. It helps you ease deeper into the stretch.
steps: Stand and rest one heel on a stability ball in front of you with your knee straight.
Hinge forward at the hips until you feel a stretch in the back of the thigh.
Gently press your heel into the ball for about 5 seconds, then relax.
Lean a little deeper into the stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.

exercises.name: transverse step up
exercises.description: A step-up performed side-on to the bench. It works the glutes and quads while challenging your balance.
steps: Stand sideways next to a bench or step.
Place the inside foot fully on top.
Drive through that heel and step up until your leg is straight.
Bring your other foot up to meet it.
Step back down with control, finish your reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: weighted exercise ball wall squat
exercises.description: A wall squat with a stability ball behind you while holding extra weight. It adds load to a back-supported squat.
steps: Place a stability ball between your lower back and a wall.
Hold your weight at chest level or at your sides.
Step your feet forward and squat as the ball rolls down your back.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Press through your heels to rise back up.

exercises.name: world greatest stretch
exercises.description: A flowing lunge with a twist and reach that opens the hips, hamstrings and upper back. A favorite warm-up move.
steps: Start in a lunge position with your right foot forward and your left foot back.
Place your hands on the ground on either side of your right foot.
Lower your left knee to the ground and extend your right leg, keeping your right foot flat on the ground.
Rotate your torso to the right, reaching your right arm up towards the ceiling.
Hold this position for a few seconds, then return to the starting position.
Switch sides and repeat the stretch with your left foot forward.

exercises.name: cable triceps pushdown (sz bar)
exercises.description: A cable pushdown using an SZ bar, a staple for building the back of the arm.
steps: Attach an SZ bar to a high pulley and grip it with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Pin your elbows to your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Squeeze your triceps for a moment.
Let the bar rise slowly until your forearms are just above parallel.

exercises.name: cable reverse grip triceps pushdown (sz bar)
exercises.description: A triceps pushdown with an underhand grip on an SZ bar. The reverse grip shifts the feel slightly and works the forearms too.
steps: Attach an SZ bar to a high pulley and grip it palms up with hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows tucked at your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are straight.
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom.
Return slowly without letting your elbows drift forward.

exercises.name: cable biceps curl (sz bar)
exercises.description: A standing cable curl with an SZ bar. The cable keeps constant tension on the biceps.
steps: Attach an SZ bar to a low pulley and grip it with an underhand grip.
Stand tall with your elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower slowly and avoid swinging your body.

exercises.name: cable standing reverse curl (sz bar)
exercises.description: A standing curl with an overhand grip on a cable SZ bar. It targets the brachialis and forearms.
steps: Attach an SZ bar to a low pulley and grip it overhand with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Stand tall with your elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the bar up while keeping your wrists straight.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly and keep your torso still.

exercises.name: cable one arm side triceps pushdown
exercises.description: A one-armed cable pushdown done from the side. It isolates each triceps and lets you focus on form.
steps: Attach a handle to a high pulley and stand sideways to the machine.
Grip the handle with the arm closest to the stack and keep your elbow at your side.
Push the handle down until your arm is straight.
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom.
Return slowly, finish your reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: barbell behind back finger curl
exercises.description: A forearm exercise where you hold the bar behind your back and roll it down to your fingertips. It builds grip and forearm strength.
steps: Stand holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip, arms straight.
Let the bar roll down to your fingertips.
Curl your fingers closed and lift the bar back into your palms.
Curl your wrists up a little at the top.
Lower with control and repeat.

exercises.name: dumbbell behind back finger curl
exercises.description: Holding a dumbbell behind your back, you roll it down to your fingertips and curl it back up. It builds finger and forearm flexor strength and grip.
steps: Stand tall with a light dumbbell held in one hand behind your back.
Let the dumbbell roll down until it rests on your fingertips.
Close your fingers and curl the weight back into your palm.
Keep your wrist still and your arm close to your body.
Lower under control and repeat, then switch hands.

exercises.name: swimmer hips
exercises.description: A prone floor move where opposite arm and leg lift in alternation, training the back and glutes.
steps: Lie face down with your arms extended overhead and your legs straight.
Lift your chest slightly and brace your glutes.
Raise one arm and the opposite leg a few inches.
Switch sides in a controlled flutter.
Keep your neck neutral and breathe steadily.

exercises.name: lever preacher curl v. 2
exercises.description: A preacher curl on a lever machine, version 2. The pad locks your upper arms in place so the biceps do the work.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your upper arms resting on the pad and your chest against the support.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your upper arms stationary and exhale as you curl the handles towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale as you slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever hammer grip preacher curl
exercises.description: A preacher curl on a lever machine with a neutral hammer grip. It hits the brachialis and forearms along with the biceps.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the leverage machine.
Place your upper arms on the preacher pad, ensuring your chest is pressed against it.
Grasp the handles with a hammer grip (palms facing each other).
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the handles towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever reverse grip preacher curl
exercises.description: A preacher curl on a lever machine with an overhand grip. It shifts work to the forearms and brachialis.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the leverage machine.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Rest your upper arms on the preacher pad, ensuring your elbows are fully extended.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the handles towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, fully extending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell decline one arm hammer press
exercises.description: A one-arm press on a decline bench with a neutral grip. It targets the triceps and the lower chest.
steps: Lie on a decline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your chest.
Extend your arm straight up, keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Lower the dumbbell down towards your shoulder, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Press the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline hammer press on exercise ball
exercises.description: A neutral-grip press on an incline bench set on an exercise ball. The ball adds an unstable challenge for the triceps.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder level, elbows bent and pointing out to the sides.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly inward, keeping your palms facing each other.
Extend your arms fully, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline one arm hammer press
exercises.description: A one-arm neutral-grip press on an incline bench. It trains the triceps and upper chest on one side at a time.
steps: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your thigh.
Lean back on the bench and use your thigh to help raise the dumbbell to shoulder height.
Rotate your wrist so that your palm is facing inward, towards your body.
Press the dumbbell up and away from your body, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell incline one arm hammer press on exercise ball
exercises.description: A one-arm hammer press on an incline with an exercise ball. It works the triceps and adds a balance challenge.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell with your palm facing inward and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Press the dumbbell up towards the ceiling, straightening your arm.
Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm hammer press on exercise ball
exercises.description: A one-arm neutral-grip press while lying on an exercise ball. It trains the triceps while the core keeps you stable.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing inwards and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Place your other hand on your hip for stability.
Press the dumbbell upwards, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: dumbbell one arm reverse grip press
exercises.description: A one-arm dumbbell press with your palm facing you. It shifts focus to the upper chest and biceps.
steps: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing towards your body.
Place your feet flat on the ground and keep your back straight.
Raise the dumbbell to shoulder height, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Press the dumbbell upwards until your arm is fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: dumbbell palms in incline bench press
exercises.description: An incline bench press with palms facing in. It trains the triceps and the front delts with a shoulder-friendly grip.
steps: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your back against the backrest and feet flat on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing inwards.
Extend your arms straight up above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells slowly towards your shoulders, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then press the dumbbells back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell reverse bench press
exercises.description: A bench press with a reverse grip using dumbbells. It targets the upper chest and the triceps.
steps: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing towards your feet.
Extend your arms straight up towards the ceiling, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells towards your chest, allowing your elbows to flare out to the sides.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the dumbbells back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith machine decline close grip bench press
exercises.description: A close grip bench press on a decline bench in the smith machine. It builds the triceps and lower chest.
steps: Adjust the bench on the smith machine to a decline position.
Lie down on the bench with your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with a close grip, slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause for a moment when the barbell is just above your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: smith machine reverse decline close grip bench press
exercises.description: A reverse grip, close grip decline bench press in the smith machine. It works the chest and triceps.
steps: Adjust the smith machine to a decline position.
Lie down on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Grasp the barbell with a close grip, slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: ez barbell close grip preacher curl
exercises.description: A preacher curl with an EZ bar and a close grip. It emphasizes the outer biceps.
steps: Sit on a preacher curl bench and place your upper arms on the pad, gripping the ez barbell with an underhand grip.
Rest your triceps on the pad and fully extend your arms, keeping your back straight.
Slowly curl the barbell towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: ez barbell spider curl
exercises.description: A spider curl with an EZ bar, lying chest down on an incline bench. It isolates the biceps with no swing.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Rest your upper arms on a preacher bench or stability ball, allowing your elbows to hang down.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the barbell up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell standing wide grip biceps curl
exercises.description: A standing barbell curl with a wide grip. It puts more load on the inner biceps.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and your elbows close to your torso.
Exhale and curl the barbell up towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable close grip curl
exercises.description: A cable curl with a close grip. It keeps constant tension on the biceps.
steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Exhale and curl the bar up towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable concentration curl
exercises.description: A concentration curl using a cable. The elbow stays braced so the biceps do the work.
steps: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the floor and your knees slightly bent.
Hold the cable handle with an underhand grip and rest your elbow against the inside of your thigh.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the cable handle towards your shoulder while contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then inhale and slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: cable drag curl
exercises.description: A cable curl where you drag the handle up along your body. It trains the biceps with the elbows pulled back.
steps: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the cable attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and arms fully extended.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the cable attachment towards your shoulders by contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the cable attachment back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable one arm preacher curl
exercises.description: A one-arm preacher curl on a cable. The pad blocks swinging, so the biceps take the load.
steps: Adjust the cable machine so that the preacher curl pad is at chest height.
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the cable handle with an underhand grip and position your upper arm against the preacher curl pad.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Slowly curl the cable handle towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm against the pad.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.

exercises.name: cable lying bicep curl
exercises.description: A biceps curl lying on your back with a cable. It keeps tension constant through the whole motion.
steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.
Lie face up on a flat bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms fully, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the bar up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable one arm reverse preacher curl
exercises.description: A one-arm reverse grip preacher curl on a cable. It works the brachialis and forearms along with the biceps.
steps: Adjust the cable machine so that the pulley is at the lowest position.
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the cable handle with an underhand grip and position your upper arm against the preacher bench pad.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Slowly curl your forearm towards your bicep, keeping your upper arm stationary against the pad.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your bicep.
Slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.

exercises.name: cable overhead curl
exercises.description: A curl with the cable set high so the arms are lifted overhead. It trains the biceps through a short range.
steps: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary.
Exhale and curl the bar down towards your forehead, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly return the bar to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable overhead curl on exercise ball
exercises.description: An overhead cable curl while sitting on an exercise ball. The ball adds core demand to the biceps work.
steps: Sit on an exercise ball and hold the cable handle with an underhand grip.
Extend your arms fully overhead, keeping your elbows close to your ears.
Slowly curl the cable down towards your forehead, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable pulldown bicep curl
exercises.description: A curl at a high pulley that begins with a pulldown. It builds the biceps and also the lats.
steps: Attach a straight bar to the cable machine at the highest setting.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary.
Exhale and slowly curl the bar down towards your thighs, keeping your wrists straight.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly return the bar to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable rope hammer preacher curl
exercises.description: A hammer grip preacher curl with a rope on a cable. It targets the brachialis and the biceps.
steps: Attach a rope attachment to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Position your upper arms against the preacher bench pad, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the rope towards your shoulders by contracting your biceps.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the rope back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable rope one arm hammer preacher curl
exercises.description: A one-arm hammer preacher curl with a rope on a cable. It targets the brachialis and the biceps on one side.
steps: Attach a rope handle to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the rope handle with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Position your upper arm against the preacher bench pad, keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Slowly curl the rope handle towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the rope handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.name: cable seated curl
exercises.description: A seated cable biceps curl. The seat keeps you steady so the biceps do the lifting.
steps: Sit on a cable machine with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Grasp the cable attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your arms fully extended.
