exercises.description: A standing lunge-style stretch for the front of the hip and thigh.
steps: Stand and step one foot forward and the other back into a staggered stance.
Tuck your pelvis and squeeze the glute of the back leg.
Shift your hips slightly forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip.
Keep your torso upright.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: sitting one leg external stretch
exercises.description: A seated stretch that opens one hip by turning the leg outward.
steps: Sit on the floor and bend one leg so the foot rests against the opposite thigh.
Lean your chest forward over the bent leg while pressing the knee toward the floor until the hip stretches.
Keep your back long.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: assisted one leg extension
exercises.description: A partner-assisted leg movement that gently stretches the hip and thigh.
steps: Lie on your back and relax.
Have a partner support one leg and gently extend it.
Let the partner move the leg only to a mild stretch.
Keep your lower back flat on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.

exercises.name: supported one leg standing hip flexor and knee extensor stretch
exercises.description: A supported standing quad stretch that also opens the front of the hip.
steps: Stand tall holding a wall or chair for support.
Bend one knee and hold the ankle behind you.
Pull the heel toward your glutes and push the hip slightly forward.
Keep your knees close together.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: quadriceps stretch on box
exercises.description: A quad stretch with the back foot resting on a box or bench, opening the front of the thigh.
steps: Stand facing away from a box or bench and place the top of one foot on it behind you.
Stand tall on the front leg with a soft knee.
Tuck your pelvis and lower the hips slightly until you feel a stretch in the front of the thigh.
Hold a support for balance if needed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: single lean back quadriceps stretch
exercises.description: Kneeling with one leg folded and leaning back to stretch the quadriceps.
steps: Kneel on both knees, then lift one foot out in front so that the other leg is folded.
Place your hands behind you on the floor.
Lean back slowly until you feel a stretch in the front of the folded thigh.
Keep your hips lifted and avoid sagging into the lower back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: double lean back quadriceps stretch
exercises.description: Sitting back on your heels and leaning back to stretch both quadriceps at once.
steps: Kneel and sit back so your hips rest on your heels.
Place your hands on the floor behind you.
Lean back slowly and lift the hips slightly until you feel a stretch in the front of both thighs.
Stop if you feel any pinch in the knees.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then come back up slowly.

exercises.name: standing shin stretch
exercises.description: Standing with the top of the foot on the floor to stretch the muscles at the front of the shin.
steps: Stand tall and hold a wall for balance.
Place the top of one foot on the floor behind you with the toes curled under.
Gently press the foot down by bending the standing knee.
Feel the stretch along the front of the shin and ankle.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: standing toe extensor stretch
exercises.description: Pressing the tops of the toes against the floor to stretch the front of the foot and shin.
steps: Stand next to a support and place the top of one foot on the floor behind you with the toes curled under.
Gently bend your standing knee and press the toes down until you feel the stretch on top of the foot and shin.
Keep the pressure light and controlled.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: raised foot shin stretch
exercises.description: A stretch with the foot raised on a support, easing the shin and top of the ankle.
steps: Stand next to a wall and lift one foot behind you onto a low support with the top of the foot down.
Keep your torso upright and your standing leg soft.
Press your hips forward gently until you feel the shin stretch.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: double kneeling shin stretch
exercises.description: Kneeling and sitting back onto your heels to stretch the front of the shins and ankles.
steps: Kneel on a mat with your feet pointing straight back and the tops of the feet on the floor.
Slowly sit back toward your heels until you feel the shins and ankles stretch.
Place your hands on the floor in front of you to control the pressure.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: squatting toe stretch
exercises.description: A deep squat on the balls of the feet that stretches the toes and the bottom of the feet.
steps: Crouch down with your heels lifted and toes tucked under.
Place your hands on the floor in front of you for support.
Slowly sit back toward your heels until you feel the toes and soles stretch.
Ease off if the stretch is too sharp.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release.

exercises.name: seated toe extensor stretch
exercises.description: A seated stretch for the muscles that lift the toes, using your hand to point the toes downward.
steps: Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the top of the foot and toes with your hand.
Gently curl the toes and foot downward until you feel a stretch on the top.
Keep the motion gentle.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: seated toe extensor and foot everter stretch
exercises.description: Seated stretch combining pointing the toes down with a turn of the sole outward.
steps: Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the top of the foot and toes with your hand.
Curl the toes down and turn the sole gently outward.
Feel the stretch along the top and outer edge of the foot.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: seated toe extensor and foot inverter stretch
exercises.description: Seated stretch combining pointing the toes down with a turn of the sole inward.
steps: Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the top of the foot and toes with your hand.
Curl the toes down and turn the sole gently inward.
Feel the stretch along the top and inner edge of the foot.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: seated toe flexor stretch
exercises.description: A seated stretch pulling the toes back to lengthen the bottom of the foot.
steps: Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the toes with your hand.
Gently pull the toes back toward your shin.
Feel the stretch along the sole of the foot.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: seated toe flexor and foot everter stretch
exercises.description: Seated stretch pulling the toes back while turning the sole outward.
steps: Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the toes with your hand.
Pull the toes back toward your shin and turn the sole gently outward.
Feel the stretch along the sole and inner edge of the foot.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: seated toe flexor and foot inverter stretch
exercises.description: Seated stretch pulling the toes back while turning the sole inward.
steps: Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the toes with your hand.
Pull the toes back toward your shin and turn the sole gently inward.
Feel the stretch along the sole and outer edge of the foot.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: standing toe flexor stretch
exercises.description: Pulling the toes back against a wall to stretch the sole of the foot and the calf.
steps: Stand facing a wall and place the toes of one foot on it with the heel on the floor.
Lean forward gently until you feel the stretch along the bottom of the foot and into the calf.
Keep your heel firmly on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: mobilization of ankle stretch
exercises.description: A gentle rocking stretch that improves ankle movement and loosens the calf.
steps: Stand facing a wall with one foot forward, toes a few inches from it.
Keep your front heel on the floor.
Bend the front knee and glide it toward the wall.
Return and repeat slowly for 10-15 reps, then switch feet.

exercises.name: standing upright shoulders stretch
exercises.description: A tall standing stretch that opens the shoulders and chest.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Clasp your hands behind your back.
Straighten your arms and lift them gently away from your body.
Keep your chest open and your neck relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: reverse shoulder stretch
exercises.description: Clasping your hands behind your back and lifting them to open the front of the shoulders.
steps: Stand tall and clasp your hands behind your back.
Straighten your arms and lift your hands up and away from your body until the shoulders and chest stretch.
Keep your chest open and avoid leaning forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: sitting shoulders stretch on bench
exercises.description: A seated stretch that opens the front of the shoulders using a bench.
steps: Sit on the edge of a bench and place your hands behind you on it, fingers pointing back.
Walk your hips slightly forward off the bench.
Lower your hips gently until you feel a stretch at the front of the shoulders.
Keep your back close to the bench and shoulders down.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then rise up.

exercises.name: assisted sitting reverse shoulder stretch
exercises.description: A partner gently draws your arms back to stretch the front of the shoulders.
steps: Sit tall and put your arms behind you, palms facing down.
Have a partner stand behind and hold your wrists or forearms.
Ask them to lift your arms slowly until you feel a stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and chest open.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then lower slowly.

exercises.name: standing reverse shoulder stretch
exercises.description: Standing with your hands clasped behind you to open the front of the shoulders.
steps: Stand tall and clasp your hands behind your back.
Straighten your arms and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lift your hands slightly away from your body.
Keep your chest up and avoid arching your lower back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release.

exercises.name: seated shoulder flexor depressor retractor stretch
exercises.description: A seated stretch that lengthens the shoulder and chest by pressing the arms back and down.
steps: Sit tall on a chair or bench.
Place your hands behind you on the seat, fingers pointing back.
Press your shoulders down and back, opening your chest.
Lean slightly forward until you feel the stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then relax.

exercises.name: one arm shoulder flexor stretch
exercises.description: Stretching one arm back and down to lengthen the front of the shoulder.
steps: Stand next to a wall or post and place one hand on it behind you with the arm straight.
Slowly turn your body away until you feel the front of the shoulder stretch.
Keep the arm straight and the shoulder relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: adduction of arm in back stretch
exercises.description: Reaching one arm behind your back and pulling it across to stretch the shoulder.
steps: Stand or sit tall.
Reach one arm behind your back.
Grab that wrist with the other hand and gently pull it across your body.
Keep your shoulders level.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: shoulder extensor adductor and retractor stretch
exercises.description: A stretch for the back of the shoulder and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
steps: Stand tall and extend one arm behind you.
Reach across to grab it with the other hand.
Draw the arm gently back and across the body.
Keep your chest open and your shoulders down.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: shoulder adductor elevator and protractor stretch
exercises.description: A cross body stretch that loosens the back of the shoulder and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
steps: Stand or sit tall and bring one arm across your chest.
Use the opposite hand to press the arm toward you until the shoulder and upper back stretch.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: across chest shoulder stretch
exercises.description: A classic cross-body stretch for the back of the shoulder.
steps: Stand tall and bring one arm straight across your chest.
Use your other forearm to press the arm gently toward your body.
Keep the shoulder relaxed and down.
Feel the stretch in the back of the shoulder.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: bent arm shoulder stretch
exercises.description: A cross-body shoulder stretch with the elbow bent, easing the back of the shoulder.
steps: Stand tall and bring one arm across your chest with the elbow bent.
Hold the elbow with your other hand.
Gently pull the elbow toward the opposite shoulder.
Keep your shoulders level and your neck relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: rotation shoulder stretch
exercises.description: A gentle rotation stretch for the shoulder joint.
steps: Stand tall and bend one elbow to 90 degrees at your side.
Slowly rotate your forearm outward or inward, using the other hand to assist, until you feel the shoulder stretch.
Keep your elbow tucked in close to your body.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: reaching up shoulder stretch
exercises.description: Reaching overhead to stretch the shoulders and the sides of the upper body.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart.
Reach one or both arms overhead and up as high as you can, then press them slightly backward.
Do not arch your lower back as you reach.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: rotator cuff stretch
exercises.description: A stretch aimed at the small stabilizing muscles around the shoulder joint.
steps: Stand tall and bring one arm across your body at chest height.
Hold the arm just above the elbow with the other hand and draw it in until the back of the shoulder stretches.
Keep the shoulder blade down and relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: elbow out rotator stretch
exercises.description: A stretch for the rotator cuff with the elbow lifted out to the side.
steps: Stand tall and lift one elbow out to the side, hand behind your head.
Hold the elbow with your other hand.
Gently press the elbow back and slightly down.
Feel the stretch in the shoulder.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: arm up rotator stretch
exercises.description: An overhead stretch for the rotator cuff and back of the arm.
steps: Raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow, palm resting on your upper back.
Use your other hand to hold the elbow.
Gently press the elbow back and down.
Keep your ribs down and chest open.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: arm down rotator stretch
exercises.description: A stretch for the rotator cuff with the arm held low behind the body.
steps: Stand tall and place one arm behind your back, bent at the elbow.
Hold the wrist with the other hand.
Gently draw the hand away from your body and slightly up.
Keep your shoulders relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: kneeling one arm cross body stretch
exercises.description: A kneeling stretch where you reach one arm across the body to open the back of the shoulder.
steps: Kneel on a mat and slide one arm across the floor in front of you, palm down.
Sink your chest toward the floor and keep reaching until the shoulder and upper back stretch.
Keep your hips over your knees.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: depression in parallel bars stretch
exercises.description: A hanging stretch between parallel bars that opens the shoulders and lengthens the lats.
steps: Stand between parallel bars and grip them at hip height.
Walk back slightly, letting your arms straighten.
Lower your chest toward the floor and press your head between your arms.
Feel the stretch in the lats and shoulders.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then walk forward to release.

exercises.name: external shoulder rotation stretch
exercises.description: A stretch that eases the shoulder into outward rotation.
steps: Stand next to a doorframe and bend your elbow to 90 degrees with your forearm on the frame.
Slowly turn your body away from the arm until you feel the front of the shoulder stretch.
Keep your elbow level with your shoulder.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: internal shoulder rotation stretch
exercises.description: A stretch that eases the shoulder into inward rotation.
steps: Stand tall and place one hand behind your lower back with the elbow bent.
Use the other hand or a towel to gently draw the hand up your back until the back of the shoulder stretches.
Keep your shoulders level and do not twist.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: sled full hack squat
exercises.description: A hack squat on a sled machine through a full range of motion, loading the quads and glutes.
steps: Set your shoulders under the pads and your feet shoulder-width on the platform.
Unlock the safety and straighten your legs.
Lower your hips slowly until your thighs are below parallel.
Keep your back flat against the pad and knees tracking over your toes.
Press through your whole foot to stand back up.

exercises.name: single leg hip thrusts
exercises.description: A one-leg hip thrust that works the glutes hard and challenges balance and hip stability.
steps: Sit with your upper back against a bench and one foot flat on the floor.
Extend the other leg or hold it up.
Drive through the heel to lift your hips until your body is flat.
Squeeze your glute at the top, then lower under control.
Complete the reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: hip thrusts
exercises.description: A glute-focused bridge with the upper back on a bench, lifting the hips to build strong glutes.
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and knees bent.
Plant your feet flat, hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is level.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat.

exercises.name: shoulder adductor protractor and elevator stretch
exercises.description: A stretch for the back of the shoulder and the muscles along the upper back.
steps: Stand tall and bring one arm across your chest.
Hold it with the other arm just above the elbow.
Gently pull while rounding the upper back slightly forward.
Keep your neck relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: shoulder stretch with towel behind the back
exercises.description: Using a towel behind the back to ease the shoulders into a deeper stretch.
steps: Hold a towel in one hand and raise that arm overhead, bending the elbow.
Reach the other hand up from behind your back and grab the towel.
Gently pull the towel down with the lower hand.
Keep your head upright.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: finger stretch
exercises.description: A simple stretch that opens the fingers and forearm muscles, useful after typing or gripping.
steps: Hold one arm out in front of you with the elbow straight.
Use the other hand to gently pull the fingers back until you feel a stretch in the palm and forearm.
Keep the fingers straight and relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: palms out forearm stretch
exercises.description: Clasped hands pressed forward with the palms facing out to stretch the forearms.
steps: Stand or sit tall and interlace your fingers.
Turn your palms outward and straighten your arms in front of you.
Push your hands gently away until you feel the stretch in the forearms.
Keep your shoulders relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release.

exercises.name: fingers down forearm stretch
exercises.description: A stretch for the top of the forearm with the fingers pointing down.
steps: Extend one arm in front of you with the palm facing down.
Bend the wrist so the fingers point toward the floor.
Use your other hand to press the back of the hand gently toward you.
Keep your elbow straight.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: wall flexors stretch
exercises.description: Pressing the palm against a wall to stretch the forearm flexors.
steps: Stand facing a wall and place one palm on it with the fingers pointing down.
Keep your arm straight.
Slowly turn your body away until you feel the stretch in the forearm.
Keep your fingers flat on the wall.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: seated wrist ulnar deviator and flexor stretch
exercises.description: A seated wrist stretch for the inner forearm and the little finger side of the wrist.
steps: Sit tall and extend one arm forward with the palm facing up.
Use the other hand to bend the wrist back and tilt it toward the thumb side until the forearm stretches.
Keep the elbow straight.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: thumb stretch
exercises.description: A gentle stretch for the thumb and the muscles at its base.
steps: Extend one arm with the palm facing up.
Use your other hand to hold the thumb.
Gently pull the thumb back and away from the palm.
Stop at a mild stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: finger extension stretch
exercises.description: A stretch that bends the fingers back to lengthen the palm side of the forearm.
steps: Extend one arm in front with the palm facing up.
Use your other hand to hold the fingers.
Gently pull the fingers back toward you.
Keep your elbow straight and the wrist relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: flexion finger stretch
exercises.description: Gently bends the fingers down to stretch the tight tissue on the top of the hand and fingers. Handy after typing or gripping work.
steps: Hold one arm out in front of you with the palm facing down.
Use your other hand to press the fingers of the extended hand gently downward.
Keep the elbow of the extended arm straight and the shoulders relaxed.
Stop at a mild pull, never at pain.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Release and repeat on the other hand.

exercises.name: separation finger stretch
exercises.description: Spreads the fingers wide apart to open up the hand and loosen the small muscles between the fingers.
steps: Hold one hand up in front of you with the palm facing you.
Spread your fingers as far apart as feels comfortable.
If you want more stretch, press between the fingers with your other hand.
Keep the wrist straight and the shoulder relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Relax the hand and switch sides.

exercises.name: adduction hand with elbow extended stretch
exercises.description: Tilts the hand sideways at the wrist with a straight elbow to stretch the forearm muscles along the outer edge of the arm.
steps: Stand tall and extend one arm in front of you with the elbow straight.
Turn the palm so the thumb points up.
Grab the hand with your other hand and tilt it gently toward the little finger side.
Keep the elbow locked and the shoulder down.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Release and repeat on the other arm.

exercises.name: recumbent hip external rotator and hip extensor stretch (crossed leg)
exercises.description: A reclined figure four stretch for the buttocks and deep hip muscles.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee, then pull the legs toward your chest until the buttock stretches.
Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: seated quadriceps stretch
exercises.description: Stretches the front of the thigh from a seated position by folding one leg back while the other stays supported.
steps: Sit sideways on a bench or sturdy seat with one leg hanging off the side.
Bend the hanging knee and bring the heel back toward your glutes.
Hold the foot or ankle with your hand and gently pull the heel closer.
Keep your torso upright and your knees close together.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Release and switch legs.

exercises.name: front cross over shin stretch
exercises.description: Crossing one foot in front and pressing the toes down to stretch the front of the shin.
steps: Stand tall and cross one leg in front of the other.
Point the toes of the back foot against the floor and gently bend the knee until the shin and ankle stretch.
Hold a wall or chair for balance.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: sitting toe pull calf stretch
exercises.description: Pulls the toes back toward the shin while sitting, giving the calf and the back of the lower leg a gentle stretch.
steps: Sit on the floor with one leg straight out in front of you.
Reach forward and grab the toes or the ball of the foot of that leg.
Gently pull the toes toward your shin while keeping the knee straight.
Sit tall and avoid rounding your back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Release and switch legs.

exercises.name: separation between fingers stretch
exercises.description: Spreads the toes apart to wake up and loosen the small muscles of the foot.
steps: Sit comfortably and bring one foot up to rest on the opposite knee.
Hold the foot with your hand.
Slide your fingers between the toes and gently spread them apart.
Keep the movement slow and easy.
Hold the spread for 15-20 seconds.
Release and switch feet.

exercises.name: leaning heel back achilles stretch
exercises.description: Targets the lower calf and Achilles tendon area by leaning into a wall with the back heel pressed down and the knee bent.
steps: Stand facing a wall and place your hands on it at chest height.
Step one foot back and keep that heel on the floor.
Bend both knees slightly and lean forward until you feel a pull low in the back calf.
Keep the back heel flat and the toes pointing forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Switch legs.

exercises.name: lower trunk flexor stretch
exercises.description: A backbend style stretch that lengthens the front of the abdomen and hips.
steps: Lie face down with your hands under your shoulders.
Press up through your hands and let your hips sink toward the floor until the lower abdomen stretches.
Keep your hips on the floor and your shoulders relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: cat stretch v. 2
exercises.description: Rounds the spine upward from all fours to loosen the back and gently engage the abs. A classic mobility move for stiff backs.
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Tuck your chin and tilt the pelvis as you push the floor away.
Round your back up toward the ceiling like a cat.
Hold the rounded position for a few seconds.
Return slowly to the neutral starting position.
Repeat for 8-10 slow reps.

exercises.name: cow stretch
exercises.description: Lets the belly sink and the chest lift from all fours to stretch the front of the trunk and mobilise the spine.
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale and let your belly drop toward the floor.
Lift your chest and tailbone while looking slightly forward.
Keep your arms straight and shoulders away from your ears.
Hold for a couple of seconds, then return to neutral.
Repeat for 8-10 slow reps.

exercises.name: standing lean back stomach stretch
exercises.description: A standing lean back that stretches the abdominal wall.
steps: Stand tall with your hands on your hips.
Gently lean back and push your hips slightly forward until you feel a stretch across the stomach.
Keep your movement small and avoid cranking your lower back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: kneeling abdominal stretch
exercises.description: A kneeling backbend that opens the front of the torso.
steps: Kneel with your knees hip width apart and place your hands on your lower back.
Push your hips forward and lean back until the abdominal muscles stretch.
Tuck your chin a little and avoid dropping your head back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: standing abs rotation stretch
exercises.description: Rotates the upper body from a standing position to stretch the abs and obliques and loosen the trunk.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed.
Place your hands on your hips or hold them out to the sides.
Keep the hips facing forward and turn your upper body slowly to one side.
Look over your shoulder and breathe steadily.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Return to the front and rotate to the other side.

exercises.name: rotating stomach stretch
exercises.description: Combines a gentle lift of the chest with a twist to stretch the stomach muscles and the sides of the trunk.
steps: Lie face down and prop yourself up on your forearms or hands.
Keep your hips on the floor and lift your chest.
Slowly turn your head and shoulders toward one side.
Stay relaxed and avoid pushing into pain in the lower back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Return to centre and rotate to the other side.

exercises.name: hip extension supported from back
exercises.description: Lifts the hips while the upper back is supported, teaching the glutes to extend the hip through a full range.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your arms by your sides for support.
Push through your heels and lift the hips until the body forms a straight line.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without arching the lower back.
Lower the hips back down with control.
Repeat for 10-12 reps.

exercises.name: standing lower trunk lateral flexor stretch
exercises.description: Bends the lower trunk sideways from a standing position to stretch the muscles along the flank and low back.
steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width.
Place one hand on your hip and reach the other arm overhead.
Push the hips slightly to the side opposite your reach.
Bend sideways from the waist without leaning forward or back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Return to upright and switch sides.

exercises.name: seated lower trunk lateral flexor stretch
exercises.description: A seated side bend that lengthens the muscles along the side of the waist.
steps: Sit tall on the floor or a chair with your legs crossed or feet flat.
Reach one arm overhead and bend sideways away from it until you feel the side of the waist stretch.
Keep both hips grounded and avoid leaning forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: hip extension on knees
exercises.description: Opens the front of the hips from a kneeling position by pushing the pelvis forward, which also wakes up the glutes.
steps: Kneel on a soft surface with knees hip-width apart and thighs upright.
Place your hands on your hips or the back of your pelvis.
Squeeze your glutes and push your hips forward.
Keep your ribs down and avoid over-arching your lower back.
Hold for a moment, then return to the start.
Repeat for 8-12 reps.

exercises.name: lying knee roll over stretch
exercises.description: Rolls the knees to one side while lying on your back to twist the lower spine and loosen the hips and sides.
steps: Lie on your back with arms out to the sides and knees bent.
Keep your shoulders flat on the floor.
Slowly lower both knees to one side.
Turn your head the other way if it feels comfortable.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Bring the knees back to centre and roll to the other side.

exercises.name: standing lateral side stretch
exercises.description: A standing side bend for the sides of the waist and ribs.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart.
Reach one arm overhead and bend sideways away from it until you feel the side stretch.
Keep your chest open and your hips level.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: sitting lateral side stretch
exercises.description: A seated side bend that stretches the sides of the waist and the lats.
steps: Sit tall with your legs crossed or feet flat on the floor.
Reach one arm overhead and lean sideways away from it, placing the other hand on the floor for support.
Keep both sit bones grounded.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: standing side stretch
exercises.description: Reaches an arm overhead and leans to the side to lengthen the flank, lats and obliques.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Raise one arm overhead with the palm facing inward.
Lean your torso sideways away from the raised arm.
Keep both hips level and your chest facing forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Return upright and repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: standing side stretch with stick
exercises.description: Uses a stick held overhead to guide a deeper side bend, stretching the flank and the lats.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a stick with both hands overhead.
Keep your arms straight and your shoulders relaxed.
Lean your torso slowly to one side without twisting.
Keep your hips steady and your chest facing forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Return to upright and lean to the other side.

exercises.name: lateral bend lying down
exercises.description: Curves the body sideways while lying down, which stretches the flank without any need to balance.
steps: Lie on your back with legs together and arms stretched overhead.
Slide both feet and both hands to the same side so the body forms a gentle arc.
Keep your hips and shoulders on the floor.
Breathe slowly and relax into the curve.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Return to centre and bend to the other side.

exercises.name: assisted side bent
exercises.description: A partner helps guide a sideways bend of the trunk, making it easier to relax into the stretch along the flank.
steps: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and one arm overhead.
Have your partner stand behind you with a hand on your hip and a hand on your raised arm.
Lean sideways as your partner gently guides the movement.
Tell your partner to stop at a mild pull.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Return upright and switch sides.

exercises.name: assisted obliques stretch
exercises.description: With help from a partner, this stretch lengthens the oblique muscles on the side of the trunk through a slow bend or twist.
steps: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
Raise one arm overhead while your partner steadies your hips.
Lean away from the raised arm while your partner gently guides your arm.
Keep your chest open and avoid leaning forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Come back to upright and switch sides.

exercises.name: lateral bend on floor by kneeling
exercises.description: A kneeling side bend where you reach along the floor to stretch the side of the waist.
steps: Kneel on a mat and extend one arm sideways along the floor.
Walk your hands to one side and sink your hips the other way until the side of the waist stretches.
Keep your hips over your knees.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: lateral stretch on floor lying down
exercises.description: A lying side stretch that gently lengthens one side of the body.
steps: Lie on your back with your arms extended overhead.
Shift your feet and your upper body to one side to form a gentle banana curve until the opposite side stretches.
Keep both shoulders and hips on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.name: weighted captain's chair leg raise
exercises.description: A captain's chair leg raise with added weight, building lower ab and hip flexor strength.
steps: Position yourself on a captain's chair with your forearms on the pads and back against the backrest.
Hold the weight securely between your feet or on your ankles.
Brace your core and raise your knees or legs up toward your chest.
Curl your pelvis slightly at the top.
Lower your legs slowly without swinging.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: weighted decline crunch
exercises.description: A decline bench crunch with a weight held at the chest, adding resistance for the abs.
steps: Lie on a decline bench and hook your feet under the pads.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Curl your upper body up by contracting the abs.
Pause briefly at the top without pulling on your neck.
Lower back down with control.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: farmers walk
exercises.description: A loaded carry holding a dumbbell in each hand while walking tall. Builds grip, core and total-body strength.
steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your sides.
Keep your back straight and your shoulders back.
Take small, controlled steps forward, maintaining an upright posture.
Continue walking for the desired distance or time.
To finish, stop walking and carefully lower the dumbbells to your sides.

exercises.name: weighted front plank
exercises.description: A forearm plank held with extra weight on your back. Builds core strength and stability.
steps: Start by lying face down on the floor.
Place your forearms on the ground, with your elbows directly under your shoulders.
Extend your legs straight out behind you, with your toes on the ground.
Engage your core and lift your body off the ground, balancing on your forearms and toes.
Keep your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.
Hold this position for the desired amount of time.
Lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell cuban press v. 2
exercises.description: A cuban press variation with dumbbells that mixes a press and a wrist rotation. Works the shoulders and rotator cuff.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing down.
Keeping your core engaged and your back straight, press the dumbbells straight up overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Rotate your wrists so that your palms are facing forward.
Lower the dumbbells back down to shoulder height, rotating your wrists back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell arnold press
exercises.description: A seated dumbbell press that rotates the palms from facing you to facing forward as you lift. Hits all three heads of the shoulder.
steps: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level, palms facing your body and elbows bent.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended and your palms are facing forward.
Rotate your wrists as you lift, so that your palms are facing forward at the top of the movement.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: stationary bike run v. 3
exercises.description: Steady pedalling on a stationary bike at a pace that suits you. Builds endurance and leg conditioning.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position to ensure proper alignment.
Place your feet on the pedals and secure them with the straps if available.
Start pedaling at a comfortable pace.
Maintain a steady rhythm and increase the resistance as desired.
Engage your core muscles to maintain stability and proper posture.
Continue pedaling for the desired duration of your workout.
Gradually decrease the resistance and slow down before coming to a complete stop.
Stretch your legs and cool down after the workout.

exercises.name: hands bike
exercises.description: Cranking pedals with your hands on an upper body ergometer. Gets your heart rate up using the arms and shoulders.
steps: Adjust the seat height and handlebar position to a comfortable level.
Sit on the ergometer with your back straight and feet on the pedals.
Grasp the handles with your hands and position your arms at a 90-degree angle.
Start pedaling with your hands, pushing and pulling the handles in a controlled motion.
Continue pedaling for the desired duration or number of repetitions.

exercises.name: walk wave machine
exercises.description: A low-impact cardio machine session that works the legs in a smooth walking motion to raise your heart rate.
steps: Step onto the machine and hold the handles lightly.
Start moving your legs in a smooth walking rhythm.
Keep your posture tall and your core lightly braced.
Pick a pace that lets you breathe steadily.
Keep going for 10-30 minutes depending on your fitness.
Slow down for the last minute before stepping off.

exercises.name: walk elliptical cross trainer
exercises.description: Smooth walking-style motion on an elliptical cross trainer. Low-impact cardio that builds endurance.
steps: Adjust the resistance level and incline of the elliptical machine to your desired settings.
Step onto the pedals of the machine and grip the handles lightly.
Begin by pushing down with your feet and pulling the handles towards your body.
Continue this motion, alternating between pushing and pulling, to simulate a walking or running motion.
Maintain a steady pace and keep your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Continue for the desired duration of your cardio workout.
Gradually decrease the intensity and speed of the machine before stepping off.

exercises.name: ski ergometer
exercises.description: Pulling the handles of a ski ergometer down in a rhythmic stroke. Works the arms, back and core while raising your heart rate.
steps: Adjust the seat height and footrests to a comfortable position.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Sit up straight with your feet flat on the footrests.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Engage your triceps and push the handles down towards your thighs.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell standing around world
exercises.description: Dumbbell circles around the body with straight arms, going out to the side and overhead. Works the shoulders through a wide range.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Extend your arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing down.
Keeping your arms straight, slowly rotate your arms in a circular motion, bringing the dumbbells in front of your body and then overhead.
Continue the circular motion, bringing the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: cable seated chest press
exercises.description: A seated cable press pushing the handles away from your chest. Builds the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Adjust the seat height and cable handles to a comfortable position.
Sit on the bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the cable handles with an overhand grip at shoulder height.
Push the handles forward and away from your body, extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bring the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever hip thrust
exercises.description: A machine version of the hip thrust that loads the glutes with a fixed path of motion.
steps: Sit on the machine with your upper back against the pad and the belt across your hips.
Plant your feet flat, about hip width apart.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your torso and thighs are in line.
Squeeze your glutes at the top for a moment.
Lower with control and repeat, keeping your chin tucked.

exercises.name: lever hip thrust with resistance band
exercises.description: A machine hip thrust with a band around the thighs, adding hip abductor work to the glute drive.
steps: Sit on the machine with your upper back on the pad and a band around your thighs above the knees.
Place your feet flat and push your knees gently out against the band.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your torso and thighs are in line.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat, keeping the knees pressed out.

exercises.name: lever single leg hip thrust
exercises.description: A one sided machine hip thrust that hits each glute on its own and challenges hip stability.
steps: Sit on the machine with your upper back on the pad and the belt across your hips.
Plant one foot flat and lift the other leg off the floor.
Drive through the planted heel and raise your hips until your torso is level.
Squeeze your glute at the top, keeping your hips level.
Lower with control, finish your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: resistance band bent leg kickback (kneeling)
exercises.description: A kneeling kickback with a band that isolates the glutes by pressing the bent leg up and back.
steps: Anchor the band low and loop it around one foot, then get on all fours.
Keep your back flat and your core braced.
Press the foot with the bent knee up toward the ceiling against the band.
Squeeze your glute at the top without arching your lower back.
Lower slowly, finish your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: resistance band clam
exercises.description: A side-lying clam with a band around the thighs that strengthens the outer hip and glutes.
steps: Lie on your side with a loop band just above your knees and knees bent.
Stack your hips and keep your feet together.
Open the top knee away from the bottom one like a clam.
Keep your pelvis still and do not roll backward.
Lower the knee slowly.
Complete the reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: resistance band external rotation
exercises.description: Rotates the arm outward against band tension to strengthen the small muscles that stabilise the shoulder.
steps: Anchor a band at elbow height and stand sideways to it.
Hold the handle with the hand farther from the anchor.
Tuck your elbow against your side with the elbow bent to 90 degrees.
Rotate your forearm outward, away from your belly.
Return slowly to the start.
Finish the reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: resistance band front plank with kicked leg
exercises.description: A plank hold while one leg kicks back against a band, working the glutes and core together.
steps: Place a band around your feet or ankles and get into a forearm or high plank.
Brace your core so your body forms a straight line.
Kick one leg back and up against the band without shifting your hips.
Return the leg with control.
Alternate legs, keeping your hips level throughout.

exercises.name: resistance band full squat
exercises.description: A deep squat with a band for added resistance, training the thighs and glutes.
steps: Stand on the band with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the handles at your shoulders.
Keep your chest up and your core braced.
Sit your hips back and down into a full squat.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes and heels on the floor.
Drive up through your feet to stand tall.

exercises.name: resistance band glute bridge
exercises.description: A floor bridge with a band around the thighs to keep the glutes working hard.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and a band around your thighs just above the knees.
Place your feet flat, hip width apart.
Push your knees gently out against the band.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
Squeeze your glutes, then lower slowly and repeat.

exercises.name: resistance band kneeling side plank
exercises.description: A side plank from the knees with a band, training the sides of the waist and the hips with less load than a full plank.
steps: Wrap a band around your thighs and lie on one side with your knees bent.
Place your elbow under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from knees to head.
Push your top knee gently out against the band.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: resistance band lying leg raise
exercises.description: A side lying leg raise against a band that works the outer hip and glutes.
steps: Place a band around your thighs or ankles and lie on your side with your legs straight.
Rest your head on your arm and keep your hips stacked.
Raise the top leg against the band without rolling backward.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly, finish your reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: resistance band one leg glute bridge with straight leg
exercises.description: A single leg bridge with a band and the free leg held straight, demanding strong glutes and a level pelvis.
steps: Lie on your back with a band around your thighs and one knee bent, foot flat.
Extend the other leg straight, in line with your thigh.
Drive through the planted heel and lift your hips.
Keep your hips level and squeeze your glute at the top.
Lower slowly, finish your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: resistance band one leg glute bridge
exercises.description: A single-leg glute bridge with a band added, making your glutes and hamstrings work harder on each side.
steps: Lie on your back with a loop band above your knees and knees bent.
Lift one foot off the floor and extend that leg.
Drive through the other heel and lift your hips.
Squeeze the glutes at the top and keep the hips level.
Lower with control.
Finish the reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: resistance band one leg kickback
exercises.description: A standing or all fours kickback with a band that targets the glutes one leg at a time.
steps: Loop a band around your ankles or anchor it and loop it around one foot.
Stand holding a support, or get on all fours, with your core braced.
Kick one leg back against the band, keeping the knee straight.
Squeeze your glute and avoid arching your lower back.
Return slowly, finish your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: resistance band plank march
exercises.description: Marching the knees while holding a plank with a band around the legs, which challenges the core and hips together.
steps: Place a loop band around your thighs or ankles and get into a forearm or high plank.
Keep a straight line from head to heels.
Lift one knee toward your chest against the band.
Return it quietly and lift the other knee.
Keep your hips from rocking side to side.
Alternate for the planned time or reps.

exercises.name: resistance band reverse hyperextension
exercises.description: Swings the legs up behind you against a band to train the glutes and the muscles along the lower back.
steps: Lie face down over a bench or box with a band anchored near your feet.
Hold the bench edge and loop the band around your ankles.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your legs until they are in line with your body.
Avoid swinging or arching the lower back.
Lower the legs slowly.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: resistance band side plank
exercises.description: A side plank with a band around the legs to fire up the hips and the sides of the waist.
steps: Place a band around your thighs and lie on one side with your legs straight.
Put your elbow under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Press your top leg gently up against the band.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: resistance band side walk
exercises.description: A lateral band walk that strengthens the outer hips and glutes.
steps: Place a band around your thighs or ankles and stand with your feet hip width apart.
Bend your knees slightly into a quarter squat.
Step sideways with the lead foot, keeping tension on the band.
Bring the trailing foot in without letting the feet touch.
Take 10-15 steps one way, then walk back the other way.

exercises.name: resistance band supine hip bridge march
exercises.description: A glute bridge held while you march your knees one at a time against a band, testing hip stability.
steps: Lie on your back with a band around your thighs and your knees bent.
Lift your hips into a bridge and squeeze your glutes.
Lift one foot off the floor, drawing the knee toward your chest.
Lower it and lift the other foot, keeping your hips level.
Continue alternating at a steady pace, then lower your hips.

exercises.name: ez barbell decline triceps extension
exercises.description: A decline EZ bar triceps extension lowering the bar toward your forehead. Builds triceps strength.
steps: Lie on a decline bench with your head lower than your feet and your feet secured.
Hold the ez barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms fully, keeping your elbows close to your head.
Lower the barbell slowly towards your forehead, bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell reverse close-grip bench press
exercises.description: A close-grip bench press using a reverse (underhand) grip. Emphasises the triceps and upper chest.
steps: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Grasp the barbell with a reverse grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell down towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause for a moment when the barbell is just above your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell seated triceps extension
exercises.description: A seated overhead extension with one dumbbell held in both hands. Builds the back of the upper arms.
steps: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up overhead.
Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your upper arms close to your ears.
Pause for a moment, then straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbells seated triceps extension
exercises.description: A seated overhead extension with one dumbbell held in both hands. Builds the back of the upper arms.
steps: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in both hands with an overhand grip, and raise it above your head.
Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your upper arms close to your ears.
Extend your arms and raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: elliptical machine walk
exercises.description: A steady, low-impact walk on the elliptical that builds endurance and works the legs without pounding the joints.
steps: Step onto the pedals and hold the handles.
Start walking forward in a smooth rhythm.
Stand tall and keep your shoulders relaxed.
Set a resistance and pace you can keep up while breathing steadily.
Continue for 15-45 minutes.
Slow down for a minute before you step off.

exercises.name: bicycle recline walk
exercises.description: A relaxed walking-style pedal motion on a recumbent bike that builds leg endurance with the back well supported.
steps: Sit on the recumbent bike and adjust the seat so your knees stay slightly bent at full extension.
Place your feet on the pedals and hold the handles.
Pedal at an easy, walking-like pace.
Keep your back against the backrest and breathe steadily.
Continue for 15-30 minutes.
Cool down by slowing the pedalling gradually.

exercises.name: run on treadmill
exercises.description: Running at a steady pace on a treadmill to build endurance and burn energy.
steps: Step onto the belt and clip the safety key to your clothing.
Start at a walk and raise the speed gradually to a comfortable jog.
Keep your chest tall and your arms swinging loosely at your sides.
Land softly under your hips and keep your steps quick.
Run for 10-30 minutes at a pace where you can still breathe steadily.
Slow to a walk for a few minutes to cool down.

exercises.name: lever triceps extension v. 3
exercises.description: A machine-based triceps extension that lets you load the back of the arm with a steady, guided path.
steps: Adjust the seat and sit with your upper arms on the pad.
Grip the handles with your elbows bent.
Press down by straightening your elbows.
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom.
Return slowly to the start without lifting your shoulders.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: roll hip thrust
exercises.description: A hip thrust done by rolling a ball under your body, which trains the glutes and challenges your balance.
steps: Lie on your back with your heels on a stability ball and your arms by your sides.
Brace your core and press your heels into the ball.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top for a second.
Lower your hips slowly without letting the ball drift away.
Repeat for the planned reps, keeping the ball steady.

exercises.name: roller hip stretch
exercises.description: A roller-assisted hip opener for the glutes. Helps loosen tight hips with a controlled rolling motion.
steps: Start by sitting on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Place the roller under your glutes, just above your knees.
Lean back and place your hands on the ground behind you for support.
Engage your glutes and slowly roll the roller forward, bending your knees and bringing them towards your chest.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, feeling a stretch in your glutes.
Slowly roll the roller back to the starting position, extending your legs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: roller seated shoulder flexor depresor retractor
exercises.description: A seated roller drill that rolls forward and back to work shoulder control. Helps with shoulder mobility and posture.
steps: Sit on a flat surface with your legs extended in front of you.
Hold the roller with both hands, palms facing down, and place it on your thighs.
Lean forward slightly and roll the roller away from your body, extending your arms straight in front of you.
Pause for a moment, then slowly roll the roller back towards your body, bending your arms and bringing the roller back to your thighs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: roller body saw
exercises.description: A plank with forearms on a roller, rolling forward and back like a saw. Challenges the abs and core.
steps: Start in a plank position with your forearms on the roller and your body in a straight line.
Engage your core and slowly roll the roller forward, extending your body as far as you can while maintaining control.
Pause for a moment at the furthest point, then slowly roll the roller back towards your starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: roller hip lat stretch
exercises.description: A kneeling roller stretch that opens the hips and glutes. Helps release tension around the hips.
steps: Start by kneeling on the ground with the roller positioned under your hips.
Place your hands on the roller for support.
Slowly roll the roller forward, extending your hips and stretching your glutes.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then roll back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: roller reverse crunch
exercises.description: A reverse crunch where you roll a roller toward you with your feet. Trains the lower abs.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your arms extended straight above your head and your legs straight out in front of you.
Place the roller between your feet and grip it with your toes.
Engaging your abs, lift your legs off the ground and curl your knees towards your chest, rolling the roller towards your body.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position, rolling the roller away from your body.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: roller side lat stretch
exercises.description: A roller stretch that reaches forward to lengthen the sides of your back. Helps loosen the lats.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the roller with both hands in front of your body.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Extend your arms forward and roll the roller down towards your feet, feeling a stretch in your lats.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly roll the roller back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: roller back stretch
exercises.description: Rolling your back over a roller to loosen it up. Helps ease stiffness along the spine.
steps: Start by sitting on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Place the roller perpendicular to your body, just below your glutes.
Slowly roll your body backwards, allowing the roller to move up your back.
Continue rolling until the roller reaches your upper back.
Pause for a moment, then slowly roll back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: roller seated single leg shoulder flexor depresor retractor
exercises.description: A seated single-leg roller drill for shoulder control. Helps with shoulder mobility and posture.
steps: Sit on a flat surface with your legs extended in front of you.
Hold the roller with both hands, palms facing down, and place it on your thighs.
Lean back slightly and engage your core muscles.
Raise the roller up to shoulder level, keeping your arms straight.
Slowly lower the roller back down to your thighs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: sled 45 degrees leg press
exercises.description: A leg press on a 45 degree sled that loads the thighs and hips while your back stays supported.
steps: Sit in the seat with your back and head flat against the pad.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Release the safety handles and lower the sled until your knees are bent to about 90 degrees.
Keep your lower back pressed into the pad as you descend.
Push through your whole foot to extend your legs without locking your knees.
Lower under control and repeat.

exercises.name: dumbbell standing lateral raise
exercises.description: Raising dumbbells out to your sides to build the middle part of the shoulders.
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and brace your core.
Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lead with your elbows and avoid shrugging.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly to the start and repeat.

exercises.name: cable triceps pushdown (v bar)
exercises.description: A cable pushdown with a V bar that isolates the back of the upper arm.
steps: Attach a V bar to a high pulley and stand facing the stack.
Grip the bar with your elbows pinned to your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Squeeze your triceps for a moment at the bottom.
Let the bar rise until your forearms are just past parallel.
Keep your upper arms still throughout the set.

exercises.name: walking
exercises.description: Plain walking at an easy to brisk pace, a simple way to build endurance and stay active.
steps: Stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and your gaze ahead.
Start walking with a natural stride.
Swing your arms gently opposite to your legs.
Land softly on your heel and roll through to the toes.
Keep a pace that lets you breathe comfortably.
Walk for 20-60 minutes.

exercises.name: walking on treadmill
exercises.description: Walking on a treadmill lets you control speed and incline for steady, low-impact cardio.
steps: Step onto the belt and hold the rails while you start at a slow speed.
Increase to a comfortable walking pace.
Let go of the rails and swing your arms naturally.
Keep your head up and your steps even.
Add some incline if you want more challenge.
Walk for 20-45 minutes and slow down before stepping off.

exercises.name: lever seated row v. 2
exercises.description: A plate-loaded seated row that trains the upper back and lats through a guided pulling path.
steps: Adjust the seat and chest pad, then sit with your chest against the pad.
Grip the handles with arms extended.
Pull the handles toward your torso by driving the elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly until your arms are straight again.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: lever back extension v. 2
exercises.description: A machine back extension that strengthens the muscles along the lower back with support from the pad.
steps: Adjust the machine and sit with your back against the pad.
Cross your arms or hold the handles as the machine allows.
Push back by extending at the hips and lower back.
Stop when your torso is in a neutral, tall position.
Return slowly to the start.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: lever seated leg press
exercises.description: A seated machine leg press that drives the legs forward to build thigh and glute strength with back support.
steps: Adjust the seat and sit with your back flat against the pad.
Place your feet on the platform about shoulder-width apart.
Push through your heels until your legs are nearly straight.
Do not lock your knees.
Bend your knees slowly to return.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: lever seated crunch (hands pad)
exercises.description: A seated machine crunch where the hands press on a pad, working the abs against steady resistance.
steps: Sit on the machine and adjust the seat so your hands reach the pad.
Place your hands on the pads and brace your feet.
Curl your torso forward by contracting your abs.
Pause briefly at the bottom.
Return slowly to the upright start.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: ab roller crunch
exercises.description: A crunch done with an ab wheel that works the abdominal wall through a compact range.
steps: Kneel on a mat and hold the ab wheel with both hands in front of your knees.
Round your lower back slightly and brace your abs.
Roll forward a short distance while keeping your hips stable.
Pull the wheel back toward your knees by curling your ribs toward your hips.
Exhale as you crunch and avoid arching your back.
Repeat with smooth control.

exercises.name: left hook. boxing
exercises.description: A boxing left hook thrown with a hip and torso rotation. Builds rotational power and conditioning.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Keep your left hand up to protect your face and your right hand by your chin.
Rotate your hips and pivot on your left foot as you extend your left arm forward in a punching motion.
Twist your torso and engage your core muscles to generate power in the punch.
Snap your arm back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: boxing jab
exercises.description: A quick straight punch with the lead hand, used to build speed, shoulder endurance and timing.
steps: Stand in a boxing stance with your lead foot forward and hands up by your chin.
Extend your lead hand straight toward the target.
Rotate your fist so the palm faces down as it lands.
Keep your chin tucked and your rear hand guarding.
Snap the hand back to the guard quickly.
Repeat, then switch stance if you want.

exercises.name: boxing right cross
exercises.description: A powerful straight punch with the rear hand, driven by a turn of the hips and back foot.
steps: Stand in a boxing stance with hands up.
Push off the back foot and rotate your hips and shoulders.
Throw your rear hand straight toward the target.
Keep your lead hand up to protect your chin.
Pull the hand back along the same line.
Return to your stance and repeat.

exercises.name: boxing right uppercut
exercises.description: A rising punch with the right hand aimed upward, using leg drive and a hip turn.
steps: Stand in a boxing stance with hands up.
Bend your knees slightly and dip your right side.
Drive up through your legs as you rotate your hips.
Throw your right fist upward with the palm facing you.
Keep your left hand guarding your chin.
Return to stance and repeat.

exercises.name: boxing left uppercut
exercises.description: A rising punch with the left hand, thrown upward from the hips and legs.
steps: Stand in a boxing stance with hands up.
Bend your knees slightly and dip your left side.
Drive up through your legs as you rotate your hips.
Throw your left fist upward with the palm facing you.
Keep your right hand guarding your chin.
Return to stance and repeat.

exercises.name: lever lying crunch
exercises.description: A machine crunch performed lying back, letting you load the abs while the lower back stays supported.
steps: Lie back on the machine and place your hands or arms as indicated.
Hook your feet or grip the handles for stability.
Curl your torso up by contracting your abs.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly back to the start.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: lever chest press v. 4
exercises.description: A plate-loaded chest press that trains the pecs and triceps along a guided path.
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at mid-chest height.
Sit back with your shoulder blades pulled together.
Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Do not lock your elbows.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch in the chest.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: lever decline chest press v. 2
exercises.description: A decline-angle machine press that emphasises the lower part of the chest.
steps: Adjust the seat and sit with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles with elbows bent.
Press forward and slightly downward until your arms are almost straight.
Keep your shoulders down and your chest up.
Return slowly under control.
Repeat for the planned reps.

exercises.name: stationary bike run v. 4
exercises.description: A stationary bike session at a brisk pace, similar to running in effort, to build heart and leg endurance.
steps: Adjust the seat so your knees stay slightly bent at the bottom of the stroke.
Hold the handles and sit tall.
Start pedalling at an easy pace to warm up.
Raise the speed to a brisk rhythm you can sustain.
Keep your upper body relaxed.
Continue for 10-30 minutes, then slow down to cool off.

exercises.name: lever neck extension (plate loaded)
exercises.description: A plate-loaded machine movement that strengthens the muscles at the back of the neck.
steps: Set the weight light and adjust the pad to rest on the back of your head.
Sit tall and bring your chin slightly down.
Press your head back against the pad slowly.
Move only through a comfortable range.
Return slowly to the start.
Repeat for the planned reps with control.

exercises.name: lever neck left side flexion (plate loaded)
exercises.description: A plate-loaded neck exercise that bends the head sideways to the left to strengthen the side neck muscles.
steps: Set the weight light and position the pad against the left side of your head.
Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Tilt your head to the left against the resistance.
Keep the movement small and smooth.
Return slowly to the centre.
Repeat for the planned reps with control.

exercises.name: lever neck right side flexion (plate loaded)
exercises.description: A plate-loaded neck exercise that bends the head sideways to the right to strengthen the side neck muscles.
steps: Set the weight light and position the pad against the right side of your head.
Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Tilt your head to the right against the resistance.
Keep the movement small and smooth.
Return slowly to the centre.
Repeat for the planned reps with control.

exercises.name: lever pullover
exercises.description: A machine pullover that sweeps the handles toward you. Works the lats with a long range of motion.
steps: Adjust the seat and handles of the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and grasp the handles with an overhand grip.
Keep your arms slightly bent and your core engaged.
Slowly pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your lats.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever hip extension v. 2
exercises.description: A machine hip extension that drives your leg back against resistance. Targets the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Adjust the machine to fit your body and sit on it with your back against the backrest.
Place your feet on the footrests and grip the handles for stability.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings, then push against the footrests to extend your hips and raise your legs backward.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever alternate leg press
exercises.description: A machine leg press done one leg at a time, alternating. Builds the quads and glutes.
steps: Adjust the seat and foot platform of the leverage machine to your desired position.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet on the foot platform.
Place your hands on the handles or sides of the machine for stability.
Push one foot against the foot platform, extending your leg until it is almost fully straight.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bend your leg and return to the starting position.
Repeat with the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever gripper hands
exercises.description: A machine gripper where you squeeze the handles closed. Strengthens the forearms and grip.
steps: Adjust the seat height and grip the handles of the leverage machine.
Keep your back straight and your feet flat on the ground.
Exhale and squeeze the handles, contracting your forearms.
Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly release and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever calf press
exercises.description: A machine calf press pushing the pad with your toes. Builds the calf muscles.
steps: Adjust the seat of the leverage machine so that your shoulders are aligned with the lever pad.
Place your toes on the lever pad, with your heels hanging off the edge.
Grasp the handles or side supports for stability.
Push the lever pad down by extending your ankles, contracting your calf muscles.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position by allowing your heels to rise back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell bulgarian split squat
exercises.description: A single-leg squat with the back foot raised, building leg strength and balance.
steps: Stand a stride length in front of a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Rest the top of your back foot on the bench.
Lower straight down until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee tracking over your toes.
Drive through your front heel to stand back up.
Finish all reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: cable wide grip lat pulldown
exercises.description: A pulldown with a wide grip that builds the broad muscles of the upper back.
steps: Sit at the pulldown station and secure your thighs under the pads.
Grab the bar with a wide overhand grip.
Lean back slightly and pull the bar down to your upper chest.
Drive your elbows down and back, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Control the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
Avoid swinging your torso.

exercises.name: dumbbell rear delt raise
exercises.description: A bent-over dumbbell raise to the sides. Trains the rear delts and upper back.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Raise your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until they are parallel to the floor.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell standing zottman preacher curl
exercises.description: A standing zottman curl against a preacher bench, curling up then turning your palms down to lower. Works the biceps and forearms.
steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Place your upper arms against the preacher bench and keep your elbows slightly bent.
Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders while keeping your upper arms stationary.
At the top of the movement, rotate your wrists so that your palms are facing downward.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, rotating your wrists back to the starting position as well.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: dumbbell zottman preacher curl
exercises.description: A seated zottman curl on a preacher bench, curling up then turning your palms down to lower. Works the biceps and forearms.
steps: Sit on a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up and elbows resting on the pad.
Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms stationary and your palms facing up.
At the top of the curl, rotate your wrists so that your palms are facing down.
