Set the kettlebell down with a flat back.

exercises.name: dumbbell farmers carry
exercises.description: Walking while holding a heavy dumbbell in each hand. It builds grip strength, traps and overall posture.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and stand tall.
Pull your shoulders back and down and brace your abs.
Walk with quick, controlled steps without swinging the weights.
Cover the set distance, then lower the dumbbells safely.

exercises.name: barbell suitcase carry
exercises.description: Carrying a barbell off to one side with a single-handed grip. It trains your trunk to resist leaning and builds grip.
steps: Stand with the barbell at your side and grip it near its center of balance.
Lift it while keeping your torso tall and level.
Walk with steady steps and resist tilting toward the weight.
Cover the set distance, then lower the bar carefully.
Switch hands and repeat.

exercises.name: smith hex press
exercises.description: A press with the weights squeezed together, done on a Smith machine. The squeeze keeps tension on the chest throughout.
steps: Lie on a bench under the Smith bar and hold a weight plate between your palms if you like.
Unrack the bar with a close grip and hold it over your chest.
Squeeze your hands inward as you lower the bar to your mid chest.
Press back up while still squeezing.
Rerack the bar when done.

exercises.name: single leg bodyweight deadlift with arm and leg extended
exercises.description: A single-leg hinge with your arms extended that trains hamstrings, glutes and balance.
steps: Stand on one leg with arms reaching forward.
Soften your standing knee slightly.
Hinge at the hips as your free leg lifts behind you.
Keep your back flat and body in a long line.
Return to standing and repeat, then switch legs.

exercises.name: pike push up
exercises.description: A push-up with hips lifted high so you press more overhead. It builds shoulder strength using only your body weight.
steps: Start in a push-up position, then walk your feet in and lift your hips into an inverted V.
Keep your arms and back straight.
Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your core tight throughout.

exercises.name: bodyweight standing biceps curl
exercises.description: A curl done with your own body resistance, such as pushing one hand against the other. It is a simple way to train the biceps without equipment.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Place one hand under the wrist of your other hand to give resistance.
Curl the working hand toward your shoulder while the other hand pushes down.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Lower slowly, finish the reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: cable side lying lateral raise
exercises.description: A lateral raise performed while lying on your side with a cable. Lying down keeps constant tension on the side delt.
steps: Lie on your side next to a low cable pulley and grab the handle with your top hand.
Keep your arm straight with a slight bend in the elbow.
Raise your arm out to the side until it is near shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly, finish the reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: dumbbell single leg step up
exercises.description: Stepping up onto a bench with one leg while holding dumbbells. It builds single-leg strength in the quads and glutes.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand facing a box or bench.
Place one foot fully on the box.
Drive through that heel to stand up tall.
Lower back down under control without bouncing off the floor foot.
Finish the reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: x band side walk
exercises.description: Stepping sideways against a band anchored in an X pattern. It fires up the hips and outer glutes.
steps: Cross the band into an X and place it around your feet or lower legs, holding the ends as needed.
Stand in a quarter squat with your chest up.
Step sideways, keeping tension on the band.
Bring the trailing foot in without letting your feet touch.
Walk the set distance, then return the other way.

exercises.name: kettlebell kneeling one arm bottoms up press
exercises.description: Pressing a kettlebell held upside down from a kneeling position. The unstable load demands shoulder control and grip.
steps: Kneel on both knees and hold a kettlebell bottoms up at shoulder height.
Squeeze the handle tight and keep your wrist straight.
Press the bell straight overhead.
Lower slowly to your shoulder, keeping the bell balanced.
Finish the reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: barbell overhead shrug
exercises.description: A shrug done with the barbell locked out overhead. It targets the traps and helps with overhead stability.
steps: Hold a barbell locked out overhead with a wide grip.
Keep your arms straight and your ribs down.
Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly without bending your elbows.

exercises.name: kneeling battling ropes
exercises.description: Making waves with heavy ropes while kneeling. It raises your heart rate and burns the shoulders and arms.
steps: Kneel in front of the anchored ropes and hold an end in each hand.
Brace your abs and keep your chest up.
Raise and lower your arms alternately to create waves.
Keep the waves quick and steady.
Work for a set time, then rest.

exercises.name: resistance band pullapart (supination at 90 degrees)
exercises.description: A band pull-apart with palms facing up and elbows bent at 90 degrees. It targets the rear delts and external shoulder rotation.
steps: Hold a band in front of you at chest height with palms up and elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Keep your elbows tucked near your sides.
Rotate your forearms outward, pulling the band apart.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together briefly.
Return slowly and repeat.

exercises.name: shoulder flexion back to wall
exercises.description: Raising your arms overhead while your back stays against a wall. It improves shoulder mobility and posture.
steps: Stand with your back, head and hips against a wall.
Keep your arms at your sides with elbows straight.
Raise your arms forward and up overhead as far as you can without arching your back.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat.

exercises.name: kettlebell kneeling one arm shoulder press
exercises.description: A one-arm kettlebell press from a kneeling position. Kneeling takes the legs out of it and challenges your trunk.
steps: Kneel on both knees with a kettlebell racked at your shoulder.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs.
Press the kettlebell overhead until your arm is straight.
Lower it slowly back to your shoulder.
Finish the reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: rear lunge with battling ropes
exercises.description: Alternating rear lunges while making waves with heavy ropes. It combines leg work with a hard cardio effort.
steps: Stand holding the ends of the battle ropes, feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back into a lunge while making a wave with the ropes.
Push through your front heel to return to standing.
Alternate legs, keeping the rope waves going.
Work for a set time, then rest.

exercises.name: kettlebell half kneeling shoulder press
exercises.description: A one-arm kettlebell press from a half-kneeling stance. The position teaches hip stability while you press.
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward and a kettlebell racked at your shoulder.
Brace your abs and squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg.
Press the bell straight overhead.
Lower it back under control.
Finish the reps, then switch sides.

exercises.name: half kneeling pvc pec mobilization stretch
exercises.description: A chest opener using a PVC pipe from a half-kneeling position. It loosens tight pecs and the front of the shoulder.
steps: Kneel on one knee and grip a pipe or stick with one hand while the other arm reaches out.
Place the working forearm against a wall or post.
Gently rotate your torso away until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Switch sides.

exercises.name: rocking ankle stretch
exercises.description: Rocking forward over a bent knee to open the ankle and calf. It helps ankle mobility for squats and walking.
steps: Kneel on one knee with the front foot flat on the floor.
Keep your front heel down.
Rock your front knee forward over your toes until you feel a stretch.
Rock back and forth slowly for 20-30 seconds.
Switch legs.

exercises.name: stability ball rounded rollout
exercises.description: A rollout on a stability ball with a rounded back that trains the abs hard.
steps: Kneel in front of a stability ball with forearms on top.
Round your back slightly and tuck your pelvis.
Roll the ball forward by extending your arms.
Pull it back using your abs.
Keep your hips from sagging and move slowly.

exercises.name: band upper body resistance dead bug
exercises.description: A dead bug with a band resisting your arms. It adds shoulder and trunk demand to a classic core drill.
steps: Lie on your back holding a band overhead and bring your knees up at 90 degrees.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Lower the opposite arm and leg while keeping band tension.
Return to the start and switch sides.
Keep your ribs down and move slowly.

exercises.name: kettlebell around head rotation
exercises.description: Circling a kettlebell around your head, also called a halo. It loosens the shoulders and warms up the upper back.
steps: Hold a kettlebell by the horns at chest height.
Stand tall with your abs braced.
Circle the bell around your head, keeping it close.
Keep your hips and ribs still.
Finish the reps, then reverse direction.

exercises.name: prone single arm trap raise
exercises.description: A raise lying face down on a bench or floor with one arm. It targets the lower and middle traps and shoulder blade control.
steps: Lie face down with one arm hanging or reaching overhead, thumb up.
Keep your forehead down and neck relaxed.
Lift your arm in a Y shape by squeezing your shoulder blade down and back.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly, finish the reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: forearm wall slide
exercises.description: Sliding your forearms up a wall to wake up the shoulder blade muscles. It improves overhead movement.
steps: Stand facing a wall with your forearms on it, elbows at shoulder height.
Lean in slightly and keep your abs braced.
Slide your forearms up the wall as you reach upward.
Pause at the top without arching your back.
Slide back down and repeat.

exercises.name: kettlebell angled press
exercises.description: A kettlebell press at an angle between a front and a side raise path. It suits natural shoulder movement and builds pressing strength.
steps: Hold a kettlebell at your shoulder and stand tall.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bell up and slightly out to the side in a diagonal path.
Lock out your arm without leaning back.
Lower under control, finish the reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: resistance band spider crawls
exercises.description: A spider crawl performed with a band around your legs. The band adds hip effort to a classic core and shoulder crawl.
steps: Place a band around your thighs and start in a push-up position.
Brace your core.
Bring one knee toward the same-side elbow while crawling forward.
Alternate sides while keeping the band under tension.
Crawl the set distance, then rest.

exercises.name: seal push up
exercises.description: A push-up where your hands lift off the floor and reach out at the top. It builds chest and back strength together.
steps: Lie face down with your hands under your shoulders and legs straight.
Push your upper body up with your arms like a seal.
Keep your hips on the floor and your core tight.
Lower slowly to the floor.
Repeat for smooth, controlled reps.

exercises.name: scapular slide back to wall
exercises.description: Sliding your shoulder blades along a wall to improve their control. It helps shoulder blade mobility and posture.
steps: Stand with your back flat against a wall and your elbows bent at your sides.
Press your forearms and head lightly into the wall.
Slide your arms up the wall while keeping your shoulder blades down.
Stop before your back arches.
Slide down slowly and repeat.

exercises.name: single arm scapula push up
exercises.description: A small push-up movement with one arm that moves only the shoulder blades. It builds control of the serratus anterior.
steps: Start in a plank with one hand on the floor, the other behind your back or on your hip.
Keep your elbow locked straight.
Let your chest sink slightly between your shoulder blades.
Push the floor away to round your upper back slightly.
Finish the reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: roll anterior calf foam rolling
exercises.description: Rolling the front of the lower leg on a foam roller. It can loosen the muscles beside your shin.
steps: Kneel on the floor and place the roller under the front of your shin.
Support yourself with your hands on the floor.
Roll slowly up and down the shin muscle.
Pause on tight spots for a few seconds.
Switch legs and keep the pressure comfortable.

exercises.name: roll pec foam rolling
exercises.description: Rolling the chest on a foam roller. It can loosen tight pecs before pressing or after desk work.
steps: Lie face down and place the roller under one side of your chest.
Extend that arm out to the side.
Roll slowly side to side and up and down.
Pause on tight spots for a few seconds.
Switch sides and keep the pressure comfortable.

exercises.name: roll lat foam rolling
exercises.description: Rolling the side of your back on a foam roller. It can loosen tight lats before overhead work.
steps: Lie on your side with the roller under your armpit area and your arm extended.
Support yourself with your lower arm and legs.
Roll slowly along your side toward the ribs.
Pause on tight spots for a few seconds.
Switch sides and keep the pressure comfortable.

exercises.name: lever belt squat
exercises.description: A squat on a machine where the weight hangs from a belt at your hips. It loads the legs without stressing your spine.
steps: Step into the belt and stand on the platforms with the belt snug on your hips.
Stand tall and brace your abs.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel.
Push through your heels to stand back up.
Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.

exercises.name: lever horizontal leg press
exercises.description: A leg press on a horizontal lever machine. It builds the quads and glutes with back support.
steps: Sit on the machine with your back flat against the pad and feet on the platform.
Set your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Press the platform away until your legs are nearly straight.
Do not lock your knees.
Lower slowly until your knees are bent about 90 degrees and repeat.

exercises.name: smith kneeling rear kick (with partner)
exercises.description: A kneeling glute kick using a Smith machine with a partner helping. It works the glutes with a steady guided path.
steps: Get on all fours and place the sole of one foot on the Smith bar, with your partner steadying you if needed.
Brace your core.
Press the bar up by extending your hip.
Squeeze your glute at the top.
Lower slowly, finish the reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: cable standing reverse grip curl (straight bar)
exercises.description: A standing curl with an overhand grip on a straight cable bar. It targets the forearms and brachialis.
steps: Stand facing a low cable with a straight bar in an overhand grip.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders without swinging.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.

exercises.name: dumbbell goblet split squat front foot elevated
exercises.description: A goblet split squat with the front foot on a raised platform. The extra height deepens the range for the quads and glutes.
steps: Hold one dumbbell at your chest and place your front foot on a low platform.
Place your back foot behind you on the floor.
Lower your back knee toward the floor with your torso upright.
Push through your front heel to stand.
Finish the reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: dumbbell split squat front foot elevated
exercises.description: A split squat holding dumbbells at your sides with the front foot raised. It deepens the range for the quads and glutes.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and place your front foot on a low platform.
Step your back foot behind you.
Lower your back knee toward the floor with your torso upright.
Push through your front heel to stand.
Finish the reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: dumbbell split squat
exercises.description: A stationary lunge with dumbbells at your sides. It strengthens one leg at a time, mainly the quads and glutes.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and take a long stance, one foot forward.
Keep your torso upright.
Lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push through your front heel to stand.
Finish the reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: plank push up row
exercises.description: A plank sequence combining a push-up and a row. It trains the chest, back and core in one flowing move.
steps: Start in a plank with a dumbbell in each hand and your feet wide.
Do a push-up, keeping your body straight.
Row one dumbbell up to your ribs without twisting your hips.
Lower it and row the other side.
Repeat the sequence with control.

exercises.name: lever seated hammer grip shoulder press
exercises.description: A seated machine shoulder press with a neutral hammer grip. It trains the delts with a joint-friendly hand position.
steps: Sit with your back against the pad and grip the neutral handles.
Keep your feet flat on the floor.
Press the handles overhead until your arms are almost straight.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly to shoulder height and repeat.

exercises.name: captains chair straight leg raise
exercises.description: A straight leg raise on a captain's chair, lifting your legs in front of you. Works the abs and hip flexors.
steps: Sit on the captain's chair with your back against the backrest and your forearms resting on the arm pads.
Keep your upper body stable and your back straight.
Engage your abs and lift your legs up in front of you, keeping them straight.
Continue lifting until your legs are parallel to the ground or as high as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell glute bridge (hands on bar)
exercises.description: A glute bridge with the barbell resting on your hips and your hands on the bar. It builds the glutes and hamstrings with load.
steps: Sit on the floor with a barbell over your hips, padded if needed.
Roll back, set your feet, and hold the bar with both hands.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat.

exercises.name: dumbbell front squat
exercises.description: A squat with dumbbells held at your shoulders. The front load keeps your chest upright and challenges the quads and core.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your shoulders, elbows forward.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel.
Keep your chest up and knees tracking your toes.
Drive through your heels to stand.

exercises.name: dumbbell thruster
exercises.description: A front squat that flows into an overhead press. It is a hard whole-body move that raises your heart rate.
steps: Hold dumbbells at your shoulders and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down with your chest up.
Drive up through your heels and press the dumbbells overhead in one motion.
Lock out your arms at the top.
Lower the weights to your shoulders and go straight into the next rep.

exercises.name: dumbbell thruster v. 2
exercises.description: A squat into overhead press with dumbbells that works the legs and shoulders in one flow.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your shoulders.
Squat down with your chest tall and knees tracking over your toes.
Drive up through your heels as you stand.
Use that momentum to press the dumbbells overhead.
Lower them to your shoulders and go into the next squat.

exercises.name: band thruster
exercises.description: A squat into an overhead press using a band for resistance. It trains the legs, shoulders and heart in one move.
steps: Stand on the band and hold the ends at your shoulders.
Squat down with your chest up.
Drive up and press your hands overhead in one motion.
Lock out your arms at the top.
Lower your hands to your shoulders and repeat.

exercises.name: side lunge
exercises.description: Stepping out to the side into a deep lunge. It works the quads and glutes while opening the inner thighs.
steps: Stand tall with your feet together and hands in front of your chest.
Step wide to one side.
Bend that knee and sit your hips back, keeping the other leg straight.
Push off the bent leg to return.
Alternate sides.

exercises.name: lever one arm chest press (plate loaded)
exercises.description: A single-arm chest press on a plate-loaded machine. It lets each side work on its own.
steps: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and grip one handle.
Set your feet flat on the floor.
Press the handle forward until your arm is nearly straight.
Pause briefly.
Return slowly, finish the reps, then switch arms.

exercises.name: landmine squat and press
exercises.description: A squat that flows into a press with a landmine bar. It works legs and shoulders in one smooth motion.
steps: Hold the end of the landmine bar at your chest with both hands.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down with your chest up.
Drive up and press the bar away until your arms are straight.
Lower the bar to your chest and repeat.

exercises.name: elbow up and down dynamic plank
exercises.description: Moving between a forearm plank and a high plank, one arm at a time. It builds the core and shoulders under constant tension.
steps: Start in a forearm plank with your body in a straight line.
Place one hand on the floor and press up to a high plank.
Place the other hand down.
Lower back to your forearms one arm at a time.
Alternate the leading arm and keep your hips still.

exercises.name: dumbbell renegade row
exercises.description: A row from a plank position with dumbbells. It builds the back while your core fights rotation.
steps: Start in a high plank with a dumbbell in each hand and your feet wide.
Brace your core.
Row one dumbbell to your ribs without twisting your hips.
Lower it with control.
Repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: dumbbell alternating floor press
exercises.description: A floor press where you press one dumbbell at a time. It trains the chest and triceps with a limited range for the shoulders.
steps: Lie on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand and knees bent.
Press both dumbbells up over your chest.
Lower one dumbbell until your upper arm touches the floor.
Press it back up and lower the other side.
Keep alternating.

exercises.name: pistol squat to box
exercises.description: A single-leg squat down to a box. The box gives you a target for depth as you build strength.
steps: Stand in front of a box with one leg extended forward.
Brace your core and reach your arms forward for balance.
Sit back and down slowly on the standing leg until you touch the box.
Drive through your heel to stand.
Finish the reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: weighted hammer grip pull up on dip cage
exercises.description: A weighted pull-up with a neutral hammer grip on a dip cage. It builds the lats and arms with extra load.
steps: Attach a belt or vest with weight and grip the neutral handles of the cage.
Hang with your arms straight and your core braced.
Pull your chest up until your chin passes the handles.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly to a full hang and repeat.

exercises.name: weighted close grip chin-up on dip cage
exercises.description: A weighted close-grip chin-up on a dip cage. Builds the lats, biceps and upper back.
steps: Stand in front of the dip cage and grab the parallel bars with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bars with your arms fully extended, feet off the ground, and body straight.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bars, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bars, then pause for a moment.
Slowly lower your body back down to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: squat mobility
exercises.description: A deep squat hold and rock that opens the hips and ankles.
steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder width.
Sink into a deep squat, keeping your heels down.
Press your elbows gently against your knees.
Rock side to side and sit tall.
Spend 30-45 seconds there, then stand up.

exercises.name: squat mobility complex
exercises.description: A short flow of deep squat positions that opens up the hips, knees and ankles. Good as a warm-up before leg work.
steps: Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder width and toes turned out slightly.
Sink into a deep squat and keep your heels on the floor.
Press your elbows against your knees to open the hips and hold for a moment.
Shift gently from side to side, then rock forward and back.
Stand up tall and repeat the flow for 6-8 rounds.
Keep your chest lifted and your back long throughout.

exercises.name: barbell walk calves activation
exercises.description: Walking on the balls of your feet with a barbell on your back to wake up the calves before heavy lower body training.
steps: Rest a light barbell across your upper back and hold it with both hands.
Stand tall with your core braced and rise onto the balls of your feet.
Walk forward in small, controlled steps without letting your heels drop.
Keep your ankles steady and your hips level.
Walk 10-15 metres, rest, then repeat for a few rounds.
Use a light load so you can stay high on your toes.

exercises.name: rollball seated single leg shoulder flexor depressor retractor
exercises.description: A seated shoulder control drill on a ball with one leg lifted. It challenges balance while you raise, lower and pull back the shoulder blades.
steps: Sit tall on a stability ball with your feet on the floor.
Lift one foot slightly off the ground and hold your balance.
Raise your arms forward, then press your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull your shoulder blades back and together without arching your back.
Return slowly to the start and complete your reps.
Switch legs and repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: calf self massage with barbell
exercises.description: A self-massage for the calves using a barbell to roll over tight spots.
steps: Sit on the floor with one calf resting on a barbell.
Support yourself with your hands behind you.
Roll your calf slowly back and forth over the bar.
Pause on tender spots for a few breaths.
Switch to the other leg.

exercises.name: kettlebell goblet squat mobility
exercises.description: A goblet squat held low with a kettlebell as a counterweight, used to loosen the hips and ankles.
steps: Hold a kettlebell by the horns against your chest.
Stand with your feet wider than your shoulders and toes slightly out.
Squat down as deep as you comfortably can with your chest up.
Use your elbows to push your knees out and pause at the bottom.
Rock gently side to side to open the hips.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.

exercises.name: self anterior calf foam rolling
exercises.description: A foam roller technique for the front of the lower leg that eases tightness.
steps: Kneel on a mat with the foam roller under your shins.
Support yourself with your hands in front.
Shift your weight to roll along the front of your lower leg.
Move slowly and pause on tight spots.
Roll for 30-60 seconds per leg.

exercises.name: band single arm shoulder press
exercises.description: A one-arm overhead press against a band. It trains the shoulders and makes your core resist twisting.
steps: Stand on the band with your feet hip width apart and hold the other end at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your ribs down.
Press the hand straight overhead until your arm is almost straight.
Lower under control back to your shoulder.
Complete your reps without leaning sideways.
Switch arms and repeat.

exercises.name: band assisted pull up v. 3
exercises.description: A pull-up where a band under your foot or knee takes some of your weight, so you can build up to full reps.
steps: Loop a band over the pull-up bar and place a foot or knee in it.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Hang with your arms long and your shoulders engaged.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight again.
Use a thinner band as you get stronger.

exercises.name: seated ankle stretch
exercises.description: A gentle seated stretch for the front of the ankle and shin that eases stiffness after sitting or training.
steps: Sit on a chair or the floor with one leg extended.
Point your toes away from you so the top of the foot lengthens.
Slowly circle or press the foot until you feel a comfortable stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without forcing it.
Release and switch legs.
Repeat 2-3 times on each side.

exercises.name: resistance band standing back achilles stretch
exercises.description: A calf and Achilles stretch with a band that gently pulls the toes toward you while the leg is behind you.
steps: Loop a resistance band around the front of the foot of your back leg.
Hold the band ends in your hands and stand tall.
Step that leg back with the heel on the floor.
Pull the band gently so your toes move toward your shin.
Hold for 20-30 seconds with your back leg fairly straight.
Switch sides and repeat.

exercises.name: resistance band standing forward achilles stretch
exercises.description: A standing calf stretch with a band around the forward foot, pulling the toes back to lengthen the Achilles area.
steps: Loop a resistance band around the ball of your front foot.
Hold the band ends and stand tall.
Place the front heel on the floor with the toes lifted.
Pull the band so your toes draw toward you and lean slightly forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds with a comfortable stretch.
Switch feet and repeat.

exercises.name: squats knee position
exercises.description: A bodyweight squat focused on where your knees travel, helping you learn to track them over your toes.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and toes slightly out.
Brace your core and lift your chest.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower into a squat.
Push your knees out so they follow the line of your toes.
Go down as deep as feels controlled.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.

exercises.name: single arm push up (on knees)
exercises.description: A one-arm push-up from the knees, a stepping stone toward the full single-arm version. It builds chest and trunk strength.
steps: Kneel and place one hand under your shoulder, with the other arm behind your back.
Spread your knees a bit wider for balance.
Keep a straight line from your head to your knees.
Lower your chest toward the floor with control.
Press back up without twisting your hips.
Switch arms and repeat.

exercises.name: briskly walking
exercises.description: A fast-paced walk that lifts your heart rate without the impact of running. Easy on the joints and good for steady fitness.
steps: Stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Start walking at a pace faster than a stroll.
Swing your arms naturally with elbows bent.
Land on your heel and roll through to your toes.
Keep breathing steadily and stay able to talk.
Walk for 20-45 minutes.

exercises.name: resistance band seated hip abduction
exercises.description: A seated hip abduction pushing your knees apart against a resistance band. Works the outer hips and glutes.
steps: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Wrap the resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
Place your hands on the sides of the chair or bench for support.
Engage your abductors (outer thigh muscles) and slowly push your knees apart, against the resistance of the band.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly bring your knees back together.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: resistance band leg extension
exercises.description: A leg extension with a resistance band around your ankle. Builds the quads.
steps: Attach the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point and secure it around your ankle.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Keeping your core engaged and your upper body stable, extend your leg straight out in front of you.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly return your leg to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.

exercises.name: stair up
exercises.description: Stepping up stairs at a steady pace to train the legs and raise your heart rate.
steps: Stand at the bottom of a staircase, standing tall.
Step up with one foot, placing your whole foot on the step.
Press through your heel and bring the other foot up.
Keep your torso upright and swing your arms naturally.
Continue at a steady pace and alternate the leading leg.

exercises.name: ez bar lying bent arms pullover
exercises.description: A lying EZ bar pullover with slightly bent arms. Works the lats and chest.
steps: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Hold the EZ barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms straight above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the barbell in an arc motion behind your head, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then return the barbell to the starting position by reversing the arc motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: incline scapula push up
exercises.description: An incline push-up where you retract your shoulder blades. Strengthens the serratus anterior and upper back.
steps: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Place your hands on the bench slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Position your feet on the ground, hip-width apart.
Lower your chest towards the bench, keeping your elbows tucked in.
As you lower, retract your shoulder blades, squeezing your scapulae together.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: scapula dips
exercises.description: A scapular dip, moving the shoulder blades while your arms stay straight. Strengthens the traps and shoulder stabilisers.
steps: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended in front of you.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Lower your body by bending your elbows and retracting your shoulder blades, as if you are trying to squeeze a pencil between them.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your hands to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: low glute bridge on floor
exercises.description: A low glute bridge on the floor, lifting your hips. Works the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your arms by your sides, palms facing down.
Engage your glutes and core, then lift your hips off the ground until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your glutes.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: curl-up
exercises.description: A curl-up lifting your shoulders off the floor. Works the abs.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is at a 45-degree angle.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: barbell pendlay row
exercises.description: A pendlay row from the floor, pulling the barbell to your upper abdomen. Builds the upper back and lats.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your chest up.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Pull the barbell towards your upper abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: standing calf raise
exercises.description: A bodyweight calf raise that builds lower-leg strength and ankle stability.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Rise up onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause at the top for a second.
Lower your heels slowly back to the floor.
Hold a wall for balance if needed.

exercises.name: bench pull-ups
exercises.description: A bodyweight bench pull-up variation hanging beneath a bar. Works the lats and biceps.
steps: Position yourself under a bar or a sturdy horizontal surface that is at chest height.
Grab the bar or surface with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Pull your chest towards the bar or surface by squeezing your shoulder blades together and bending your elbows.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar or surface.
Lower yourself back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: scapula push-up
exercises.description: A scapular push-up, protracting and retracting the shoulder blades. Strengthens the serratus anterior and upper back.
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your body.
As you lower, squeeze your shoulder blades together and push your chest forward.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: band lying hip internal rotation v. 2
exercises.description: Lying hip internal rotation against a band to build control through the hip.
steps: Lie on your back with a band around your lower leg anchored to the side.
Bend your knees with your feet on the floor.
Rotate your lower leg outward against the band, turning the hip inward.
Return slowly to the start.
Complete your reps and switch legs.

exercises.name: barbell split squat
exercises.description: A split-stance squat with a barbell on your back. It works each leg on its own and builds strength and balance.
steps: Rest a barbell across your upper back and step one foot forward.
Stand with a long stride and your torso upright.
Bend both knees and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Keep your front heel down and your front knee over your foot.
Press through the front foot to rise.
Finish your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: bent leg kickback (kneeling)
exercises.description: From all fours, you drive one bent knee up toward the ceiling. It targets the glutes without any equipment.
steps: Start on hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Lift one leg with the knee bent at 90 degrees.
Push the sole of your foot toward the ceiling and squeeze your glute.
Lower slowly without arching your back.
Complete your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: bent leg side kick (kneeling)
exercises.description: From all fours, you lift one bent leg out to the side. It works the outer hip and glutes.
steps: Start on hands and knees with a flat back.
Keep your knee bent at about 90 degrees.
Lift the bent leg out to the side to hip height.
Squeeze your outer hip at the top without rotating your torso.
Lower under control.
Finish your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: butt kicks
exercises.description: A running drill where your heels flick up toward your glutes. It warms up the hamstrings and raises your heart rate.
steps: Stand tall with your arms bent at your sides.
Jog on the spot or move forward slowly.
Kick each heel up toward your glute.
Stay on the balls of your feet and keep your knees pointing down.
Pump your arms in rhythm.
Continue for 20-40 seconds.

exercises.name: cable bar high pulley overhead tricep extension
exercises.description: A cable overhead extension from a high pulley that isolates the triceps.
steps: Attach a bar to a high pulley and face away from the machine.
Hold the bar behind your head with elbows pointing forward.
Step forward and stagger your feet.
Extend your arms to press the bar overhead.
Lower slowly back and keep your elbows in place.

exercises.name: cable hip abduction v. 2
exercises.description: Standing hip abduction against a low cable that trains the outer hip and glutes.
steps: Attach an ankle cuff to a low pulley and strap it to your outer ankle.
Stand sideways to the machine and hold a support.
Keep your torso upright and your standing leg slightly bent.
Lift the cuffed leg out to the side.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
Finish your reps and switch legs.

exercises.name: cable standing biceps curl (with rope)
exercises.description: A standing cable curl with a rope for constant tension on the biceps.
steps: Attach a rope to a low pulley and hold an end in each hand.
Stand tall with elbows by your sides.
Curl the rope up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower under control without swinging.

exercises.name: dumbbell close grip press v. 2
exercises.description: A press with dumbbells held close together that shifts the work toward the triceps and inner chest.
steps: Lie on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand pressed together over your chest.
Keep your palms facing each other.
Lower the dumbbells to your chest with your elbows tucked.
Press back up while keeping the weights touching.
Keep your wrists straight.

exercises.name: dumbbell seated curl v. 2
exercises.description: A seated curl that keeps the body steady while the biceps do the work.
steps: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang by your sides, palms forward.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top and keep elbows pinned.
Lower slowly to full extension.

exercises.name: dumbbell single arm preacher curl
exercises.description: A one-arm curl braced on a preacher pad for strict biceps isolation.
steps: Sit at a preacher bench with your upper arm on the pad.
Hold a dumbbell with your palm facing up.
Curl the weight toward your shoulder.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until nearly straight, then switch arms.

exercises.name: elbow to knee twists
exercises.description: A standing move where you twist to bring an elbow toward the opposite knee. It raises your pulse and works the sides of your waist.
steps: Stand tall with your hands behind your head.
Lift one knee up and across your body.
Twist your torso to meet the knee with the opposite elbow.
Return to standing.
Alternate sides at a steady pace.
Keep your chest lifted and breathe evenly.

exercises.name: frog hops
exercises.description: Explosive hops from a deep squat, like a frog. They build leg power and get your heart pumping.
steps: Stand with your feet wider than your shoulders and sink into a deep squat.
Place your fingertips on the floor between your feet.
Jump forward and up, swinging your arms.
Land softly back in the squat.
Reset and hop again right away.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes.

exercises.name: high knee skips
exercises.description: A bouncy skip with high knee lifts. It warms up the legs and raises your heart rate.
steps: Stand tall and relaxed.
Skip forward, driving one knee up high.
Hop lightly on the other foot.
Swing the opposite arm forward with each knee.
Alternate legs in a smooth rhythm.
Keep your chest up and land softly.

exercises.name: high knee squat
exercises.description: A squat followed by a high knee drive as you stand. It combines leg strength with a cardio push.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Squat down with your chest up.
Drive up through your feet to stand.
Lift one knee toward your chest as you reach the top.
Lower the foot and go back into the squat.
Alternate knees on each rep.

exercises.name: jumping jack
exercises.description: The classic jump where your arms and legs swing out and back. A simple full-body warm-up that raises your heart rate fast.
steps: Stand with your feet together and your arms at your sides.
Jump your feet apart as you swing your arms overhead.
Jump back to the start position.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Keep a steady rhythm.
Continue for 30-60 seconds.

exercises.name: lateral bound
exercises.description: A sideways leap from one leg to the other. It builds lateral power and balance.
steps: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Push off hard to leap sideways.
Land on the opposite foot and bend to absorb the impact.
Hold the landing for a second to stay balanced.
Bound back the other way.
Keep your chest up and your knee over your toes.

exercises.name: lever alternating narrow grip seated row (plate loaded)
exercises.description: A plate-loaded seated row with a narrow grip, one arm at a time for balanced back strength.
steps: Sit with your chest against the pad and grab the narrow handles.
Pull one handle back, driving your elbow behind you.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the end.
Return slowly and pull with the other arm.
Alternate sides and keep your torso still.

exercises.name: lever narrow grip seated row (plate loaded)
exercises.description: A plate-loaded machine row with a narrow grip for the lats and mid back.
steps: Sit with your chest against the pad and take the narrow handles.
Pull both handles toward your torso.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Pause briefly.
Return slowly with control.

exercises.name: plyo jacks
exercises.description: A jumping jack with a squat landing. The extra depth makes it harder on the legs and your heart.
steps: Stand with your feet together.
Jump your feet wide and land in a quarter squat.
Swing your arms out as you land.
Jump your feet back together.
Land softly each time.
Keep a quick, controlled pace.

exercises.name: skater
exercises.description: A side-to-side leap like a speed skater. It trains leg power, balance and stamina.
steps: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Leap sideways to the other leg.
Land softly and sweep the back leg behind you.
Swing your arms across your body for balance.
Immediately bound back the other way.
Keep your hips low and your chest forward.

exercises.name: smith hip thrust
exercises.description: A hip thrust with the bar on a Smith machine, giving a steady path to load the glutes.
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and the Smith bar over your hips.
Pad the bar and roll it into the crease of your hips.
Plant your feet hip width apart and unrack the bar.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your body is level.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat.

exercises.name: split jacks
exercises.description: A jumping move where your legs split front and back while your arms swing. It's a light, fast cardio burst.
steps: Stand tall with your arms at your sides.
Jump one foot forward and the other back as you swing opposite arms.
Land softly with soft knees.
Jump again and switch legs.
Keep your torso upright.
Continue at a steady pace for 30-45 seconds.

exercises.name: straight leg kickback (kneeling)
exercises.description: From all fours, you extend one straight leg back and up. It isolates the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Start on hands and knees with a flat back.
Brace your core.
Extend one leg straight back.
Lift it to hip height and squeeze your glute.
Lower without letting your back arch.
Finish your reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: band fixed back underhand pulldown
exercises.description: A band pulldown with an underhand grip from an overhead anchor. Builds the lats and biceps.
steps: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point above your head.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the band with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step back to create tension in the band, keeping your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Pull the band down towards your chest, leading with your elbows.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, feeling the contraction in your lats.
Slowly release the tension in the band and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: band fixed back close grip pulldown
exercises.description: A band pulldown with a close grip from an overhead anchor. Builds the lats and biceps.
steps: Attach the band to a fixed point above you, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam.
Sit down on a bench or chair facing the band, with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent.
Grasp the band with a close grip, palms facing towards you.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the band down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, feeling the contraction in your lats.
Slowly release the band back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: potty squat
exercises.description: A bodyweight squat done as a deep, comfortable squat. Works the legs, glutes and core.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Lower your body down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back as if you were sitting on a chair.
Keep your chest up and your back straight throughout the movement.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: standing calf raise with support
exercises.description: A calf raise holding on for balance, so you can focus on the calves.
steps: Stand holding a wall or rail for balance.
Place your feet hip-width apart.
Rise up on your toes as high as you can.
Pause and squeeze your calves.
Lower slowly.

exercises.name: band seated straight back row
exercises.description: A seated row with a band and a straight back that trains the lats and mid back.
steps: Sit on the floor with legs extended and a band around your feet.
Hold the ends with your arms straight.
Sit tall with a flat back.
Pull the band toward your waist, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly.

exercises.name: resistance band seated shoulder press
exercises.description: A seated shoulder press using a resistance band. Builds the shoulders and triceps.
steps: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the resistance band with both hands, palms facing forward, and bring it up to shoulder level.
Press the band overhead, extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the band back down to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: resistance band seated biceps curl
exercises.description: A seated biceps curl using a resistance band. Builds the biceps.
steps: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the resistance band with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and arms extended down by your sides.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the resistance band up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the resistance band back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: resistance band seated chest press
exercises.description: A seated chest press using a resistance band. Builds the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the resistance band handles in each hand, with your palms facing down and elbows bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend your arms forward, pushing the resistance band away from your chest.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: resistance band foot external rotation
exercises.description: A seated ankle drill where you turn the foot outward against a band. It strengthens the outer ankle muscles.
steps: Sit with one leg out and a band looped around the forefoot.
Anchor the other end to a fixed point on the inside.
Keep your heel still on the floor.
Turn your foot outward against the band.
Return slowly to the start.
Complete your reps, then switch feet.

exercises.name: resistance band foot plantar flexion
exercises.description: Pointing the foot against a band to strengthen the calf and ankle.
steps: Sit with your leg straight and a band looped around the ball of your foot.
Hold the band ends in your hands.
Point your toes away from you against the band.
Pause at the end of the range.
Return slowly.
Finish your reps, then switch feet.

exercises.name: resistance band foot eversion
exercises.description: Turning the sole of the foot outward against a band to train the muscles on the outer side of the ankle.
steps: Sit with your leg extended and a band around your forefoot.
Anchor the band on the inside of your foot.
Keep your leg still.
Turn the sole of your foot outward against the band.
Return slowly.
Complete your reps, then switch feet.

exercises.name: resistance band foot inversion
exercises.description: Turning the sole of the foot inward against a band to train the muscles on the inner side of the ankle.
steps: Sit with your leg extended and a band around your forefoot.
Anchor the band on the outside of your foot.
Keep your leg still.
Turn the sole of your foot inward against the band.
Return slowly.
Complete your reps, then switch feet.

exercises.name: scapula retraction protraction
exercises.description: A shoulder blade drill where you pull the blades together and then spread them apart. It improves control of the scapulae.
steps: Stand or sit tall with your arms forward at shoulder height.
Pull your shoulder blades together behind you.
Hold for a moment.
Then push your hands forward and let the blades spread apart.
Move slowly between the two positions.
Keep your neck relaxed and your ribs down.

exercises.name: scapula elevation depression
exercises.description: A drill where you shrug your shoulders up and then press them down. It builds control of the shoulder blades.
steps: Stand or sit tall with your arms at your sides.
Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears.
Hold for a second.
Press your shoulders down away from your ears.
Move slowly through the full range.
Keep your arms relaxed and your head still.

exercises.name: potty squat with support
exercises.description: A deep squat done holding a support for balance. Works the glutes and legs.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Hold onto a stable support, such as a chair or wall, for balance.
Lower your body down into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Keep your chest up and your back straight throughout the movement.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: bird dog v. 2
exercises.description: A floor stability move reaching opposite arm and leg to train the back and core.
steps: Start on all fours with a neutral spine.
Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
Keep your hips level and avoid arching your back.
Pause for a moment.
Return and switch sides.

exercises.name: smith sumo squat
exercises.description: A sumo squat on a smith machine. Targets the glutes, inner thighs and quads.
steps: Set up the smith machine with the barbell at hip height.
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing outwards.
Position yourself under the barbell, resting it on your upper back and shoulders.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you lower your body down into a squat position, pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: resistance band seated straight back row
exercises.description: A seated straight-back row using a resistance band. Builds the upper back and lats.
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and loop the resistance band around your feet.
Hold the ends of the resistance band with your hands, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly back, engaging your core.
Pull the resistance band towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: push-up plus
exercises.description: A push-up finished with an extra shove that spreads the shoulder blades at the top. It trains the chest and the serratus muscles that stabilise the shoulder blades.
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Once your chest is just above the ground, push through your hands to extend your arms and lift your upper body up.
At the top of the movement, protract your shoulder blades by pushing your upper back towards the ceiling.
Pause for a moment, then reverse the movement by retracting your shoulder blades and lowering your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: pelvic tilt
exercises.description: A small rocking movement of the pelvis while lying on your back. It wakes up the abs and teaches you to control the position of your lower back.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands by your sides.
Engage your abs and tilt your pelvis upward, pressing your lower back into the ground.
Hold this position for a few seconds, focusing on contracting your abs.
Release the tilt and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: chin tuck
exercises.description: Drawing your chin straight back to line up your head over your shoulders. It's a simple neck posture exercise.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your eyes level.
Place a finger on your chin if it helps.
Draw your chin straight back as if making a double chin.
Keep your head level without tilting.
Hold for 3-5 seconds.
Release and repeat 8-10 times.

exercises.name: assisted chin tuck
exercises.description: A chin tuck with light help from your hand to guide the movement and feel the right position.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your eyes level.
Place two fingers on your chin.
Gently guide your chin straight back.
Keep your head level and your shoulders relaxed.
Hold for 3-5 seconds.
Release and repeat 8-10 times.

exercises.name: side kick burpee
exercises.description: A burpee that finishes with a side kick. It's a tough full-body conditioning move.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Drop your hands to the floor and jump your feet back to a plank.
Do a push-up, then jump your feet back in.
Stand up and kick one leg out to the side.
Land and go straight into the next rep.
Alternate kicking sides.

exercises.name: bodyweight standing close-grip one arm row
exercises.description: A standing, bent-over one arm row with a close grip, working the muscles between and around the shoulder blades. A light handheld weight keeps the pull honest.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the dumbbell up towards your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exercises.name: bodyweight standing close-grip row
exercises.description: A bent-over standing row with a close grip, pulling the hands toward your body. It builds the upper back and the muscles that squeeze the shoulder blades together.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Extend your arms straight in front of you, gripping the bar or handles with a close grip.
Pull the bar or handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: bodyweight standing one arm row (with towel)
exercises.description: A standing one arm row using a towel as the handle, pulled toward the chest. It trains the upper back with very little equipment.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a towel with one hand.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the towel towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the towel back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exercises.name: bodyweight standing one arm row
exercises.description: A standing one arm row from a hip hinge, pulling a weight toward your chest one side at a time. Good for the upper back and lats.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a dumbbell in one hand.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Let the dumbbell hang straight down in front of you, with your arm fully extended.
Pull the dumbbell up towards your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exercises.name: bodyweight standing row (with towel)
exercises.description: A standing row done with both hands on a towel, pulling toward your chest. It trains the upper back and shoulder blade squeeze with no gear.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a towel in front of you with both hands.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Pull the towel towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: bodyweight standing row
exercises.description: A standing, bent-over row pulling a bar or handles toward your body with an overhand grip. It builds the upper back and the muscles that retract the shoulder blades.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Grasp a bar or handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Pull the bar or handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: bodyweight squatting row (with towel)
exercises.description: A squat combined with a towel row, so legs and upper back work together. You pull the towel toward your chest as you sink down.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a towel in front of you with your palms facing down.
Bend your knees and lower your body into a squat position, keeping your back straight and your chest up.
As you lower into the squat, simultaneously pull the towel towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the squat, then slowly return to the starting position while extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: bodyweight squatting row
exercises.description: A squat paired with a pulling motion on a sturdy anchor or suspension trainer. It trains the legs and upper back in one flowing movement.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding onto a sturdy object or suspension trainer with your arms extended.
Lower your body into a squat position, keeping your back straight and your knees behind your toes.
From the squat position, pull your body up towards the object or suspension trainer, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: boxing right hook
exercises.description: A right-handed hook punch thrown in a boxing stance. It trains rotation and power from the hips.
steps: Stand in a boxing stance with your hands up.
Bend your right elbow to about 90 degrees.
Pivot on your back foot and rotate your hips and torso.
Swing your fist in an arc to your target.
Snap back to guard position.
Keep your chin tucked and your left hand up.

exercises.name: barbell bench press (knees at 90 degrees)
exercises.description: A bench press with your feet up and your knees bent to 90 degrees. This keeps your lower back flat and your trunk working.
steps: Lie on a bench and lift your feet with your knees bent to 90 degrees.
Grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders.
Unrack and hold it over your chest.
Lower the bar to your mid chest with control.
Press it back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your lower back flat on the bench.

exercises.name: dumbbell fly (knees at 90 degrees)
exercises.description: A dumbbell fly with your feet lifted and knees at 90 degrees. It stretches the chest and keeps your back flat.
steps: Lie on a bench holding dumbbells above your chest.
Lift your feet so your knees are bent to 90 degrees.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Open your arms out wide until you feel a chest stretch.
Bring the dumbbells back together over your chest.
Move slowly and keep your back flat.

exercises.name: dumbbell straight arm pullover (knees at 90 degrees)
exercises.description: A straight-arm pullover with knees bent to 90 degrees on a bench. It works the chest and lats and keeps the trunk braced.
steps: Lie on a bench with your feet up and knees at 90 degrees.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands above your chest.
Keep your arms nearly straight.
Lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head.
Pull it back over your chest.
Keep your ribs down and your back flat.

exercises.name: stability ball reverse hyperextension (off a bench)
exercises.description: A reverse hyperextension over a ball at the edge of a bench for glutes and lower back.
steps: Lie face down with your hips over the ball and hands on the floor.
Hold the bench or the ball for stability.
Lift your legs until they are in line with your body.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower with control.

exercises.name: incline reverse hyperextension
exercises.description: A reverse hyperextension on an incline bench that trains the glutes and lower back.
steps: Lie face down on an incline bench with hips at the edge.
Hold the sides of the bench.
Raise both legs until they are in line with your torso.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat.

exercises.name: bodyweight frog pump
exercises.description: A glute bridge with the soles of your feet together, taking glute work to the next level.
steps: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees dropped open.
Bring your heels close to your hips.
Drive your hips up by squeezing your glutes.
Pause at the top.
Lower and repeat in quick pumps.

exercises.name: weighted frog pump
exercises.description: A frog-style glute bridge with extra weight on your hips for stronger glutes.
steps: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees open.
Rest a weight on your hips.
Drive your hips up by squeezing your glutes.
Pause at the top.
Lower and repeat.

exercises.name: barbell hang clean below the knees v. 2
exercises.description: A clean started with the bar hanging below the knees. It builds explosive hip power.
steps: Stand with the bar hanging below your knees in an overhand grip.
Hinge back with a flat back and shoulders over the bar.
Drive your hips forward and jump explosively.
Shrug and pull your elbows high.
Drop under the bar and catch it on your shoulders.
Stand tall, then lower the bar under control.

exercises.name: barbell squat (with hanging band technique)
exercises.description: A barbell squat with bands hanging weights from the bar. The wobble forces you to stay stable.
steps: Set up the bar with bands hanging kettlebells or weights from each end.
Rest the bar across your upper back and step out.
Stand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Squat down with a braced core.
Drive up through your feet.
Use a lighter load and move slowly.

exercises.name: barbell bench press (with hanging band technique)
exercises.description: A bench press with bands hanging weights from the bar. The shaky load trains control and stability.
steps: Hang weights from each end of the bar with bands.
Lie on the bench and unrack the bar.
Hold it over your chest.
Lower the bar slowly to your mid chest.
Press up and keep the bar steady.
Use a lighter load than a normal bench press.

exercises.name: barbell military press (with hanging band technique)
exercises.description: An overhead press with bands hanging weights from the bar. The unstable load trains control in the shoulders.
steps: Hang weights from each end of the bar with bands.
Hold the bar at your shoulders and stand tall.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar straight overhead.
Lower it slowly back to your shoulders.
Use a lighter load and keep the bar steady.

exercises.name: kettlebell goblet squat jump
exercises.description: A goblet squat that finishes with an explosive jump for leg power.
steps: Hold a kettlebell at your chest with both hands.
Squat down with your chest tall.
Explode upward into a jump.
Land softly with bent knees.
Reset and go into the next squat.

exercises.name: dumbbell straight arm pullover (with hanging band technique)
exercises.description: A straight-arm pullover with weights hung from the dumbbell by a band. The swing makes your shoulders and trunk work harder.
steps: Hang a weight from the dumbbell with a band.
Lie on a bench and hold it above your chest with straight arms.
Lower it in an arc behind your head.
Pull it back over your chest slowly.
Keep your ribs down and your core tight.
Use a light load to stay controlled.

exercises.name: glute-ham raise
exercises.description: A hamstring exercise where you lift your torso from a face-down position on a glute-ham bench. It strengthens the hamstrings, glutes and lower back.
steps: Adjust the glute-ham raise machine to fit your body.
Position yourself face down on the machine with your ankles secured.
Place your hands on your chest or cross them over your chest.
Engage your hamstrings and glutes to lift your upper body up towards the ceiling.
Continue lifting until your body is in a straight line from your head to your heels.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: frankenstein squat
exercises.description: A front-loaded barbell squat held out in front of the body with straight arms. It hits the glutes and quads and demands a tall, braced torso.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell in front of your body with straight arms.
Keeping your back straight, lower your body by bending at the knees and hips, as if sitting back into a chair.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: lever lying two-one leg curl
exercises.description: A lying machine leg curl that starts with both legs and finishes with one. It targets the hamstrings with a controlled, heavier lowering phase.
steps: Adjust the machine to fit your body and sit on it with your back against the backrest.
Place your legs on the lever pad, just above your ankles.
Grasp the handles on the sides of the machine for support.
Keeping your upper body still, exhale and curl your legs up towards your glutes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: quick feet run
exercises.description: Running on the spot with very fast, small steps. It's a classic warm-up and speed drill.
steps: Stand tall with your knees slightly bent.
Run on the spot as fast as you can with small steps.
Stay on the balls of your feet.
Pump your arms.
Keep your chest up.
Continue for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: prancing
exercises.description: A light, springy trot with high knees, like a pony. It's a fun cardio warm-up.
steps: Stand tall and relaxed.
Move forward in a bouncy trot.
Lift each knee up with a springy step.
Stay on the balls of your feet.
Swing your arms in rhythm.
Continue for 30-60 seconds.

exercises.name: zigzag hops
exercises.description: Hopping diagonally forward in a zigzag pattern. It trains agility and lower leg power.
steps: Stand with your knees slightly bent.
Hop forward and to one side.
Land softly on both feet.
Hop forward and to the other side.
Keep your hops light and quick.
Continue for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: skips
exercises.description: A simple skipping step with a hop on each foot. A playful way to warm up and lift your heart rate.
steps: Stand tall and relaxed.
Step forward and hop on the same foot.
Switch and hop on the other foot.
Swing the opposite arm forward with each step.
Stay light on the balls of your feet.
Keep a steady rhythm.

exercises.name: lever bent-over row with v-bar
exercises.description: A machine row done in a bent-over stance with a v-bar handle. It builds the upper back and lats by pulling the handle toward your abdomen.
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself facing the machine.
Grasp the v-bar with an overhand grip, keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent.
Pull the v-bar towards your abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: quarter sit-up
exercises.description: A short-range sit-up where you curl only partway up. It keeps tension on the abs and is easier on the lower back than a full sit-up.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is at a 45-degree angle.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: half sit-up (male)
exercises.description: A sit-up that stops at roughly half height, keeping constant tension on the abs. A gentle way to train the midsection.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is at a 45-degree angle.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: prisoner half sit-up (male)
exercises.description: A half sit-up with the hands held behind the head, like a prisoner. It trains the abs through a short, controlled range.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is at a 45-degree angle.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: arms overhead full sit-up (male)
exercises.description: A full sit-up with the arms stretched overhead, which makes the lever longer and the move harder. It trains the abs and hip flexors.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Extend your arms overhead, keeping them straight.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is upright.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: kneeling push-up (male)
exercises.description: A beginner-friendly push-up with the knees on the floor. It builds chest, shoulder and triceps strength with less load than a standard push-up.
steps: Start by kneeling on the ground with your hands shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward.
Extend your legs behind you, resting on the balls of your feet, so that your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Continue lowering until your chest is just above the ground, then push back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: basic toe touch (male)
exercises.description: A simple standing forward fold to reach your toes. It loosens the hamstrings and lower back and gets the hips moving.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms by your sides.
Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent.
Reach down towards your toes with your hands, keeping your legs as straight as possible.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: side-to-side toe touch (male)
exercises.description: A standing side bend where each hand slides down toward the same-side foot in turn. It mobilises the trunk and trains the obliques.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended to the sides.
